children.title: Box-Constrained Quadratic Programs
children.top_down_role: Quadratic models over rectangular domains.

assumptions_latex: \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\) are finite and satisfy \(\ell_i<u_i\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha:\ell\le x\le u\}\) is attained, and the problem is convex if and only if \(Q\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: The componentwise box containing every x satisfying ell less than or equal to x less than or equal to u.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quadratic minimization over a bounded rectangular domain.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given symmetric \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), and finite vectors \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\ell_i<u_i\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,n\), a box-constrained quadratic program is
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha:\ \ell\le x\le u\right\}.
\]
Its feasible set is nonempty and compact, so the minimum is attained. Because the box has nonempty interior in \(\mathbb R^n\), this minimization problem is convex if and only if \(Q\succeq0\). If \(Q\not\succeq0\), the quadratic objective is nonconvex on the box; this includes, but is not limited to, indefinite matrices \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic objective is minimized over finite componentwise bounds. The nonempty compact box guarantees attainment. The problem is convex exactly when the quadratic matrix is positive semidefinite; a matrix that is not positive semidefinite gives a nonconvex objective on the box but need not be indefinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Box-Constrained Quadratic Programs

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

children.title: Polyhedrally Constrained Indefinite Quadratic Programs
children.top_down_role: Indefinite quadratic objectives over bounded polyhedra.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) is nonempty and bounded
\(Q=Q^\top\) has at least one positive and at least one negative eigenvalue
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in P}(x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha)\) is attained; its restriction to \(P\) is convex exactly when \(v^\top Qv\ge0\) for every \(v\in\operatorname{lin}(P-P)\).

notation.meaning: The direction space parallel to the affine hull of P.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indefinite quadratic minimization over a nonempty bounded polyhedron.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) be nonempty and bounded. A polyhedrally constrained indefinite quadratic program has the form
\[
\min_{x\in P}\;x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha,
\]
where \(Q=Q^\top\) has at least one positive and at least one negative eigenvalue. The feasible polyhedron \(P\) is compact, so the minimum is attained. Although the objective is nonconvex on \(\mathbb R^n\), its restriction to \(P\) is convex exactly when
\[
v^\top Qv\ge0\qquad\text{for every }v\in\operatorname{lin}(P-P),
\]
where \(\operatorname{lin}(P-P)\) is the direction space parallel to \(\operatorname{aff}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This regime minimizes a genuinely indefinite quadratic, whose matrix has both positive and negative eigenvalues, over a nonempty bounded polyhedron. A minimum is attained. The restriction can nevertheless be convex when the quadratic matrix is positive semidefinite on every direction parallel to the feasible polyhedron's affine hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedrally Constrained Indefinite Quadratic Programs

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

children.title: Standard Quadratic Programs over Simplices
children.top_down_role: Simplex-constrained quadratic models with specialized conic representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Standard Quadratic Programs over Simplices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact copositive representation of the standard quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Q=Q^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), the standard quadratic program is
\[
p^*=\min\{x^\top Qx:x\ge0,\ e^\top x=1\}.
\]
Let \(\operatorname{COP}_n=\{M=M^\top:y^\top My\ge0\ \text{for every }y\ge0\}\). Then
\[
p^*=\max\{\lambda\in\mathbb R:Q-\lambda ee^\top\in\operatorname{COP}_n\}.
\]
Indeed, copositivity of the displayed matrix is equivalent to \(x^\top Qx\ge\lambda\) throughout the simplex after positive scaling. Replacing the copositive cone by tractable inner approximations yields lower-bounding conic relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a quadratic over the simplex is exactly equivalent to maximizing a scalar subject to a copositive-matrix constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\max\{\lambda:Q-\lambda ee^\top\in\operatorname{COP}_n\}\).

notation.meaning: The cone of n-by-n copositive symmetric matrices.
The optimal value of the standard quadratic program.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical homogeneous copositive reformulation of standard quadratic optimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The copositive representation is mathematically precise and its representation content kind fits the simplex-program leaf, but the record has no inspectable citation. The standard-field rationale cannot replace a source for this nontrivial exact conic representation.

children.title: Quadratically Constrained Regimes
children.top_down_role: Quadratic models distinguished by the number and geometry of their quadratic constraints.

children.title: Single Quadratic Constraint Regime
children.top_down_role: Quadratic optimization governed by one principal quadratic constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Single Quadratic Constraint Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: S-lemma exactness for one inhomogeneous quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q_i(x)=x^\top Q_i x+2c_i^\top x+d_i\) with symmetric \(Q_i\), consider \(p^*=\inf\{q_0(x):q_1(x)\le0\}\). Assume there exists \(\bar x\) satisfying \(q_1(\bar x)<0\), and that \(p^*>-\infty\). Then the S-lemma gives
\[
p^*=\sup_{\gamma\in\mathbb R,\,\tau\ge0}\left\{\gamma:q_0(x)-\gamma+\tau q_1(x)\ge0\ \text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n\right\}.
\]
The universal quadratic inequality is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness of its augmented coefficient matrix, so the resulting semidefinite relaxation is exact in value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict feasibility and finite value, a problem with one quadratic inequality has an exact semidefinite dual furnished by the S-lemma.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\sup\{\gamma:\exists\tau\ge0,\ q_0-\gamma+\tau q_1\ge0\text{ on }\mathbb R^n\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated S-lemma duality is mathematically plausible under the given strict-feasibility and finite-value hypotheses, and duality is the correct content kind. However, the cited locator concerns linear matrix inequalities and does not specifically identify the S-lemma or its exact-value conclusion. A source locator for the S-lemma theorem is required.

children.title: Few-Quadratic-Constraint Regimes
children.top_down_role: Low-constraint-count models supporting specialized rank and exactness analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Few-Quadratic-Constraint Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: QCQPs parameterized by a fixed, small number of quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed integer \(m\ge1\), a few-quadratic-constraint problem is
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{q_0(x):q_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\right\},
\]
where every \(q_i(x)=x^\top Q_i x+2c_i^\top x+d_i\) and \(m\) is treated as a structural parameter independent of the ambient dimension \(n\). Its Shor relaxation replaces \(xx^\top\) by \(X\) and imposes \(X\succeq xx^\top\). A small value of \(m\) enables constraint-count-dependent rank analysis, but does not by itself guarantee a rank-one optimum or exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This regime has a fixed small number of quadratic inequalities. Low constraint count supports rank analysis, but alone does not make the standard SDP relaxation exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\) is the constraint-count parameter governing applicable low-rank analyses; exactness requires additional hypotheses.

notation.meaning: The number of quadratic inequality constraints.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional parameterized QCQP regime and Shor lifting
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes a fixed small constraint count from an exactness guarantee, and definition is appropriate for this regime leaf. No source is supplied for the Shor relaxation and constraint-count-dependent rank-analysis claims, so the record requires an inspectable citation.

children.title: General Nonconvex QCQP Regime
children.top_down_role: Quadratically constrained models outside the classical low-constraint exactness settings.

knowledge_statements.title: General Nonconvex QCQP Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple-constraint QCQPs without convexity or low-constraint exactness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A general nonconvex quadratically constrained quadratic program has the form
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{x^\top Q_0x+2c_0^\top x+d_0:x^\top Q_ix+2c_i^\top x+d_i\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\right\},
\]
with symmetric matrices \(Q_i\), where at least one objective or feasible-set quadratic is nonconvex and no single-constraint or other stated exactness hypothesis is imposed. Its standard semidefinite relaxation substitutes \(X\) for \(xx^\top\) and retains only \(X\succeq xx^\top\), thereby producing a lower bound for minimization rather than a generally exact reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general nonconvex QCQP has several arbitrary quadratic functions and lacks special exactness assumptions. Its basic semidefinite lifting generally supplies only a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: At least one quadratic destroys convexity
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation obtained from \(X\succeq xx^\top\) is a valid lower-bounding relaxation, not a universally exact formulation.

notation.meaning: Coefficients of the i-th quadratic function.
The lifted matrix variable replacing xx^T.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

children.title: Binary Quadratic Programs
children.top_down_role: Quadratic optimization over zero-one or signed-binary domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Quadratic Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent zero-one and signed-binary quadratic formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A zero-one binary quadratic program is
\[
\min\{x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha:x\in\{0,1\}^n\},
\]
where \(Q=Q^\top\). Under the bijection \(s=2x-e\), equivalently \(x=(s+e)/2\), it becomes a signed-binary quadratic program over \(s\in\{-1,1\}^n\). Substitution yields
\[
x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha=\tfrac14s^\top Qs+\tfrac12(Qe+c)^\top s+\alpha+\tfrac14e^\top Qe+\tfrac12c^\top e.
\]
Thus the two binary conventions are affinely equivalent and preserve minimizers under the stated bijection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero-one and signed-binary quadratic programs are equivalent through the affine change of variables s=2x−e, with explicitly transformed objective coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The substitution \(s=2x-e\) gives an equivalent problem over \(\{-1,1\}^n\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct affine substitution between the two binary encodings
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine substitution and transformed coefficients are consistent, and representation is the correct role for this equivalence. The record nevertheless has no citation with an inspectable locator, so it cannot pass statement review solely on standard-field rationale.

children.title: Mixed Binary–Continuous Bilinear Models
children.top_down_role: Bounded continuous variables coupled to binary variables through products.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Binary–Continuous Bilinear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear convex hull for one binary–bounded-continuous product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z\in\{0,1\}\), \(\ell\le x\le u\), and \(y=zx\), where \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R\) are finite and \(\ell<u\). The convex hull of this bilinear graph is exactly the polyhedron
\[
0\le z\le1,\qquad \ell z\le y\le uz,
\]
\[
y\ge x-u(1-z),\qquad y\le x-\ell(1-z),\qquad \ell\le x\le u.
\]
Consequently, each separable binary–continuous product with valid finite bounds admits an ideal local linear formulation. Applying these inequalities componentwise remains valid, although additional coupling constraints can require further strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product of one binary and one bounded continuous variable has an exact four-inequality linear convex-hull formulation. Coupled models may still need stronger global inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed polyhedron equals \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,z,y):y=zx,\ z\in\{0,1\},\ \ell\le x\le u\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical exact binary–continuous product hull obtained from the two disjuncts
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed formulation is the exact convex hull for one binary variable multiplied by one finitely bounded continuous variable, and representation fits the leaf. An authoritative source with a specific theorem, proposition, section, or page locator is still required.

children.title: Quadratic Indicator Models
children.top_down_role: Quadratic epigraphs and constraints controlled by activation variables.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}(S)=\{(x,t,z):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge0,\ tz\ge x^\top Qx\}\).

notation.meaning: The closed convex hull of S.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed perspective hull for an activated positive-definite quadratic epigraph with a nonnegative epigraph variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=Q^\top\succ0\), and define the activated epigraph
\[
S=\{(x,t,z):z\in\{0,1\},\ t\ge0,\ z=0\Rightarrow x=0,\ z=1\Rightarrow t\ge x^\top Qx\}.
\]
Its closed convex hull is
\[
\operatorname{clconv}(S)=\{(x,t,z):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge0,\ tz\ge x^\top Qx\}.
\]
Equivalently, this perspective inequality has the linear-matrix representation
\[
\begin{pmatrix}t&x^\top\\x&zQ^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
At \(z=0\), positive definiteness of \(Q\) and the matrix inequality force \(x=0\). Thus the perspective formulation is the ideal closed convex relaxation of this activated nonnegative quadratic epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite quadratic activated by a binary variable, with the epigraph variable constrained to be nonnegative in both activation states, the perspective inequality and its equivalent matrix inequality describe the closed convex hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Indicator Models

children.title: General Mixed-Integer QCQP Regime
children.top_down_role: Mixed-integer models containing quadratic objectives or constraints beyond indicator structure.

knowledge_statements.title: General Mixed-Integer QCQP Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-integer QCQPs without restriction to product or indicator structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition \(x=(x_I,x_C)\), with \(x_I\in\mathbb Z^p\) and \(x_C\in\mathbb R^{n-p}\). A general mixed-integer quadratically constrained quadratic program is
\[
\inf\{x^\top Q_0x+2c_0^\top x+d_0:x^\top Q_ix+2c_i^\top x+d_i\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\ x\in P,\ x_I\in\mathbb Z^p\},
\]
where \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is polyhedral and the symmetric matrices \(Q_i\) may be indefinite. The regime includes arbitrary quadratic interactions among integer and continuous variables and therefore is not limited to isolated indicator or binary–continuous product structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general mixed-integer QCQP combines integral variables, polyhedral restrictions, and arbitrary quadratic objectives or constraints, possibly with indefinite curvature and unrestricted variable interactions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed model defines the general mixed-integer QCQP regime.

children.title: Sign-Structured Quadratic Forms
children.top_down_role: Quadratic interaction patterns organized by coefficient signs and their convexification implications.

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Structured Quadratic Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic forms reducible to nonpositive off-diagonal interactions by sign switching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Q=Q^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), the quadratic form \(x\mapsto x^\top Qx\) is sign-structured of switched-Z type if there exists a diagonal signature matrix \(D=\operatorname{Diag}(\sigma)\), with \(\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}\), such that
\[
(DQD)_{ij}\le0\qquad\text{for all }i\ne j.
\]
Equivalently, after the variable substitution \(x=Dy\), every cross-term coefficient in \(y^\top(DQD)y\) is nonpositive. This property constrains only the interaction signs; it neither requires positive semidefiniteness nor fixes the diagonal entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic form has switched-Z sign structure when flipping selected variable signs makes every off-diagonal coefficient nonpositive. This does not imply convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(D=\operatorname{Diag}(\sigma)\) with \(\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}\) such that \((DQD)_{ij}\le0\) for every \(i\ne j\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard diagonal-sign switching definition for signed Z-matrices
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagonal-sign-switching condition is internally precise and definition fits the leaf, but the label switched-Z sign structure requires alignment with an authoritative source. No citation is supplied, so the intended terminology and scope cannot yet be confirmed.

children.title: M-Matrix Quadratic Forms
children.top_down_role: Quadratic models whose matrix structure supports specialized relaxation behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: M-Matrix Quadratic Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic forms generated by symmetric nonsingular M-matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A symmetric matrix \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is a nonsingular M-matrix if
\[
Q=sI-B,
\]
for some symmetric entrywise-nonnegative matrix \(B\ge0\) and scalar \(s>\rho(B)\). An M-matrix quadratic form is \(x\mapsto x^\top Qx\) with such a coefficient matrix. For symmetric \(Q\), this is equivalent to \(Q\succ0\) together with \(Q_{ij}\le0\) for all \(i\ne j\). Hence the form is strictly convex and has nonpositive pairwise cross-interactions, while \(Q^{-1}\) is entrywise nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric nonsingular M-matrix is a positive-definite matrix with nonpositive off-diagonal entries. Its quadratic form is strictly convex, and its inverse is entrywise nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=sI-B\) with \(B\ge0\) and \(s>\rho(B)\), equivalently \(Q\succ0\) and \(Q_{ij}\le0\) for \(i\ne j\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical equivalent characterizations of symmetric nonsingular M-matrices
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalent characterizations and inverse-nonnegativity claim are standard for symmetric nonsingular M-matrices, and definition is the correct content kind. Because these are nontrivial equivalences and no inspectable citation is present, the record requires a source.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in[0,1]^n,\,w\in\mathcal M(x)} c^\top x+\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}w_{ij}=\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}c^\top x+\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}x_ix_j\).

notation.meaning: McCormick system for binary pair products
lifted surrogate for the product of coordinates i and j

review_flags: Exactness version selected for submodular binary quadratic minimization.
A direct authoritative source for the stated LP-value exactness theorem is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Submodular binary quadratic objectives with nonpositive pairwise coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) and let \(q_{ij}\le 0\) for all \(i<j\). For each pair introduce \(w_{ij}\) and impose \(0\le w_{ij}\), \(w_{ij}\le x_i\), \(w_{ij}\le x_j\), and \(w_{ij}\ge x_i+x_j-1\), with \(x\in[0,1]^n\). Then the resulting linear relaxation has the same optimal value as the binary quadratic problem:
\[
\min\left\{c^\top x+\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}w_{ij}:(x,w)\text{ satisfies the displayed relaxation}\right\}
=
\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}\left(c^\top x+\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}x_ix_j\right).
\]
An optimal binary solution therefore exists for the relaxation, although fractional optimal solutions need not be absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary quadratic objective with nonpositive pairwise coefficients has an exact McCormick LP optimal value, though the relaxation may also possess fractional optima.
knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Structure Exactness Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The LP-value exactness claim is mathematically plausible for submodular binary quadratic minimization, but no citation supports the precise McCormick formulation and conclusion. A direct authoritative source is required.

children.title: Low-Rank Quadratic Structure
children.top_down_role: Quadratic models organized by low-rank objective or constraint matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Quadratic Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact symmetric factorization defining objective or constraint matrices of rank at most \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A symmetric quadratic form \(x^\top Qx\), with \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), has rank at most \(r\) precisely when there exist \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) and \(S\in\mathbb S^r\) such that \(Q=USU^\top\). In that case
\[
x^\top Qx=(U^\top x)^\top S(U^\top x),
\]
so all quadratic dependence is mediated by the projected vector \(U^\top x\in\mathbb R^r\). For a positive semidefinite matrix, one may choose \(S=I_r\), giving \(x^\top Qx=\lVert U^\top x\rVert_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-at-most-r quadratic matrix factors through an r-dimensional projection, so the quadratic value depends only on r linear combinations of the variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)\le r\iff Q=USU^\top\) for suitable \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) and \(S\in\mathbb S^r\).

notation.meaning: real symmetric n by n matrices

children.title: Sparse Interaction-Graph Quadratics
children.top_down_role: Quadratic models whose product structure follows a sparse graph.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\top Qx=\sum_iQ_{ii}x_i^2+2\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}Q_{ij}x_ix_j\).

notation.meaning: interaction graph of the quadratic form

review_flags: A source explicitly connecting quadratic sparsity with the interaction-graph representation is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph representation induced by the nonzero off-diagonal entries of a symmetric quadratic matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), define its interaction graph by \(G_Q=(V,E)\), where \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and
\[
E=\bigl\{\{i,j\}:1\le i<j\le n,\ Q_{ij}\ne0\bigr\}.
\]
Then
\[
x^\top Qx=\sum_{i=1}^nQ_{ii}x_i^2+2\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}Q_{ij}x_ix_j.
\]
The quadratic is graph-sparse when \(G_Q\) is sparse; each lifted product variable is naturally indexed by an edge, and variables belonging to different connected components have no cross-component quadratic interaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic interaction graph places an edge exactly where an off-diagonal product has a nonzero coefficient; sparse graphs yield few coupled products.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Interaction-Graph Quadratics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interaction-graph representation is mathematically correct and appropriately classified, but the record supplies no inspectable citation.

children.title: McCormick Envelope Principle
children.top_down_role: Convex-hull organization of bounded bilinear graphs and their domain specializations.

children.title: Continuous Bilinear Box Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Envelope geometry for products of two bounded continuous variables.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,xy)\}=\{(x,y,w):\text{the four McCormick inequalities hold}\}\).

notation.meaning: lower and upper bounds for x
lower and upper bounds for y

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex hull of one continuous bilinear graph over a finite rectangle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite bounds \(L_x<U_x\) and \(L_y<U_y\), the convex hull of the bilinear graph \(w=xy\) over \([L_x,U_x]\times[L_y,U_y]\) is described by the box bounds and
\[
\begin{aligned}
w&\ge L_xy+L_yx-L_xL_y, & w&\ge U_xy+U_yx-U_xU_y,\\
w&\le U_xy+L_yx-U_xL_y, & w&\le L_xy+U_yx-L_xU_y.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus these four affine inequalities give both the convex envelope and the concave envelope of the product, with no additional inequalities required for a single bounded bilinear term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four McCormick inequalities exactly describe the convex hull of one continuous bilinear product over a finite rectangular box.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Bilinear Box Envelopes

children.title: Binary–Continuous Product Hulls
children.top_down_role: Product convexification when one factor is binary and the other is bounded.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}\{(z,x,zx)\}=\{(z,x,w):0\le z\le1,\ L\le x\le U,\text{ and the four displayed inequalities hold}\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal linear formulation for one binary factor and one finitely bounded continuous factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z\in\{0,1\}\), let \(L\le x\le U\) with finite \(L<U\), and set \(w=zx\). The convex hull of this product graph is obtained by replacing integrality with \(0\le z\le1\) and imposing
\[
Lz\le w\le Uz,
\qquad
x-U(1-z)\le w\le x-L(1-z).
\]
At \(z=0\) these inequalities force \(w=0\), and at \(z=1\) they force \(w=x\). Consequently, the formulation is ideal for this isolated binary-continuous product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four linear inequalities give the exact convex hull of a binary variable times a finitely bounded continuous variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Binary–Continuous Product Hulls

children.title: Sign-Bound Envelope Regimes
children.top_down_role: Envelope-strength regimes induced by factor signs and interval geometry.

children.title: Fixed-Sign Factor Regimes
children.top_down_role: Envelope behavior when each factor remains within a single sign orthant.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(xy\) is coordinatewise nondecreasing, and its graph hull is the four-facet McCormick polytope.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative fixed-sign case; other fixed-sign patterns follow by sign changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(0\le L_x<U_x\) and \(0\le L_y<U_y\). On \([L_x,U_x]\times[L_y,U_y]\), the product \(xy\) is nondecreasing in each factor, and its minimum and maximum are \(L_xL_y\) and \(U_xU_y\), respectively. Its convex-hull formulation remains the four McCormick inequalities. Fixed signs simplify product bounds and monotonic propagation but do not, by themselves, make the relaxed graph equal to \(w=xy\) at every interior point. Other fixed-sign patterns reduce to this case by replacing one or both factors with their negatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed factor signs make product extrema and monotonicity explicit, but do not remove the interior gap in a continuous McCormick relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Sign Factor Regimes

children.title: Sign-Crossing Factor Regimes
children.top_down_role: Envelope behavior when factor intervals cross zero.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(xy\) is not monotone in \(y\) uniformly over the box, while the four McCormick inequalities still describe its graph hull.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: At least one factor interval contains both negative and positive values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_x<0<U_x\) and let \(L_y<U_y\) be finite. Because the derivative of \(xy\) with respect to \(y\) equals \(x\), the product is increasing in \(y\) where \(x>0\) and decreasing where \(x<0\); hence no single monotonicity direction is valid throughout the box. Nevertheless, the convex hull of \(w=xy\) is still exactly the four-corner McCormick polytope. When both factor intervals cross zero, all four corner sign combinations may influence product bounds, so sign-aware corner evaluation is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a factor crosses zero, product monotonicity reverses inside the box, although the four McCormick inequalities still give the exact graph hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Crossing Factor Regimes

children.title: Tight Finite-Bound Regimes
children.top_down_role: Relaxation strength under informative finite factor bounds.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M(L'_x,U'_x,L'_y,U'_y)\subseteq\mathcal M(L_x,U_x,L_y,U_y)\) after restriction to the smaller box.

notation.meaning: McCormick polytope generated from the indicated bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strengthening and quantitative envelope width under finite bound tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the primed factor intervals be contained in the corresponding unprimed finite intervals. On the smaller box, the McCormick polytope generated from the primed bounds is contained in the restriction of the polytope generated from the unprimed bounds. Thus bound tightening cannot weaken the single-product relaxation. Moreover, if \(\Delta_x=U_x-L_x\) and \(\Delta_y=U_y-L_y\), the maximum vertical distance between the McCormick concave and convex envelopes equals
\[
\frac{\Delta_x\Delta_y}{2}.
\]
Consequently, shrinking either interval proportionally reduces the worst envelope width.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tighter finite factor bounds produce a nested stronger McCormick relaxation; its maximum vertical width equals half the product of the interval widths.
knowledge_statements.title: Tight Finite-Bound Regimes

children.title: Weak-Bound Envelope Regimes
children.top_down_role: Loss of envelope strength as factor bounds become loose.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Bound Envelope Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantified deterioration of a bilinear envelope as finite factor bounds widen.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in[L_x,U_x]\) and \(y\in[L_y,U_y]\), write \(\Delta_x=U_x-L_x\) and \(\Delta_y=U_y-L_y\). The greatest vertical width between the McCormick concave and convex envelopes is \(\Delta_x\Delta_y/2\), attained at the box midpoint. Hence a sequence of valid boxes with \(\Delta_x\Delta_y\to\infty\) has unbounded envelope width. If either factor lacks finite two-sided bounds, the standard four-facet McCormick construction contains infinite coefficients and does not furnish a finite polyhedral envelope without additional domain information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: McCormick quality deteriorates with the product of factor widths, and the standard four-facet formulation fails when required finite bounds are absent.
assumptions_latex: \(L_x<U_x\) and \(L_y<U_y\), with all four endpoints finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\bigl(\operatorname{cav}(xy)-\operatorname{vex}(xy)\bigr)=(U_x-L_x)(U_y-L_y)/2\), so the maximum width diverges along any sequence for which \((U_x-L_x)(U_y-L_y)\to\infty\).

children.title: Shared-Factor Product Consistency
children.top_down_role: Strengthening beyond independent envelopes when lifted products share variables.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&W\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) is a necessary joint consistency condition for all shared-factor products.
review_flags: A source explicitly supporting this shared-factor strengthening formulation is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint semidefinite consistency for multiple lifted products sharing original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If all lifted products are exact, so that \(W=xx^\top\), then their shared factors obey the joint identity
\[
Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&W\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}1\\x\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1\\x\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top},
\]
and therefore \(Y\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\). Dropping the rank constraint while retaining \(Y\succeq0\) gives a convex necessary consistency condition coupling all entries of \(W\). It can exclude assignments that satisfy separate McCormick envelopes for every \(W_{ij}\) but cannot arise jointly from one common vector \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Products sharing variables must fit one joint rank-one moment matrix; retaining positive semidefiniteness couples them beyond independent McCormick envelopes.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Factor Product Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-one identity and resulting positive-semidefinite necessity are correct, but no source supports the claimed strengthening beyond independently imposed McCormick envelopes.

children.title: Quadratic Envelopes over Boxes
children.top_down_role: Envelope and underestimator families for quadratic functions on rectangular domains.

children.title: Separable Quadratic Box Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise convexification for diagonal quadratic structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_B q(x)=c+\sum_i\operatorname{vex}_{[L_i,U_i]}(a_it^2+b_it)(x_i)\).

notation.meaning: convex envelope on the indicated domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex envelope of a diagonal quadratic over a Cartesian box.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 DC Representation of Separable Functions p. 110

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[L_i,U_i]\) and let \(q(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n(a_ix_i^2+b_ix_i)\). Its convex envelope over \(B\) is separable:
\[
\operatorname{vex}_B q(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n g_i(x_i),
\]
where
\[
g_i(t)=
\begin{cases}
a_it^2+b_it,&a_i\ge0,\\
(a_iL_i^2+b_iL_i)\dfrac{U_i-t}{U_i-L_i}+(a_iU_i^2+b_iU_i)\dfrac{t-L_i}{U_i-L_i},&a_i<0.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus convex coordinates retain their quadratic graphs, while concave coordinates are replaced by endpoint secants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex envelope of a diagonal quadratic over a box is the sum of coordinate envelopes: convex terms remain quadratic and concave terms become secants.
knowledge_statements.title: Separable Quadratic Box Envelopes

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 DC Representation of Separable Functions p. 110

children.title: Edge-Concave Quadratic Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral envelope structure for edge-concave quadratics on boxes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_B q(x)=\min\{\sum_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(B)}\lambda_vq(v):\sum_v\lambda_vv=x,\ \sum_v\lambda_v=1,\ \lambda_v\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: convex envelope of q on B

review_flags: The supplied source discusses concave-function properties; direct confirmation of the edge-concave envelope formulation remains pending.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratics concave along every coordinate-parallel edge of a finite box.

source_refs.locator: 3. Some Key Properties of Concave Functions p. 49

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=x^\top Qx+c^\top x+d\) on the finite box \(B=\prod_i[L_i,U_i]\), and suppose \(Q_{ii}\le0\) for every \(i\). Then the restriction of \(q\) to every coordinate-parallel box edge is concave. Its convex envelope is the polyhedral lower hull of its vertex values:
\[
\operatorname{vex}_Bq(x)=
\min\left\{
\sum_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(B)}\lambda_vq(v):
\sum_v\lambda_vv=x,
\sum_v\lambda_v=1,
\lambda_v\ge0
\right\}.
\]
This representation may require exponentially many vertex weights even though it is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An edge-concave quadratic has a polyhedral convex envelope obtained as the lower convex hull of its values at box vertices.
knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Concave Quadratic Envelopes

source_witnesses.locator: 3. Some Key Properties of Concave Functions p. 49

children.title: Coupled Indefinite Box Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Underestimation families retaining interactions among several quadratic terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Indefinite Box Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint spectral correction for an indefinite quadratic on a finite box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=[l,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(q(x)=x^\top Qx+c^\top x+d\), where \(Q=Q^\top\). Choose a coupled matrix \(P\succeq0\) satisfying \(Q+P\succeq0\), and an affine function \(h(x)=a^\top x+b\) satisfying \(h(x)\ge x^\top Px\) for every \(x\in B\). Then \[g(x)=x^\top(Q+P)x+c^\top x+d-h(x)\] is convex on \(B\) and satisfies \(g(x)\le q(x)\) there. Off-diagonal entries of \(P\) preserve interactions among variables; diagonal \(P\) gives the separable special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite coupled correction and an affine overestimate of its quadratic term produce a convex box-wide underestimator of the original indefinite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\) is convex on \([l,u]\) and \(g(x)\le q(x)\) for every \(x\in[l,u]\).

notation.meaning: affine majorant of the correction quadratic

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

children.title: General Quadratic Envelope Hardness
children.top_down_role: The boundary between tractable special envelopes and hard coupled box convexification.

knowledge_statements.title: General Quadratic Envelope Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: NP-hardness boundary for exact convexification of coupled box quadratics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative edge weights \(w_{ij}\), define on \([0,1]^n\) the concave quadratic \[q(x)=-\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(x_i-x_j)^2.\] Its minimum is attained at a vertex, and \(\min_{x\in[0,1]^n}q(x)\) equals the negative maximum-cut weight of the graph. Because a function and its convex envelope have the same minimum over their domain, any polynomial-time procedure that constructs an exactly optimizable representation of \(\operatorname{conv}_B q\) for arbitrary coupled quadratics would solve weighted maximum cut in polynomial time. Thus exact general quadratic box-envelope construction is NP-hard unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact, efficiently optimizable convex envelopes for arbitrary coupled box quadratics would solve weighted maximum cut, so their general construction is NP-hard.
assumptions_latex: The envelope representation can be optimized in time polynomial in its encoding length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constructing an exactly optimizable convex-envelope representation for arbitrary quadratic functions on boxes is NP-hard unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).

notation.meaning: convex envelope of q over the box B
edge set of the weighted graph

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximum-cut reduction is plausible, but the NP-hardness claim has no citation and the meaning and encoding of an “exactly optimizable representation” require authoritative support.

children.title: Quadratic Bilinearization-Factorization Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Representations that expose quadratic interactions as lifted products before convexification.

children.title: Direct Pairwise Product Liftings
children.top_down_role: Liftings that assign a common coordinate to each quadratic product.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Pairwise Product Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical linear lifting of all quadratic monomials used by a quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in[l,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\), introduce one symmetric lifted coordinate \(X_{ij}=X_{ji}\) for every product \(x_ix_j\) appearing in the formulation. Then \[x^\top Qx=\langle Q,X\rangle\quad\text{whenever}\quad X=xx^\top.\] The direct pairwise-product lifting replaces each quadratic expression by its linear expression in \((x,X)\) and retains the nonconvex consistency equations \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\). A polyhedral relaxation results by replacing each such equation with its four bound-factor inequalities; using one common \(X_{ij}\) across all expressions preserves shared-product consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each distinct product receives one shared lifted coordinate, making every quadratic expression linear while isolating nonconvexity in product-consistency equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under \(X=xx^\top\), every quadratic form becomes linear as \(x^\top Qx=\langle Q,X\rangle\).

notation.meaning: symmetric matrix of lifted pairwise products
trace inner product between Q and X

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

children.title: Bipartite Bilinear Representations
children.top_down_role: Bilinear formulations organized by partitioned variable sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Bipartite Bilinear Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bilinearization when quadratic interactions cross a variable partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the variables be partitioned as \(x=(x_L,x_R)\). If every quadratic interaction joins the two parts and there are no square or within-part terms, then the quadratic component has the form \[x_L^\top Bx_R=\sum_{i\in L}\sum_{j\in R}B_{ij}x_ix_j.\] Introducing \(W_{ij}=x_ix_j\) only for edges \((i,j)\in L\times R\) yields the exact lifted expression \(\langle B,W\rangle\). With finite bounds, replacing each equality \(W_{ij}=x_ix_j\) by its McCormick envelope gives a polyhedral relaxation whose lifted interaction graph is bipartite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When all interactions cross a partition, the quadratic is a bipartite bilinear form requiring lifted products only across the two variable blocks.
assumptions_latex: The interaction graph admits a partition \(L\mathbin{\dot\cup}R\) with every quadratic edge crossing the partition.
All variables have finite lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic component equals \(\langle B,W\rangle\) under \(W_{ij}=x_ix_j\), using only cross-partition products.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact block-matrix expansion and termwise McCormick relaxation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-bilinear representation and termwise McCormick relaxation are mathematically standard and fit the container, but no inspectable scholarly citation is supplied.

children.title: Factorization-Dependent Relaxation Strength
children.top_down_role: Changes in bound quality caused by alternative quadratic factorizations or auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Dependent Relaxation Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxed projections need not be invariant under exact quadratic refactorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two extended formulations \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) project exactly onto the same quadratic graph before relaxation, and let \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) be obtained by separately convexifying the auxiliary product equations using their induced bounds. Exact equivalence of \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) does not imply \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}(R_1)=\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}(R_2)\): auxiliary-variable bounds and the grouping or duplication of products determine which convex-hull inequalities are imposed jointly. If \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}(R_1)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}(R_2)\), then \(R_1\) gives at least as strong a minimization lower bound as \(R_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent exact factorizations can yield different relaxations because auxiliary bounds and product grouping change the imposed convex-hull constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) are exact extended formulations of the same quadratic graph.
Each product equation is relaxed over valid finite bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact formulation equivalence does not ensure equal relaxed projections; projection inclusion orders minimization-bound strength.

notation.meaning: productwise convex relaxation of formulation k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: extended-formulation relaxations depend on auxiliary bounds and constraint grouping
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is plausible, but the assertion that exact reformulations can have unequal relaxed projections requires a cited theorem or concrete documented example.

children.title: Bound-Factor RLT
children.top_down_role: Product-derived constraints generated from finite variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Factor RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-degree RLT constraints generated solely from finite variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For bounded variables \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\), every product of two nonnegative bound factors is nonnegative. After introducing \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\), linearization gives \[X_{ij}\ge l_ix_j+l_jx_i-l_il_j,\qquad X_{ij}\ge u_ix_j+u_jx_i-u_iu_j,\] \[X_{ij}\le u_ix_j+l_jx_i-u_il_j,\qquad X_{ij}\le l_ix_j+u_jx_i-l_iu_j.\] These four inequalities are valid for every feasible product point. For \(i\ne j\) they describe the convex hull of a single bilinear graph over its rectangle; for \(i=j\) some inequalities may be redundant and the remaining constraints are only a polyhedral outer approximation of the square graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying pairs of nonnegative bound factors and linearizing yields the four standard RLT inequalities for each lifted product.
assumptions_latex: \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\) and \(l_j\le x_j\le u_j\) with finite bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The four displayed linear inequalities are valid for every point satisfying \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\).

notation.meaning: lifted coordinate for the product of variables i and j
finite lower and upper bounds for variable i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct expansion of nonnegative bound-factor products
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four bound-factor inequalities and the distinction between bilinear and square terms are correct, but the record supplies no specific RLT source.

children.title: Linear-Constraint Product RLT
children.top_down_role: RLT families generated from linear inequalities and equalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Constraint Product RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: RLT constraints obtained by multiplying linear rows by valid bound factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_r(x)=b_r-a_r^\top x\ge0\) be a valid linear inequality and let \(l_j\le x_j\le u_j\). The products \(g_r(x)(x_j-l_j)\ge0\) and \(g_r(x)(u_j-x_j)\ge0\) are valid quadratic inequalities. Replacing every \(x_ix_j\) by \(X_{ij}\) produces linear inequalities in \((x,X)\). If \(h_s(x)=d_s-c_s^\top x=0\) is a valid equality, then \(h_s(x)x_j=0\), or its shifted-bound-factor equivalents, yields valid linear equations after the same substitution. These are the linear-constraint product RLT rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply each valid linear row by nonnegative variable-bound factors, then replace quadratic monomials by lifted coordinates to obtain linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linearizing the displayed products yields constraints valid for the lifted quadratic graph.

notation.meaning: lifted replacement for the product of variables i and j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validity follows by multiplying nonnegative factors or a zero residual
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated inequality- and equality-product construction is valid and fits the RLT representation container, but it lacks a specific scholarly citation.

children.title: First-Level Quadratic RLT
children.top_down_role: The principal quadratic lifting level used for continuous QP and QCQP bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Level Quadratic RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic lifting and degree-two linearization for bounded QP or QCQP formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a bounded quadratic formulation with variables \(x\), linear rows, and quadratic objective or constraints. Introduce one symmetric coordinate \(X_{ij}\) for every required degree-two monomial. Replace each occurrence of \(x_ix_j\) by \(X_{ij}\); add all selected bound-factor and linear-row product constraints of total degree at most two after linearization. Solve the resulting linear program in \((x,X)\). Stop when the LP is solved to the prescribed tolerance and output its objective value and lifted solution. For minimization, the value is a valid lower bound because every original feasible point lifts as \((x,xx^\top)\) into the RLT relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift quadratic monomials, linearize the quadratic model and all chosen degree-two RLT products, then solve the resulting LP for a valid bound.
assumptions_latex: The original variables have finite bounds.
All generated product constraints are valid for the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The first-level RLT linear program contains every lifted feasible point \((x,xx^\top)\) and therefore returns a valid minimization lower bound.

notation.meaning: exact rank-one lift of an original point

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm describes a valid degree-two RLT relaxation and lower bound, but the precise first-level convention and construction require a cited RLT source.

children.title: Higher-Level RLT Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Successively enriched product spaces beyond the quadratic lifting level.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Level RLT Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested monomial liftings generated by products of increasing total degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a bounded polynomial formulation, level \(k\) introduces coordinates for required monomials of degree at most \(k+1\) and linearizes products of original valid constraints with nonnegative bound-factor monomials whenever the resulting degree is at most \(k+1\). Let \(R_k\) denote the resulting lifted polyhedron and \(P_k\) its projection onto coordinates retained at level \(k-1\). With consistent generation, \(P_k\subseteq R_{k-1}\). Consequently, minimization lower bounds satisfy \(v_{k-1}\le v_k\le v^*\). Convergence or finite exactness requires additional assumptions and is not implied solely by increasing the RLT level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher RLT levels add higher-degree monomials and constraint products, producing nested relaxations and nondecreasing minimization lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: The formulation is polynomial over a finite box.
Levels use consistent monomial coordinates and include all constraints retained at preceding levels.
\(v_k\) is the minimization value of level \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_k\subseteq R_{k-1}\) and \(v_{k-1}\le v_k\le v^*\).

notation.meaning: projection of level k onto preceding-level coordinates

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: adding valid lifted constraints yields nested feasible projections
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Structure-Exploiting RLT
children.top_down_role: RLT strengthening specialized to packing, covering, partitioning, sparsity, and related structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Exploiting RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selective valid-product generation guided by row supports and combinatorial structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_r\) be the support of a valid packing, covering, partitioning, or other structured linear row. A structure-exploiting RLT relaxation generates and linearizes only products whose variables and monomials lie in prescribed support neighborhoods, cliques, or sparsity blocks, while also using structure-implied identities or zeros. Every retained row must arise from a product known to be nonnegative or identically zero on the original feasible set. Hence the selective relaxation remains valid. If its rows form a subset of full-level RLT rows, its feasible region contains the full RLT region and its minimization bound cannot exceed the corresponding full-level bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate RLT products only on relevant supports or sparsity blocks and use structure-implied identities; validity is preserved, with a possible loss of bound strength.
assumptions_latex: Each generated product is validly nonnegative or identically zero on the original feasible set.
The selective rows are a subset of, or valid strengthenings of, the corresponding full-level RLT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selective generation preserves relaxation validity; when rows are omitted from full RLT, its minimization bound is no stronger than the full-level bound.

notation.meaning: variable support of structured row r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: selective retention of valid inequalities preserves outer-approximation validity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selective-generation principle and its validity comparison are sound as stated, but the claimed structure-exploiting RLT family lacks a specific source.

children.title: Formulation Sensitivity of RLT
children.top_down_role: Dependence of relaxation strength on redundant constraints and equivalent formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation Sensitivity of RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strengthening under redundant linear rows before RLT generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a bounded formulation and let \(F'=F\cup H\), where every row in \(H\) is valid for the feasible set of \(F\), so the original feasible sets coincide. Generate the same level of RLT from each displayed formulation, and denote the lifted relaxations by \(R(F)\) and \(R(F')\). All rows generated from \(F\) remain available for \(F'\), while products involving \(H\) may add constraints; therefore \[R(F')\subseteq R(F).\] The inclusion can be strict even though \(F\) and \(F'\) are equivalent before lifting. Thus redundant rows cannot weaken, and may strengthen, the associated minimization RLT bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid redundant rows before RLT generation preserves the original feasible set but can strictly strengthen the lifted relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(F'=F\cup H\) have the same original feasible set.
The same RLT level and lifting convention are used.
All original RLT rows are retained after adding \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(F')\subseteq R(F)\), so the minimization bound from \(F'\) is at least as strong as that from \(F\).

children.title: Spectral Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convex quadratic underestimators based on spectral curvature information.

children.title: Uniform Eigenvalue-Shift Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Global spectral shifts combined with bounded-domain correction.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Eigenvalue-Shift Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single spectral shift with coordinatewise box-secant correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=x^\top Qx+c^\top x+d\) on \(B=[l,u]\), where \(Q=Q^\top\), and set \(\alpha=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\). Define \[g_\alpha(x)=x^\top(Q+\alpha I)x+c^\top x+d-\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl((l_i+u_i)x_i-l_iu_i\bigr).\] Since \(Q+\alpha I\succeq0\), the function \(g_\alpha\) is convex. Moreover, \(x_i^2\le(l_i+u_i)x_i-l_iu_i\) on \([l_i,u_i]\), so \(g_\alpha(x)\le q(x)\) throughout \(B\). Equality holds at every box vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift all eigenvalues uniformly to nonnegativity and subtract coordinatewise square secants, obtaining a convex underestimator exact at box vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_\alpha\) is convex on \(B\), satisfies \(g_\alpha(x)\le q(x)\) on \(B\), and equals \(q\) at box vertices.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

children.title: Subspace Partial-Spectral Underestimator Family
children.top_down_role: Curvature corrections restricted to selected negative-curvature subspaces.

children.title: Selected-Subspace Curvature Corrections
children.top_down_role: Underestimators focused on prescribed negative-curvature subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Subspace Curvature Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex underestimation using a positive-semidefinite correction supported on a chosen subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) on a compact convex set \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\), with \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\). Choose an orthonormal matrix \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) and \(S\succeq0\), and set \(P=VSV^{\mathsf T}\). If \(Q+P\succeq0\) and an affine function \(U\) satisfies \(U(x)\ge x^{\mathsf T}Px\) for every \(x\in X\), then
\[g(x)=x^{\mathsf T}(Q+P)x+c^{\mathsf T}x+d-U(x)\]
is convex on \(X\) and satisfies \(g(x)\le q(x)\) there. Thus curvature is corrected only through directions in \(\operatorname{range}(V)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PSD correction supported on selected directions yields a convex quadratic underestimator when its quadratic contribution is subtracted through a valid affine upper estimator.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\) and \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is compact and convex.
\(U(x)\ge x^{\mathsf T}VSV^{\mathsf T}x\) for all \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\) is convex on \(X\) and \(g(x)\le q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis of the selected correction subspace.
Affine upper estimator of the correction quadratic on the domain.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected-subspace construction is mathematically consistent and the representation kind fits, but no inspectable source supports this specialized formulation.

children.title: Partial-Spectrum Curvature Corrections
children.top_down_role: Underestimators using only a selected portion of the negative spectrum.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Spectrum Curvature Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correction of selected eigenvalues with a uniform residual correction on the omitted eigenspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i v_iv_i^{\mathsf T}\), where \(\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n\) and the \(v_i\) are orthonormal. For \(k<n\), define \(V_k=[v_1,\ldots,v_k]\) and choose \(\rho\ge\max\{0,-\lambda_{k+1}\}\). The partial-spectrum correction
\[P_k=\sum_{i=1}^k\max\{0,-\lambda_i\}v_iv_i^{\mathsf T}+\rho(I-V_kV_k^{\mathsf T})\]
satisfies \(P_k\succeq0\) and \(Q+P_k\succeq0\). Consequently, replacing \(Q\) by \(Q+P_k\) convexifies the quadratic, while only the first \(k\) eigenpairs must be computed explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correct the computed negative eigenvalues exactly and shift the remaining eigenspace uniformly enough to make the entire quadratic curvature positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_k\succeq0\) and \(Q+P_k\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Matrix of the first k eigenvectors.
Uniform correction applied on the omitted eigenspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral correction formula is correct for the ordered eigendecomposition and the representation kind fits, but the record has no cited source.

children.title: Omitted-Curvature Strength Limits
children.top_down_role: Bound degradation attributable to curvature directions excluded from the correction.

knowledge_statements.title: Omitted-Curvature Strength Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary curvature coverage for convexity after a low-dimensional spectral correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(V\) have orthonormal columns, and let \(P=VSV^{\mathsf T}\) with \(S\succeq0\). Every vector \(z\in\operatorname{range}(V)^{\perp}\) satisfies \(z^{\mathsf T}(Q+P)z=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\). Hence, if an omitted direction \(z\ne0\) has \(z^{\mathsf T}Qz<0\), no choice of \(S\) can make \(Q+P\) positive semidefinite. A correction confined to \(\operatorname{range}(V)\) can therefore convexify the quadratic only if \(Q\) is already positive semidefinite on the orthogonal complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace correction cannot repair negative curvature in an orthogonal omitted direction; convexification requires nonnegative original curvature throughout the omitted space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If some \(z\in\operatorname{range}(V)^{\perp}\setminus\{0\}\) satisfies \(z^{\mathsf T}Qz<0\), then \(Q+VSV^{\mathsf T}\not\succeq0\) for every \(S\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Omitted subspace orthogonal to the corrected directions.
Correction supported on the selected subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The omitted-direction obstruction is correct and appropriately classified as a failure boundary, but it lacks source evidence.

children.title: Diagonal Convexification
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise curvature corrections exploiting finite bounds or discrete identities.

children.title: alphaBB Quadratic Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Diagonal perturbation families for box-constrained twice-differentiable models.

knowledge_statements.title: alphaBB Quadratic Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical diagonal convex underestimator for a twice-differentiable function over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=[l,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\) and let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(B\). For \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^n\), the alphaBB function is
\[g_\alpha(x)=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i).\]
Because each product \((x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\) is nonnegative on \(B\), \(g_\alpha\le f\) on \(B\). If
\[\nabla^2f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\quad\text{for every }x\in B,\]
then \(g_\alpha\) is a convex underestimator of \(f\) on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The alphaBB construction subtracts nonnegative separable box terms and chooses their weights so the resulting Hessian is positive semidefinite everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_\alpha\) is convex on \(B\) and \(g_\alpha(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in B\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The alphaBB formula, Hessian condition, and underestimation direction are correct, and definition is an appropriate kind; an authoritative alphaBB source is still required.

children.title: Optimized Diagonal Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Diagonal corrections selected for relaxation quality rather than only curvature validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimized Diagonal Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection of diagonal curvature corrections by minimizing a uniform box-loss bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(f\in C^2(B)\) on \(B=[l,u]\), choose \(\alpha\) by solving
\[\min_{\alpha\ge0}\ \sum_{i=1}^n\frac{(u_i-l_i)^2}{4}\alpha_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad \nabla^2f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\ \text{for all }x\in B.\]
For any optimizer \(\alpha^*\), output
\[g_{\alpha^*}(x)=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i^*(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i).\]
The objective minimizes the standard uniform bound on \(f(x)-g_\alpha(x)\), while the semidefinite constraint guarantees convexity. A finite SDP results whenever a valid finite family of Hessian lower bounds replaces the semi-infinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose diagonal convexification weights by minimizing their worst-case box penalty subject to positive-semidefinite corrected curvature, then form the corresponding separable underestimator.
assumptions_latex: The displayed parameter problem is feasible and attains an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(g_{\alpha^*}\) is a convex underestimator minimizing the displayed uniform-loss surrogate among feasible diagonal corrections.

notation.meaning: Maximum of the ith separable box product.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimization criterion correctly measures the uniform separable box penalty, but neither the algorithm nor the stated finite-SDP reduction has an inspectable supporting source.

children.title: Quadratic Convex Reformulation Family
children.top_down_role: Equivalent reformulations of discrete quadratic models with improved continuous quadratic relaxations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: MIQCR quadratic convex reformulation family

children.title: Integrality-Identity Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Equivalent objective transformations derived from discrete-variable identities.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Identity Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-equivalent quadratic reformulations obtained from binary-variable identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a binary quadratic problem with \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) and objective \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), where \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\). For any \(r\in\mathbb R^n\), define
\[q_r(x)=q(x)+\sum_{i=1}^nr_i(x_i^2-x_i)=x^{\mathsf T}(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(r))x+(c-r)^{\mathsf T}x+d.\]
Since \(x_i^2=x_i\) for binary variables, \(q_r=q\) at every integer-feasible point. Different choices of \(r\) alter the continuous relaxation; in particular, any \(r\) satisfying \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(r)\succeq0\) produces a convex quadratic objective without changing the discrete problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding weighted binary identities leaves every integer objective unchanged but modifies the continuous relaxation and can make the quadratic objective convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_r(x)=q(x)\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\), and \(q_r\) is convex when \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(r)\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Weights applied to the binary identities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary identity reformulation and convexity condition are correct, and representation fits the container, but no source is cited.

children.title: Constraint-Based Quadratic Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Equivalent transformations derived from valid linear and quadratic relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Based Quadratic Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent objective transformations generated by relations that vanish on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(Ax=b\), and let \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), with \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\). For arbitrary \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(W\in\mathbb S^m\), define
\[q_{y,W}(x)=q(x)+y^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)+(Ax-b)^{\mathsf T}W(Ax-b).\]
Then \(q_{y,W}(x)=q(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). Its quadratic matrix is \(Q+A^{\mathsf T}WA\); hence choosing \(W\) so that \(Q+A^{\mathsf T}WA\succeq0\) gives a convex quadratic reformulation that is objective-equivalent on \(F\), although its relaxation outside \(Ax=b\) may differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear and quadratic multiples of equality residuals vanish on feasible points, permitting equivalent objectives with altered—and potentially convex—quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_{y,W}=q\) on \(F\), and \(q_{y,W}\) is convex when \(Q+A^{\mathsf T}WA\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric weight for the quadratic residual identity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality-residual terms vanish on the feasible set and the stated quadratic matrix is correct, but the representation lacks source support.

children.title: SDP-Calibrated Quadratic Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Reformulation parameters selected through semidefinite bound information.

knowledge_statements.title: SDP-Calibrated Quadratic Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature parameters selected from a semidefinite relaxation or its dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a binary quadratic objective \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), solve a Shor semidefinite relaxation and obtain dual diagonal multipliers \(r\in\mathbb R^n\) associated with the lifted identities \(X_{ii}=x_i\). Form
\[q_r(x)=x^{\mathsf T}(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(r))x+(c-r)^{\mathsf T}x+d.\]
Accept a multiplier vector only when the associated dual slack implies \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(r)\succeq0\), and output the resulting convex quadratic reformulation. The equality \(x_i^2=x_i\) ensures that \(q_r\) and \(q\) agree on every binary point, while the SDP dual objective calibrates \(r\) to relaxation-bound information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use dual multipliers from a Shor relaxation to choose a convex diagonal reformulation that remains identical to the original objective at binary points.
assumptions_latex: The Shor SDP and its stated dual multipliers are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output objective is convex and equals \(q\) on every binary point.

notation.meaning: Lifted matrix variable representing pairwise products.
SDP-dual multipliers for diagonal lifting identities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional output is mathematically valid once the diagonal PSD condition holds, but the cited generic SDP section does not specifically support the claimed extraction and calibration of these multipliers from the Shor dual.

children.title: Lagrangian Quadratic Underestimation
children.top_down_role: Convex quadratic bounds obtained through constraint aggregation and multiplier-based curvature modification.

children.title: Quadratic Constraint Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Aggregated quadratic models used to expose tractable convex lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Constraint Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian aggregation of quadratic inequalities into a tractable lower-bounding quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[p^*=\inf\{q_0(x):x\in X,\ q_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},\]
where \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and all \(q_i\) are quadratic. For any \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), define \(L_\lambda(x)=q_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iq_i(x)\). Every feasible \(x\) satisfies \(L_\lambda(x)\le q_0(x)\), and therefore
\[\inf_{x\in X}L_\lambda(x)\le p^*.\]
If the aggregated quadratic has positive-semidefinite Hessian and \(X\) is convex with tractable constraints, this lower bound is obtained from a convex optimization problem. Maximizing it over \(\lambda\ge0\) gives the Lagrangian quadratic bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative multipliers aggregate quadratic constraints into a global lower-bounding objective; convex aggregate curvature makes evaluation tractable.
assumptions_latex: \(q_i\) are real-valued quadratic functions on \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}L_\lambda(x)\le p^*\) for every \(\lambda\ge0\).

children.title: Lagrangian–SDP Bound Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationships between multiplier-based quadratic bounds and semidefinite relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian–SDP Bound Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality between the quadratic Lagrangian dual and the dual of the inhomogeneous Shor relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_ix+2c_i^{\mathsf T}x+d_i\) and consider constraints \(q_i(x)\le0\). For \(\lambda\ge0\), let \(Q(\lambda)=Q_0+\sum_i\lambda_iQ_i\), \(c(\lambda)=c_0+\sum_i\lambda_ic_i\), and \(d(\lambda)=d_0+\sum_i\lambda_id_i\). The Lagrangian lower bound equals
\[\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\,\tau}\left\{\tau:\begin{pmatrix}d(\lambda)-\tau&c(\lambda)^{\mathsf T}\\c(\lambda)&Q(\lambda)\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.\]
This is the dual of the standard inhomogeneous Shor SDP relaxation. If that SDP satisfies strong duality, its primal relaxation value equals the displayed multiplier bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual PSD constraint for a Shor relaxation exactly encodes a global lower bound on the aggregated quadratic Lagrangian; SDP strong duality equates their values.
assumptions_latex: Equality with the primal SDP value additionally requires SDP strong duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian dual value equals the Shor SDP dual value, and equals the primal Shor value under SDP strong duality.

notation.meaning: Coefficients of the aggregated quadratic Lagrangian.
Certified global lower bound on the aggregate.

children.title: Quadratic Duality-Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem structures that preserve or destroy exact multiplier-based bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Duality-Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete gap caused by multiple quadratic integrality equalities and a non-rank-one SDP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For one quadratic inequality satisfying a strict-feasibility hypothesis, the S-lemma can make the quadratic Lagrangian bound exact. Exactness does not extend to arbitrary systems of quadratic equalities. Consider
\[\min\{x_1x_2+x_1x_3+x_2x_3:x_i^2=1,\ i=1,2,3\}.\]
Its primal value is \(-1\). The Shor relaxation minimizes \(X_{12}+X_{13}+X_{23}\) subject to \(X\succeq0\) and \(X_{ii}=1\), and has value \(-3/2\), attained by three unit vectors with pairwise inner products \(-1/2\). By Lagrangian–SDP correspondence, the multiplier bound is also \(-3/2\), producing a positive duality gap of \(1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-constraint exactness does not survive general multiple quadratic identities: the three-variable triangle example has primal value −1 but multiplier and SDP bound −3/2.
assumptions_latex: The Shor relaxation drops the rank-one requirement on \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The example has primal value \(-1\), Lagrangian–SDP bound \(-3/2\), and duality gap \(1/2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The triangle example and its values are mathematically consistent and failure_boundary fits, but the cited general duality section does not specifically evidence this example or the accompanying S-lemma contrast.

children.title: Shor Semidefinite Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: First-order matrix lifting of quadratic objectives and constraints through rank relaxation.

children.title: Inhomogeneous Quadratic Liftings
children.top_down_role: Lifted representations retaining original and pairwise-product coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Inhomogeneous Quadratic Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shor lifting that retains constant, linear, and pairwise-product coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), introduce \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and the inhomogeneous moment matrix
\[Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}.\]
The exact quadratic lifting requires \(Y=(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T}\), equivalently \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\). Under this identity,
\[x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d=\langle Q,X\rangle+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d.\]
The inhomogeneous Shor relaxation drops the rank-one condition and retains \(Y\succeq0\), together with lifted linear constraints. It therefore preserves the original and pairwise-product coordinates while replacing their nonconvex consistency relation by a semidefinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift a quadratic model to a matrix containing constants, original variables, and pairwise products, then relax rank-one consistency to positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint \(Y\succeq0\) is a convex relaxation of the exact rank-one inhomogeneous lifting.

notation.meaning: Inhomogeneous moment matrix containing constant, linear, and quadratic coordinates.
Trace inner product replacing the quadratic term.

children.title: Homogenized Quadratic Liftings
children.top_down_role: Augmented matrix representations for affine quadratic data.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogenized Quadratic Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Augmented-matrix representation of affine quadratic functions and its rank-relaxed moment lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d\in\mathbb R\), define \(q(x)=x^\top Qx+2c^\top x+d\), \(z=(1,x^\top)^\top\), and \(\bar Q=\begin{pmatrix}d&c^\top\\c&Q\end{pmatrix}\). Then \(q(x)=z^\top\bar Qz=\langle\bar Q,Z\rangle\) for \(Z=zz^\top\). Moreover, \(Z=zz^\top\) with \(z_0=1\) is equivalent to \(Z\succeq0\), \(Z_{00}=1\), and \(\operatorname{rank}Z=1\). Dropping only the rank condition gives the standard homogenized semidefinite lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine quadratic data become linear matrix functionals after homogenization; discarding the lifted matrix's rank-one condition yields the basic semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(x)=\langle\bar Q,zz^\top\rangle\), with the convex relaxation \(Z\succeq0\), \(Z_{00}=1\).

notation.meaning: augmented matrix representing the affine quadratic function
