children.title: Shor Relaxations for Quadratic Programs
children.top_down_role: Matrix-cone bounds for quadratic objectives over linear domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Shor Relaxations for Quadratic Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic Shor lower bound for a quadratic objective over a polyhedral domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(p^*=\inf\{x^\top Qx+2c^\top x+d:Ax\le b\}\), where \(Q=Q^\top\). Its basic Shor relaxation is \[p_{\mathrm S}=\inf_{x,X}\{\langle Q,X\rangle+2c^\top x+d:Ax\le b,\ \begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\}.\] Every feasible \(x\) of the quadratic program induces the feasible choice \(X=xx^\top\) with unchanged objective value. Consequently, \(p_{\mathrm S}\le p^*\), allowing either value to be \(-\infty\). Additional valid lifted linear constraints may strengthen this bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the quadratic moment xxᵀ by a matrix constrained only through positive semidefiniteness produces a computable lower bound for a linearly constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm S}\le p^*\).

notation.meaning: relaxed matrix surrogate for the quadratic moment \(xx^\top\)

children.title: Shor Relaxations for QCQP
children.top_down_role: Matrix-cone bounds jointly representing quadratic objectives and constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Shor Relaxations for QCQP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous lifted relaxation of a quadratic objective and finitely many quadratic inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_i(x)=x^\top Q_i x+2c_i^\top x+d_i\), with \(Q_i=Q_i^\top\), and consider \(p^*=\inf\{q_0(x):q_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). The Shor relaxation is \[p_{\mathrm S}=\inf_{x,X}\{\langle Q_0,X\rangle+2c_0^\top x+d_0:\langle Q_i,X\rangle+2c_i^\top x+d_i\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\ \begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\}.\] Since \(X=xx^\top\) embeds every QCQP-feasible point, \(p_{\mathrm S}\le p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The QCQP Shor relaxation linearizes every quadratic using one shared moment matrix and drops its rank-one constraint, thereby giving a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization QCQP over \(\mathbb R^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm S}\le p^*\).

children.title: Shor Dual Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual conic interpretations of Shor lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Shor Dual Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite multiplier certificates for lower bounds on a lifted minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the relaxation \(p_{\mathrm S}=\inf\{\langle C,Zangle:\langle A_i,Zangle\le b_i,\ \langle E_j,Zangle=e_j,\ Z\succeq0\}\). If \(\lambda_i\ge0\), \(
u_j\in\mathbb R\), and \[S=C+\sum_i\lambda_iA_i+\sum_j
u_jE_j\succeq0,\] then every primal-feasible \(Z\) satisfies \[\langle C,Zangle\ge-\sum_i\lambda_i b_i-\sum_j
u_j e_j.\] Thus \( eta=-\sum_i\lambda_i b_i-\sum_j
u_j e_j\) is a directly verifiable lower-bound certificate for the Shor relaxation and hence for the original minimization QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative inequality multipliers, free equality multipliers, and a positive-semidefinite dual slack certify a numerical lower bound for the Shor relaxation and original QCQP.
assumptions_latex: The displayed primal SDP is a relaxation of a minimization problem
\(Z\), \(C\), \(A_i\), and \(E_j\) are symmetric matrices of equal size
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm S}\ge\beta=-\sum_i\lambda_i b_i-\sum_j\nu_j e_j\).

children.title: Classical S-Lemma Regime
children.top_down_role: The principal one-inequality quadratic implication setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical S-Lemma Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inequality-form real S-lemma under a strict feasible-point condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_0,q_1:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be quadratic functions. Suppose there exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(q_1(\bar x)<0\). Then the implication \[q_1(x)\le0\ \Longrightarrow\ q_0(x)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n\] holds if and only if there exists a scalar \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \[q_0(x)+\lambda q_1(x)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.\] Equivalently, the augmented symmetric matrix of \(q_0+\lambda q_1\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict feasibility of one quadratic inequality, its implication of another quadratic's nonnegativity is equivalent to one nonnegative scalar-multiplier certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(q_0\) and \(q_1\) are real quadratic functions on \(\mathbb R^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_1\le0\Rightarrow q_0\ge0\) if and only if \(q_0+\lambda q_1\ge0\) globally for some \(\lambda\ge0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the standard strict-feasibility inequality form of the real S-lemma

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict-feasibility inequality form, multiplier sign, and augmented-matrix equivalence are standard and correctly stated. Because this is a nontrivial equivalence theorem and no inspectable theorem or section source is supplied, it needs an authoritative locator.

children.title: Quadratic-Equality S-Lemma Variants

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Equality S-Lemma Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unrestricted scalar-multiplier certificates for implications imposed by one quadratic equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_0,q_1:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be quadratic functions. For any \(\mu\in\mathbb R\), global nonnegativity \[q_0(x)+\mu q_1(x)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n\] certifies \[q_1(x)=0\ \Longrightarrow\ q_0(x)\ge0.\] If \(\bar Q_i\) is the augmented matrix of \(q_i\), the certificate is equivalent to \(\bar Q_0+\mu\bar Q_1\succeq0\). Unlike the inequality S-lemma, \(\mu\) is unrestricted; a converse requires additional hypotheses on the equality quadratic and is not automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free scalar multiplier making the combined quadratic globally nonnegative certifies nonnegativity on one quadratic equality, but converse validity requires extra regularity.
assumptions_latex: \(q_0\) and \(q_1\) are real quadratic functions on \(\mathbb R^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar Q_0+\mu\bar Q_1\succeq0\) implies \(q_1(x)=0\Rightarrow q_0(x)\ge0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed one-way certificate follows directly by restriction to the equality set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed unrestricted-multiplier condition is a correct sufficient certificate, and the record appropriately avoids asserting an unconditional converse. A source is still needed to support its placement among quadratic-equality S-lemma variants and the stated converse limitation.

children.title: Degenerate-Interior S-Lemma Variants

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Interior S-Lemma Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slater failure for a quadratic inequality and the resulting limit of scalar-multiplier exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a quadratic constraint \(q_1(x)\le0\), the degenerate-interior regime is \[\{x:q_1(x)\le0\}\ne\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad\{x:q_1(x)<0\}=\varnothing.\] In this regime, any \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \(q_0+\lambda q_1\ge0\) globally still certifies \(q_0\ge0\) on \(\{q_1\le0\}\), but the converse assertion of the classical S-lemma is not guaranteed. Exact variants must add structural assumptions or first reduce the problem to the affine hull or minimal face containing the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a quadratic inequality is feasible but nowhere strict, scalar certificates remain sufficient, while classical S-lemma necessity can fail without reduction or structural assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(q_0\) and \(q_1\) are real quadratic functions on \(\mathbb R^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absence of \(q_1(x)<0\) removes the classical hypothesis ensuring necessity of a scalar multiplier.

notation.meaning: strictly feasible set of the quadratic inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition of the feasible-but-nowhere-strict regime and the loss of the classical S-lemma hypothesis are correct. The broader assertion about exact variants and affine-hull or minimal-face reduction requires an authoritative variant-specific source.

children.title: Classical Trust-Region Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exact relaxation structure for the single trust-region problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Trust-Region Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Shor relaxation for one Euclidean-ball-constrained quadratic minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=Q^\top\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\Delta>0\). For \[p^*=\min_{\|x\|_2\le\Delta}\bigl(x^\top Qx+2c^\top x+d\bigr),\] consider \[p_{\mathrm S}=\min_{x,X}\left\{\langle Q,X\rangle+2c^\top x+d:\operatorname{tr}X\le\Delta^2,\ \begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.\] Then \(p_{\mathrm S}=p^*\). Moreover, the relaxation possesses an optimal lifted matrix of rank one, so an optimal trust-region vector can be recovered without a relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a single Euclidean trust-region constraint, the Shor semidefinite relaxation has the same optimum and admits a rank-one optimal lift.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm S}=p^*\), and a rank-one optimal lifted matrix exists.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 What Is a Trust-Region Algorithm? p. 1

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 What Is a Trust-Region Algorithm? p. 1

The cited introductory model section does not specifically support the SDP exactness theorem, so a theorem-level or exactness-specific locator is required.

children.title: Generalized Trust-Region Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness and duality for generalized one-quadratic-constraint models.

assumptions_latex: There exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(q_1(\bar x)<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The QCQP infimum, Shor-relaxation infimum, and attained multiplier-dual maximum are equal.

notation.meaning: homogenized matrix of the quadratic function q_i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semidefinite value and scalar-multiplier duality for one strictly feasible quadratic constraint, without asserting primal attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), let \(q_i(x)=x^\top Q_i x+2c_i^\top x+d_i\), where \(Q_i=Q_i^\top\), and let \(\bar Q_i\) be its homogenized matrix. Suppose there exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(q_1(\bar x)<0\), and suppose \[p^*=\inf\{q_0(x):x\in\mathbb R^n,\ q_1(x)\le0\}>-\infty.\] Then \[p^*=\inf\{\langle\bar Q_0,Z\rangle:\langle\bar Q_1,Z\rangle\le0,\ Z_{00}=1,\ Z\succeq0\}\] and \[p^*=\max_{\lambda\ge0,\,\gamma\in\mathbb R}\{\gamma:\bar Q_0+\lambda\bar Q_1-\gamma e_0e_0^\top\succeq0\}.\] Thus the one-constraint Shor relaxation is exact in value, and the common value has an attained scalar-multiplier semidefinite certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one strictly feasible quadratic constraint and a finite infimum, the QCQP and Shor relaxation have the same infimum, and the scalar-multiplier semidefinite dual attains that value; primal attainment is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Trust-Region Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[p^*=\min\{x_1x_2+x_1x_3+x_2x_3:x_i^2=1,\ i=1,2,3\}.\] Its Shor relaxation is \[p_{\mathrm S}=\min\{X_{12}+X_{13}+X_{23}:X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1,\ i=1,2,3\}.\] The two optimal values are \[p^*=-1\qquad\text{and}\qquad p_{\mathrm S}=-\frac32.\] Hence this three-constraint QCQP has a strict Shor relaxation gap.

children.title: Rank-One Exactness Certificates
children.top_down_role: Exactness certification through rank-one optimal lifted solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Exactness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal rank-one optimality as a verifiable certificate of relaxation exactness and recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a homogenized Shor relaxation of a minimization QCQP have optimal matrix \(Z^*\succeq0\) with \(Z^*_{00}=1\). If \(\operatorname{rank}Z^*=1\), then there is a unique vector \(z^*=(1,(x^*)^\top)^\top\), up to the fixed positive first coordinate, such that \(Z^*=z^*(z^*)^\top\). Every lifted quadratic constraint then equals its original value at \(x^*\). Consequently, \(x^*\) is feasible for the QCQP, its objective equals the relaxation optimum, and the relaxation is exact. The factorization of \(Z^*\) therefore certifies both exactness and deterministic recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal lifted matrix with rank one factors into an original feasible vector whose objective equals the relaxation bound, certifying exactness and recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(Z^*\) is optimal for the Shor relaxation
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered \(x^*\) is QCQP-optimal and the Shor relaxation has zero gap.

notation.meaning: rank-one factor encoding the recovered vector

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

children.title: Low-Constraint Rank-Reduction Families
children.top_down_role: Rank-control results tied to the number and structure of conic constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Constraint Rank-Reduction Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barvinok–Pataki rank bound for compact equality-form spectrahedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) be nonempty and compact, with the affine constraints linearly independent. For every \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), the problem \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:X\in\mathcal F\}\) has an optimal solution \(X^\star\) whose rank \(r\) satisfies \[\frac{r(r+1)}2\le m.\] More generally, the same bound applies with \(m\) replaced by the number of independent affine constraints active on the minimal face containing an optimal extreme point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact SDP with few independent affine constraints admits an optimum whose rank is bounded by the triangular-number inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists X^\star\in\operatorname{argmin}_{X\in\mathcal F}\langle C,X\rangle\) with \(r=\operatorname{rank}(X^\star)\) and \(r(r+1)/2\le m\).

notation.meaning: cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices
rank of the selected optimal matrix

children.title: Deterministic Vector Extraction
children.top_down_role: Recovery families exploiting identifiable low-rank structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Vector Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extraction from an identified rank-one lifted matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a matrix \(X^\star\in\mathbb S_+^n\) known to satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}(X^\star)=1\). Compute its unique positive eigenvalue \(\lambda_1\) and a corresponding unit eigenvector \(u_1\), and set \(x^\star=\sqrt{\lambda_1}u_1\). Choose the sign of \(u_1\) using any available affine normalization, such as a prescribed homogenizing coordinate; otherwise either sign is valid for sign-invariant quadratic data. Output \(x^\star\), for which \(X^\star=x^\star(x^\star)^\top\). Thus every lifted quadratic identity \(\langle Q,X^\star\rangle\) becomes \((x^\star)^\top Qx^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor a rank-one PSD relaxation solution through its positive eigenpair; affine normalization resolves the otherwise unavoidable sign ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^\star=x^\star(x^\star)^\top\) and \(\langle Q,X^\star\rangle=(x^\star)^\top Qx^\star\) for every \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\).

notation.meaning: positive eigenvalue and associated unit eigenvector of the lift

children.title: Randomized Vector Recovery
children.top_down_role: Sampling and rounding families for higher-rank lifted solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Vector Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian sampling and problem-specific rounding from a higher-rank PSD lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,r,N\in\mathbb N_{>0}\). Input \(X^\star\in\mathbb S_+^n\), a factor \(L\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) satisfying \(LL^\top=X^\star\), a measurable rounding-and-repair map \(R:\mathbb R^n\to F\) into the original feasible set \(F\), and an objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\). Independently draw \(g_k\sim\mathcal N(0,I_r)\), form \(z_k=Lg_k\), and set \(x_k=R(z_k)\) for \(k=1,\ldots,N\). For minimization, output any \(\widehat x\in\operatorname{argmin}_{1\le k\le N}f(x_k)\); reverse the comparison for maximization. Before rounding, \(\mathbb E[z_kz_k^\top]=X^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample Gaussian vectors whose covariance equals the PSD relaxation solution, repair them into feasibility, and return the best sampled candidate.
assumptions_latex: \(R:\mathbb R^n\to F\) is measurable and maps every sampled vector into \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x\in F\), and each unrounded sample satisfies \(\mathbb E[z_kz_k^\top]=X^\star\).

notation.meaning: rectangular square-root factor of the lifted matrix

children.title: Higher-Rank Relaxation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes in which lifted feasibility does not yield exact primal recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Rank Relaxation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Five-cycle Max-Cut exhibits a strict rank-two SDP gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For unweighted Max-Cut on the cycle \(C_5\), the integral optimum is \(4\). Its standard semidefinite relaxation is \[\max\left\{\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E(C_5)}(1-X_{ij}):X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1\right\}.\] Choose five unit vectors successively separated by angle \(4\pi/5\) in \(\mathbb R^2\), and let \(X\) be their Gram matrix. Then \(X\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(X)=2\), and every cycle edge has \(X_{ij}=\cos(4\pi/5)\). The relaxation value is therefore \(\frac52(1+\cos(\pi/5))>4\), so no exact cut vector can be recovered while preserving this lifted value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The five-cycle has maximum cut four, but a feasible rank-two Gram matrix attains a strictly larger SDP value.
assumptions_latex: The graph is the unweighted five-cycle \(C_5\).
The displayed relaxation uses unit-diagonal Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}(\mathrm{SDP})\ge\frac52(1+\cos(\pi/5))>4=\operatorname{val}(\mathrm{MaxCut})\).

notation.meaning: Gram matrix of the relaxation vectors

children.title: Scalable Semidefinite Surrogates
children.top_down_role: Cheaper approximations and decompositions of full semidefinite quadratic relaxations.

children.title: Second-Order-Cone Principal-Minor Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Conic quadratic relaxations retaining selected low-dimensional matrix conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Principal-Minor Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: All two-by-two PSD principal-minor conditions expressed as rotated-cone constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), imposing positive semidefiniteness on every principal submatrix indexed by \(\{i,j\}\) is equivalent to \[X_{ii}\ge0,\qquad X_{jj}\ge0,\qquad X_{ij}^2\le X_{ii}X_{jj}\quad(1\le i<j\le n).\] Each inequality is representable by the second-order-cone constraint \[\left\|(2X_{ij},X_{ii}-X_{jj})\right\|_2\le X_{ii}+X_{jj}.\] Every PSD matrix satisfies these constraints, so replacing \(X\succeq0\) by them gives an outer relaxation. For \(n\ge3\), the converse can fail because higher-order principal minors remain uncontrolled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requiring every two-by-two principal submatrix to be PSD yields an SOC-representable outer approximation, but not full PSD in general.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\succeq0\Rightarrow X_{\{i,j\},\{i,j\}}\succeq0\) for all \(i<j\), with each local condition second-order-cone representable.

notation.meaning: two-by-two principal submatrix indexed by i and j

children.title: Diagonal-Dominance Cone Surrogates
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral and conic substitutes based on structured matrix cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal-Dominance Cone Surrogates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP and SOCP inner surrogates of the positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(DD_n=\{X\in\mathbb S^n:X_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}|X_{ij}|\ \forall i\}\). Define \(SDD_n\) as the matrices admitting \[X=\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}E_{ij}^\top W^{ij}E_{ij},\qquad W^{ij}\in\mathbb S_+^2,\] where \(E_{ij}x=(x_i,x_j)\). Then \(DD_n\subseteq SDD_n\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\). Membership in \(DD_n\) has a linear extended formulation, while membership in \(SDD_n\) has a second-order-cone formulation because each two-by-two PSD condition is SOC representable. Replacing a PSD variable by either cone gives a tractable inner restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonally dominant and scaled-diagonally-dominant matrices provide LP- and SOCP-representable inner approximations of the PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(DD_n\subseteq SDD_n\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\), with LP and SOCP extended formulations respectively.

notation.meaning: cone of symmetric diagonally dominant matrices
coordinate selector for indices i and j

children.title: Positive-Semidefinite Cut Outer Approximations
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral approximations generated from violated matrix-cone geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Cut Outer Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvector separation for polyhedral outer approximation of the PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite set \(V_0\subset\mathbb R^n\). At iteration \(t\), solve the current relaxation with constraints \(v^\top Xv\ge0\) for all \(v\in V_t\), obtaining \(X_t\in\mathbb S^n\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(X_t)\ge-\varepsilon\), stop and return \(X_t\) as \(\varepsilon\)-PSD. Otherwise choose a unit eigenvector \(u_t\) for a negative eigenvalue and set \(V_{t+1}=V_t\cup\{u_t\}\). The added linear cut \(\langle u_tu_t^\top,X\rangle\ge0\) is valid for every \(X\succeq0\) and excludes \(X_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly separate a non-PSD matrix using its most negative eigenvector and add the resulting valid linear inequality.
assumptions_latex: Each master relaxation attains a solution \(X_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination certifies \(\lambda_{\min}(X_t)\ge-\varepsilon\); every generated cut is valid for \(\mathbb S_+^n\).

notation.meaning: finite set of accumulated separating directions

children.title: Chordal Sparse-SDP Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Clique-based decomposition of sparse lifted quadratic matrices.

children.title: Chordal Clique Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Clique-based semidefinite decomposition for chordal sparsity patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Clique Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition of a chordally sparse PSD matrix into clique-supported PSD blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\), and let \(\mathbb S_+^n(E,0)\) denote PSD matrices whose off-diagonal nonzeros are restricted to \(E\). A matrix \(X\) belongs to this sparse PSD cone if and only if there exist \(Z_k\in\mathbb S_+^{|C_k|}\) such that \[X=\sum_{k=1}^p E_{C_k}^\top Z_kE_{C_k}.\] Here \(E_{C_k}\) selects the coordinates of clique \(C_k\). Thus one large sparse PSD constraint can be represented using PSD blocks indexed by maximal cliques and a linear assembly equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PSD matrix with chordal sparsity is exactly a sum of PSD matrices embedded on the maximal cliques.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n(E,0)\iff\exists Z_k\succeq0:\ X=\sum_{k=1}^pE_{C_k}^\top Z_kE_{C_k}\).

notation.meaning: PSD cone with zeros outside the graph sparsity pattern
PSD block supported on maximal clique k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly describes decomposition of the chordally sparse PSD cone, distinct from the PSD-completion theorem, but no authoritative theorem locator is supplied.

children.title: Sparse PSD Completion
children.top_down_role: Matrix-completion structure underlying sparse semidefinite representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse PSD Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal positive-semidefinite completion theorem for partial symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal, with every diagonal specified, and let \(A\) be a partial symmetric matrix whose specified off-diagonal entries correspond exactly to \(E\). Then \(A\) admits a positive-semidefinite completion \(X\in\mathbb S_+^{|V|}\) if and only if every fully specified principal submatrix \(A[C,C]\) indexed by a maximal clique \(C\) of \(G\) is positive semidefinite. The completed entries on nonedges need not be unique; the theorem characterizes existence rather than uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chordal sparsity graph, a partial symmetric matrix has a PSD completion exactly when every maximal-clique submatrix is PSD.
assumptions_latex: All diagonal entries and precisely the edge entries of the partial symmetric matrix are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) has a PSD completion if and only if \(A[C,C]\succeq0\) for every maximal clique \(C\) of \(G\).

notation.meaning: fully specified principal submatrix on clique C
a full symmetric completion of the partial matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The chordal PSD-completion theorem is stated precisely and has the correct theorem content kind, but it requires an authoritative theorem or page locator.

children.title: Clique-Overlap Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility requirements across overlapping sparse matrix blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Overlap Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear compatibility condition for local clique matrix variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\) be maximal cliques and let \(X^{(k)}\in\mathbb S^{|C_k|}\) be a local matrix for clique \(C_k\). The family represents one well-defined partial symmetric matrix on the union of clique edges if and only if, for every pair \(k,\ell\), \[X^{(k)}[C_k\cap C_\ell,C_k\cap C_\ell]=X^{(\ell)}[C_k\cap C_\ell,C_k\cap C_\ell].\] For a clique tree satisfying the running-intersection property, it is sufficient to impose these equalities only on intersections associated with tree edges. If additionally every \(X^{(k)}\succeq0\) and the graph is chordal, the assembled partial matrix has a PSD completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local clique matrices describe one global partial matrix precisely when their entries agree on every shared clique intersection.
assumptions_latex: The local matrix indices are identified with their vertices in each clique.
For the tree-edge reduction, the clique tree has the running-intersection property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pairwise overlap equality is necessary and sufficient for assembly; clique-tree edge equalities suffice under running intersection.

notation.meaning: local symmetric matrix on clique k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The overlap compatibility condition and clique-tree reduction fit the node and are mathematically coherent, but the nontrivial running-intersection claim has no cited source.

children.title: Nonchordal Sparsity Extensions

knowledge_statements.title: Nonchordal Sparsity Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal-extension construction for nonchordal sparse PSD constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a nonchordal sparsity graph \(G=(V,E)\). Choose a chordal extension \(G'=(V,E')\) with \(E\subseteq E'\), introduce variables for the fill edges \(E'\setminus E\), enumerate the maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\) of \(G'\), and impose \(X[C_k,C_k]\succeq0\) for every \(k\), together with equality of duplicated entries on clique overlaps. Projecting out the fill-edge and duplicate variables characterizes partial matrices on \(G\) that possess a PSD completion. Different extensions are equivalent after exact projection but can differ substantially in maximal-clique sizes and computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Triangulate a nonchordal sparsity graph, add fill variables, and enforce consistent PSD constraints on the extension’s maximal cliques.
assumptions_latex: All diagonal entries belong to the specified pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After projection, the clique formulation describes exactly the partial matrices on \(G\) admitting a PSD completion.

notation.meaning: maximal cliques of the chordal extension

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The triangulation-and-projection algorithm fits the container, but exactness after projection and equivalence across chordal extensions require an authoritative source.

children.title: Exact Copositive Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Exact conic representations of bounded continuous and mixed-binary quadratic models.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Copositive Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact completely-positive and copositive formulation of standard quadratic optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(e=(1,\ldots,1)^\top\). For the standard quadratic problem on the simplex, \[p^\star=\min\{x^\top Qx:x\ge0,\ e^\top x=1\},\] one has the exact conic formulations \[p^\star=\min\{\langle Q,X\rangle:\langle ee^\top,X\rangle=1,\ X\in\mathcal{CP}_n\}=\max\{\lambda\in\mathbb R:Q-\lambda ee^\top\in\mathcal{COP}_n\}.\] Here \(\mathcal{CP}_n=\operatorname{cone}\{xx^\top:x\ge0\}\), and \(\mathcal{COP}_n=\{M:x^\top Mx\ge0\ \forall x\ge0\}\). The first equality is an exact lifting, and the second is its conic dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic minimization over the simplex equals a completely-positive conic program and its copositive dual.
assumptions_latex: The feasible region is the nonnegative simplex \(\{x\ge0:e^\top x=1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^\star=\min_{X\in\mathcal{CP}_n,\ \langle ee^\top,X\rangle=1}\langle Q,X\rangle=\max_{Q-\lambda ee^\top\in\mathcal{COP}_n}\lambda\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simplex quadratic problem, completely-positive lifting, and copositive dual are stated consistently and the duality content kind fits, but exactness and strong conic duality require authoritative support.

children.title: Completely Positive Primal Liftings
children.top_down_role: Primal matrix representations over the completely positive cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Completely Positive Primal Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact completely positive lifting for quadratic optimization over nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The completely positive cone is \(\mathcal{CP}^{m}=\operatorname{cone}\{vv^{\mathsf T}:v\in\mathbb R_+^m\}\). For a nonnegative feasible set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\), introduce \(Y=(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T}\) and replace each quadratic expression by a linear functional of \(Y\). A completely positive primal lifting has the form \[\inf\{\langle C,Y\rangle:\mathcal A(Y)=b,\ Y\in\mathcal{CP}^{n+1}\}.\] It is exact when its affine constraints satisfy \[\{Y\in\mathcal{CP}^{n+1}:\mathcal A(Y)=b\}=\operatorname{conv}\{(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T}:x\in S\}.\] Under this equality, every linear objective in \(Y\) has the same infimum as the original quadratic objective on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic problem over nonnegative variables is represented exactly when its lifted rank-one matrices have the stated completely positive convex hull.
assumptions_latex: The original objective and constraints are affine in \(Y=(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in S}\langle C,(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T}\rangle=\inf\{\langle C,Y\rangle:\mathcal A(Y)=b,\ Y\in\mathcal{CP}^{n+1}\}\).

notation.meaning: Cone of completely positive symmetric matrices of order m.
Linear map encoding the lifted constraints.
Lifted matrix representing constant, linear, and quadratic terms.

review_flags: Exact convex-hull formulation is standard but requires a directly supporting completely-positive-optimization source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and content kind fit the completely positive primal-lifting container, but no cited source supports the exact convex-hull characterization or its scope. The general optimization sources in the inventory do not provide an inspectable completely-positive-optimization locator.

children.title: Doubly Nonnegative Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Tractable semidefinite and entrywise-nonnegative outer approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Doubly Nonnegative Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer relaxation of completely positive primal matrix programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the doubly nonnegative cone by \[\mathcal{DNN}^{m}=\mathbb S_+^{m}\cap\mathbb R_+^{m\times m}.\] Every completely positive matrix is positive semidefinite and entrywise nonnegative, so \(\mathcal{CP}^{m}\subseteq\mathcal{DNN}^{m}\). Consequently, replacing \(Y\in\mathcal{CP}^{m}\) in a minimization problem by \(Y\in\mathcal{DNN}^{m}\) enlarges the feasible region. If \(v_{\mathrm{CP}}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{DNN}}\) denote the corresponding infima under identical affine constraints and objective, then \(v_{\mathrm{DNN}}\leq v_{\mathrm{CP}}\). The relaxed problem is a semidefinite program with additional entrywise linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The doubly nonnegative cone contains the completely positive cone, producing an SDP lower bound for completely positive minimization problems.
assumptions_latex: Both conic programs use the same linear objective and affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{CP}^{m}\subseteq\mathcal{DNN}^{m}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{DNN}}\leq v_{\mathrm{CP}}\).

notation.meaning: Cone of positive semidefinite symmetric matrices.
Cone of positive semidefinite, entrywise nonnegative matrices.
Completely positive and doubly nonnegative optimal values.

review_flags: A source explicitly covering the CP-to-DNN cone inclusion and relaxation bound is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cone inclusion, minimization-bound direction, and property classification are mathematically standard and match the DNN-relaxation container. A specific source for the CP-to-DNN inclusion and resulting SDP relaxation is absent.

children.title: Copositive-Cone Approximation Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Nested tractable cone families approaching copositive strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Copositive-Cone Approximation Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested inner approximations of the copositive cone and their dual primal relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal K_0\subseteq\mathcal K_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal{COP}^{m}\) be closed convex cones admitting tractable membership representations. Their dual cones satisfy \[\mathcal K_0^*\supseteq\mathcal K_1^*\supseteq\cdots\supseteq(\mathcal{COP}^{m})^*=\mathcal{CP}^{m}.\] Replacing a completely positive constraint by \(Y\in\mathcal K_r^*\) therefore gives successively stronger primal minimization relaxations, with bounds \(v_0\leq v_1\leq\cdots\leq v_{\mathrm{CP}}\). If \(\overline{\bigcup_{r\geq0}\mathcal K_r}=\mathcal{COP}^{m}\) and the conic value is stable under this approximation, then \(v_r\uparrow v_{\mathrm{CP}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested tractable inner approximations of the copositive cone yield nested outer approximations of the completely positive cone and monotonically improving bounds.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal K_r\) is a closed convex cone contained in \(\mathcal{COP}^{m}\).
All primal relaxations share the same affine constraints and linear minimization objective.
Value convergence requires the stated density and stability conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_0\leq v_1\leq\cdots\leq v_{\mathrm{CP}}\), with \(v_r\uparrow v_{\mathrm{CP}}\) under density and stability.

notation.meaning: Cone of matrices copositive on the nonnegative orthant.
Level-r tractable inner approximation of the copositive cone.
Dual outer approximation of the completely positive cone.

review_flags: The abstract hierarchy principle needs a source specifying sufficient value-convergence conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested-dual-cone principle fits the hierarchy container, but the phrase "value is stable under this approximation" is not a precise sufficient condition for convergence. A hierarchy source is required to determine and state the applicable regularity hypotheses without weakening the claim.

children.title: Doubly Nonnegative Finiteness Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where tractable copositive approximations fail to preserve finite quadratic bounds.

children.title: Finite Doubly Nonnegative Gaps
children.top_down_role: Instances with finite but nonzero separation from stronger copositive bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Doubly Nonnegative Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict but finite separation between exact and doubly nonnegative conic values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a common affine slice \(\mathcal F=\{Y:\mathcal A(Y)=b\}\) and objective matrix \(C\), define \[v_{\mathrm{CP}}=\inf\{\langle C,Y\rangle:Y\in\mathcal F\cap\mathcal{CP}^{m}\},\qquad v_{\mathrm{DNN}}=\inf\{\langle C,Y\rangle:Y\in\mathcal F\cap\mathcal{DNN}^{m}\}.\] A finite doubly nonnegative gap occurs precisely when both values are real and \[v_{\mathrm{DNN}}<v_{\mathrm{CP}}.\] The absolute gap is \(v_{\mathrm{CP}}-v_{\mathrm{DNN}}>0\); a relative gap may be reported only after specifying a nonzero normalization denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite DNN gap means that both conic optima are finite, but the DNN lower bound is strictly below the exact CP value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-\infty<v_{\mathrm{DNN}}<v_{\mathrm{CP}}<+\infty\).
review_flags: Terminology and normalization conventions require a directly supporting source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly distinguishes a strict finite DNN gap and fits the failure-regime leaf. No source or locator establishes the terminology and gap convention used here.

children.title: Unbounded Doubly Nonnegative Bounds
children.top_down_role: Instances where the tractable approximation fails to preserve a finite bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Doubly Nonnegative Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession-direction certificate for an unbounded DNN minimization relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(v_{\mathrm{DNN}}=\inf\{\langle C,Y\rangle:\mathcal A(Y)=b,\ Y\in\mathcal{DNN}^{m}\}\). Suppose a feasible matrix \(Y_0\) exists and there is a matrix \(D\) satisfying \[D\in\mathcal{DNN}^{m},\qquad \mathcal A(D)=0,\qquad \langle C,D\rangle<0.\] Then \(Y_0+tD\) is feasible for every \(t\geq0\), while its objective equals \(\langle C,Y_0\rangle+t\langle C,D\rangle\). Hence \(v_{\mathrm{DNN}}=-\infty\). The displayed \(D\) is a directly checkable certificate that the DNN relaxation supplies no finite lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DNN recession direction preserving all affine constraints and decreasing the objective certifies that the relaxed bound is minus infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{DNN}}=-\infty\).

notation.meaning: A feasible point of the DNN relaxation.
A feasible recession direction with negative objective slope.

review_flags: The recession certificate is standard conic analysis, but a directly supporting locator is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative-cost recession direction is a valid certificate and the content kind fits the unbounded-bound leaf. The record nevertheless has no inspectable conic-analysis source for the certificate.

children.title: Copositive Finiteness Separation
children.top_down_role: Regimes contrasting finite exact copositive representations with nonfinite approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Copositive Finiteness Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate that the exact CP value is finite while its DNN relaxation is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the CP minimization problem with constraints \(\mathcal A(Y)=b\). If it has a feasible point and there exists \(y\) such that \[C-\mathcal A^*(y)\in\mathcal{COP}^{m},\] then weak conic duality gives the finite lower bound \(\langle b,y\rangle\leq v_{\mathrm{CP}}\); the feasible point supplies a finite upper bound. If, simultaneously, the corresponding DNN relaxation has a direction \(D\in\mathcal{DNN}^{m}\) with \(\mathcal A(D)=0\) and \(\langle C,D\rangle<0\), then \[v_{\mathrm{DNN}}=-\infty<v_{\mathrm{CP}}<+\infty.\] Thus \((y,D)\), together with CP feasibility, certifies finiteness separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A copositive dual lower bound and a DNN negative recession direction certify a finite exact value but an unbounded relaxed value.
assumptions_latex: The CP primal has a feasible matrix with finite objective.
The CP and DNN formulations share \(C\), \(\mathcal A\), and \(b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{DNN}}=-\infty<v_{\mathrm{CP}}<+\infty\).

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the linear constraint map.

review_flags: A source explicitly treating CP-versus-DNN finiteness separation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The paired copositive dual-feasibility and DNN recession conditions have the correct certificate role and imply the stated finiteness separation under the supplied feasibility assumption. A directly supporting source and locator are missing.

children.title: Boolean Product-Polytope Geometry
children.top_down_role: Lifted polyhedral representations of pairwise binary products.

children.title: Boolean Quadric Polytope
children.top_down_role: The canonical lifted polytope for zero-one pairwise products.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Quadric Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete-graph lifting of all pairwise products of binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\geq1\), the Boolean quadric polytope is \[\operatorname{BQP}(n)=\operatorname{conv}\left\{(x,y)\in\{0,1\}^{n}\times\{0,1\}^{\binom n2}:y_{ij}=x_i x_j\ \text{for all }1\leq i<j\leq n\right\}.\] Its vertices encode a binary vector and every distinct pairwise product. Linear optimization over \(\operatorname{BQP}(n)\) therefore represents unconstrained binary quadratic optimization after placing diagonal quadratic terms into the linear coefficients using \(x_i^2=x_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Boolean quadric polytope is the convex hull of binary vectors lifted with every pairwise product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{BQP}(n)=\operatorname{conv}\{(x,(x_i x_j)_{i<j}):x\in\{0,1\}^{n}\}\).

notation.meaning: Lifted variable representing the product of binary coordinates i and j.
Boolean quadric polytope on n variables.

review_flags: A canonical polyhedral-combinatorics source and exact definition locator are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent and fits the Boolean quadric polytope container, including the treatment of diagonal binary terms. No canonical polyhedral source with a definition-level locator is cited.

children.title: Correlation Polytope
children.top_down_role: Moment-style representation of zero-one quadratic products.

knowledge_statements.title: Correlation Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-valued convex hull of binary second moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\geq1\), the correlation polytope is \[\operatorname{COR}(n)=\operatorname{conv}\{xx^{\mathsf T}:x\in\{0,1\}^{n}\}\subseteq\mathbb S^{n}.\] Every vertex \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(X_{ii}=x_i\) and \(X_{ij}=x_i x_j\). Hence the coordinate map \(X\mapsto((X_{ii})_{i=1}^{n},(X_{ij})_{i<j})\) is an affine bijection from \(\operatorname{COR}(n)\) onto \(\operatorname{BQP}(n)\), with inverse obtained by assembling the symmetric matrix from its diagonal and upper-triangular entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The correlation polytope is the convex hull of binary rank-one matrices and is affinely equivalent to the Boolean quadric polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{COR}(n)\cong_{\mathrm{aff}}\operatorname{BQP}(n)\).

notation.meaning: Space of real symmetric matrices of order n.

review_flags: The affine-equivalence statement needs a canonical source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The matrix convex-hull definition and affine equivalence with the stated BQP convention are mathematically consistent and fit the container. The definition and equivalence lack a specific authoritative source locator.

children.title: Cut-Polytope Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Affine and projection relationships between binary-product and cut representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Polytope Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine equivalence with cuts of the one-vertex suspension of a complete graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x,y)\) be a vertex of \(\operatorname{BQP}(n)\), and add a new vertex \(0\). Define edge coordinates on \(K_{n+1}\) by \[z_{0i}=x_i,\qquad z_{ij}=x_i+x_j-2y_{ij}\quad(1\leq i<j\leq n).\] Because \(y_{ij}=x_i x_j\), each \(z_{ij}\) equals \(1\) exactly when the corresponding binary labels differ; thus \(z\) is a cut vector. Extending affinely gives a bijection between \(\operatorname{BQP}(n)\) and \(\operatorname{CUT}(K_{n+1})\). Its inverse is \(x_i=z_{0i}\) and \(y_{ij}=(z_{0i}+z_{0j}-z_{ij})/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a root vertex transforms binary products into cut indicators, giving an explicit affine bijection between Boolean quadric and cut polytopes.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{CUT}(K_{n+1})\) is the convex hull of cut incidence vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{BQP}(n)\cong_{\mathrm{aff}}\operatorname{CUT}(K_{n+1})\).

notation.meaning: Complete graph on the root vertex and n original vertices.
Cut-incidence vector under the suspension transformation.
Cut polytope of the complete graph.

review_flags: The explicit suspension-map convention requires confirmation against a canonical source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The suspension transformation and its inverse are consistent with the stated cut-incidence convention, and representation is the correct content kind. A canonical source is required to confirm this exact coordinate convention.

children.title: Graph-Structured Boolean Quadric Polytope Family
children.top_down_role: Interaction-graph variants with specialized polyhedral structure.

children.title: Sparse Boolean Quadric Polytopes
children.top_down_role: Boolean product polytopes induced by sparse interaction graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Boolean Quadric Polytopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-indexed lifting containing products only on selected edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite simple graph \(G=(V,E)\), its sparse Boolean quadric polytope is \[\operatorname{BQP}(G)=\operatorname{conv}\left\{(x,y)\in\{0,1\}^{V}\times\{0,1\}^{E}:y_{ij}=x_i x_j\ \text{for every }ij\in E\right\}.\] It is the coordinate projection of the complete Boolean quadric polytope \(\operatorname{BQP}(|V|)\) onto the vertex coordinates and the product coordinates indexed by \(E\). Consequently, a binary quadratic objective whose interaction graph is contained in \(G\) becomes linear in \((x,y)\) over \(\operatorname{BQP}(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse Boolean quadric polytope retains only pairwise-product variables corresponding to edges of a specified graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{BQP}(G)=\operatorname{proj}_{V\cup E}(\operatorname{BQP}(|V|))\).

notation.meaning: Product coordinate attached to edge ij.

review_flags: A graph-structured Boolean quadric polytope source with this projection convention is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph-indexed convex-hull definition fits the sparse BQP leaf. Its identification as a projection of BQP(|V|) is standard after fixing a labeling of V, but no source establishes the naming and projection convention.

children.title: Bipartite Boolean Quadric Polytopes
children.top_down_role: Boolean product polytopes induced by bipartite interaction graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Bipartite Boolean Quadric Polytopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean product polytope indexed by the edges of a bipartite graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(U\mathbin{\dot\cup}W,E)\) be a finite bipartite graph. Its bipartite Boolean quadric polytope is \[\operatorname{BQP}_{\mathrm{bip}}(G)=\operatorname{conv}\left\{(u,w,y):u\in\{0,1\}^{U},\ w\in\{0,1\}^{W},\ y_{ij}=u_iw_j\ \text{for all }ij\in E\right\}.\] It is the graph-structured Boolean quadric polytope for \(G\), written with separate variable blocks for the two color classes. It linearizes bilinear binary objectives supported on \(E\), while omitting within-class product coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bipartite Boolean quadric polytope is the convex hull of two binary blocks and their products along bipartite edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{BQP}_{\mathrm{bip}}(G)=\operatorname{conv}\{(u,w,(u_iw_j)_{ij\in E}):u\in\{0,1\}^{U},\ w\in\{0,1\}^{W}\}\).

notation.meaning: The two color classes of the bipartite graph.
Bilinear product coordinate on edge ij.

review_flags: Naming conventions vary; a source fixing this bipartite formulation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bipartite product-polytope definition is precise and definition is the appropriate content kind. Because terminology and coordinate conventions vary, an authoritative source with an exact locator is required.

children.title: Graph-Topology Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral strength attributable to cycles, partitions, and interaction-graph topology.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Topology Strength Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary of edgewise product relaxations on acyclic interaction graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite simple graph \(G=(V,E)\), define the edgewise McCormick relaxation by \[0\leq x_i\leq1,\qquad \max\{0,x_i+x_j-1\}\leq y_{ij}\leq\min\{x_i,x_j\}\quad(ij\in E).\] If \(G\) is a forest, this polyhedron equals \(\operatorname{BQP}(G)\); equivalently, pairwise product constraints and variable bounds already describe the convex hull. When \(G\) contains cycles, the edgewise system need not be exact: globally inconsistent fractional edge marginals may satisfy every local McCormick inequality, and cycle-dependent valid inequalities can strengthen the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edgewise McCormick inequalities describe the sparse Boolean quadric polytope on forests, but cycles can create additional globally valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\text{ forest}\Longrightarrow \operatorname{Mc}(G)=\operatorname{BQP}(G)\), whereas cyclic graphs may satisfy \(\operatorname{BQP}(G)\subsetneq\operatorname{Mc}(G)\).

notation.meaning: Polyhedron defined by bounds and edgewise McCormick inequalities.
Sparse Boolean quadric polytope of G.

review_flags: Forest exactness and the precise cyclic failure boundary require verification from a graph-polytope source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property classification matches the graph-topology strength-regime leaf, and the forest-versus-cycle formulation is plausible. A graph-polytope source is required to verify forest exactness and the precise scope of cyclic strictness under this McCormick formulation.
