children.title: Fortet Product Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Classical linear strengthening for individual binary product variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Fortet Product Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear description of one lifted binary product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary variables \(x_i,x_j\) and a continuous lifted variable \(y_{ij}\), the Fortet system is \[0\le y_{ij},\qquad y_{ij}\le x_i,\qquad y_{ij}\le x_j,\qquad y_{ij}\ge x_i+x_j-1.\] Its feasible points satisfy \(y_{ij}=x_ix_j\). Moreover, after relaxing \(x_i,x_j\) to \([0,1]\), this system describes \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x_i,x_j,x_ix_j):x_i,x_j\in\{0,1\}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The four Fortet inequalities exactly linearize a product of two binary variables and give the convex hull when the binary variables are relaxed to the unit interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_{ij}=x_ix_j\), with the displayed relaxation equal to the pairwise product hull.

notation.meaning: lifted variable representing the product of variables i and j

children.title: Boolean McCormick Envelopes
children.top_down_role: McCormick envelope specialization for binary factor domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean McCormick Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: McCormick envelope specialized to two Boolean factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the box \(0\le x_i,x_j\le1\), the convex and concave envelopes of the bilinear term are encoded by \[y_{ij}\ge0,\qquad y_{ij}\ge x_i+x_j-1,\qquad y_{ij}\le x_i,\qquad y_{ij}\le x_j.\] Thus the polyhedron defined by these inequalities is exactly \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x_i,x_j,y_{ij}):x_i,x_j\in\{0,1\},\ y_{ij}=x_ix_j\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Boolean McCormick inequalities form the exact convex hull of the graph of a product of two binary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_i,x_j,y_{ij})\) lies in the convex hull of the Boolean product graph.

children.title: Pairwise Hull Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which baseline binary product descriptions yield the same local hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Hull Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence holds for isolated binary products, but not generally for jointly lifted quadratic models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For one pair \(\{i,j\}\), the Fortet and Boolean McCormick systems coincide and give the exact product hull. For a collection \(E\) of pairs, their intersection \(P_E\) remains exact when the interaction graph \((V,E)\) is a forest: \[P_E=\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y):x\in\{0,1\}^{V},\ y_{ij}=x_ix_j\text{ for }ij\in E\}.\] Graphs containing cycles need additional consistency inequalities in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise envelopes are exact on forest interaction graphs. Cycles can create fractional points requiring inequalities involving three or more variables.
assumptions_latex: \(P_E\) is the intersection of the pairwise Fortet systems
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((V,E)\text{ forest}\Rightarrow P_E=\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y):x\in\{0,1\}^{V},\ y_{ij}=x_ix_j\}\).

notation.meaning: intersection of pairwise binary-product hull formulations

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: local marginal consistency is globally realizable on a forest

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forest-exactness assertion is a nontrivial theorem and has no inspectable citation. A source must establish the precise joint-hull result, and P_E should be defined formally with its complete variable space and constraints.

children.title: Triangle Inequality Family
children.top_down_role: Three-variable consistency strengthening in product and cut spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Triangle Inequality Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-variable consistency inequalities in lifted product coordinates and their cut-metric image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), \(y_{ij}=x_ix_j\), and \(d_{ij}=x_i+x_j-2y_{ij}\). For every three distinct indices \(i,j,k\), valid triangle inequalities are \[d_{ij}\le d_{ik}+d_{jk},\qquad d_{ij}+d_{ik}+d_{jk}\le2,\] together with the first inequality under all permutations. Equivalently, the product coordinates satisfy \(y_{ij}+y_{ik}-y_{jk}\le x_i\) under all permutations and \(x_i+x_j+x_k-y_{ij}-y_{ik}-y_{jk}\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every binary assignment induces a cut semimetric whose three-coordinate restrictions obey three triangle inequalities and one perimeter inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed triangle and perimeter inequalities hold for every triple \(\{i,j,k\}\).

notation.meaning: cut coordinate induced by binary variables i and j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct affine conversion between Boolean-product and cut coordinates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The triangle, perimeter, and affine product-coordinate formulas are consistent, but this nontrivial inequality-family record lacks an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Graph-Cycle Inequality Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Graph-cycle strengthening beyond local product consistency.

children.title: Cycle Inequality Families
children.top_down_role: Valid inequalities derived from general cycles in binary interaction graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycle Inequality Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parity inequalities valid for cut vectors on arbitrary graph cycles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a simple cycle of a graph and let \(F\subseteq E(C)\) have odd cardinality. Every cut vector \(d\in\{0,1\}^{E}\) satisfies the cycle inequality \[\sum_{e\in F}d_e-\sum_{e\in E(C)\setminus F}d_e\le |F|-1.\] Consequently, imposing this family for all cycles and all odd subsets excludes edge patterns having inconsistent parity around a cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On every cycle, any odd chosen edge subset yields a parity inequality valid for all graph cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{e\in F}d_e-\sum_{e\in E(C)\setminus F}d_e\le |F|-1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cut intersections with a cycle have even parity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cycle inequality has the standard form, but no source with a specific locator supports the family or its parity interpretation.

children.title: Odd-Cycle Inequality Families
children.top_down_role: Parity-sensitive strengthening derived from odd cycles.

knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Cycle Inequality Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Odd-cycle upper bounds obtained from the cycle family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C\) is a simple cycle of odd length, selecting \(F=E(C)\) in the cycle family gives \[\sum_{e\in E(C)}d_e\le |E(C)|-1.\] The inequality is valid because a cut crosses every cycle an even number of times and therefore cannot contain all edges of an odd cycle. More generally, switching by a cut produces every odd-subset cycle inequality from this representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut cannot cross every edge of an odd cycle; its cycle incidence sum is therefore at most the cycle length minus one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{e\in E(C)}d_e\le |E(C)|-1\).

notation.meaning: edge set of the odd cycle

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: every cut meets a cycle in even cardinality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The odd-cycle specialization is mathematically plausible, but it lacks an inspectable source. The explanatory proof text beginning with the parity justification and switching claim must also be removed or converted to a sourced statement.

children.title: Cycle-Chord Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Strength variations associated with chordless cycles, added chords, and graph density.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycle-Chord Strength Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordless cycles supply the irreducible cycle inequalities for a fixed graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a simple cycle \(C\) has a chord \(f\), which splits it into cycles \(C_1\) and \(C_2\). For every odd set \(F\subseteq E(C)\), one can choose odd sets \(F_r\subseteq E(C_r)\) so that adding the two corresponding cycle inequalities cancels the coefficient of \(d_f\) and yields the inequality for \((C,F)\). Hence chorded-cycle inequalities are implied by inequalities on smaller cycles; chordless cycles are the irreducible regime for this family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chorded cycle inequality decomposes into inequalities for the two smaller cycles, while chordless cycles supply the nondecomposable cases.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a simple cycle with chord \(f\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The \((C,F)\) cycle inequality is implied by suitable cycle inequalities on \(C_1\) and \(C_2\).

notation.meaning: a chord splitting the original cycle
cycles formed by the chord and the two cycle paths

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: summing compatible subcycle inequalities eliminates the chord coordinate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The chord-decomposition and cancellation claim requires a source, and the term “irreducible” needs a precise scope distinguishing generation of the cycle family from facetness or global irredundancy.

children.title: Dense-Interaction Inequality Families
children.top_down_role: Higher-order combinatorial strengthening for dense interaction structures.

children.title: Clique Inequality Families
children.top_down_role: Higher-order strengthening associated with complete interaction subgraphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique Inequality Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-based valid inequalities over complete lifted interaction sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq V\), let \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), and set \(y_{ij}=x_ix_j\) for all pairs in \(S\). For every integer \(r\), the clique inequality \[r\sum_{i\in S}x_i-\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq S}y_{ij}\le \frac{r(r+1)}2\] is valid. Indeed, its value depends only on the selected cardinality \(k=\sum_{i\in S}x_i\), for which the inequality is equivalent to \((k-r)(k-r-1)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clique inequality couples all products inside a vertex set and follows from the integrality of the number of selected vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\sum_{i\in S}x_i-\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq S}y_{ij}\le r(r+1)/2\).

notation.meaning: vertex set inducing a complete lifted interaction set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inequality follows from nonnegativity of two consecutive integer factors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed clique inequality is algebraically correct, but the family lacks an authoritative citation. The sentence deriving it from consecutive integer factors is proof text and should not appear in the final knowledge statement.

children.title: Hypermetric Inequality Families
children.top_down_role: Metric-derived strengthening for Boolean quadratic and cut-related polytopes.

knowledge_statements.title: Hypermetric Inequality Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer-weighted dense valid inequalities for cut vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) be a cut vector on the complete graph with vertex set \(V\). For every integer vector \(b\in\mathbb Z^{V}\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in V}b_i=1\), the hypermetric inequality \[\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq V}b_i b_j d_{ij}\le0\] is valid. The family contains the triangle inequality by choosing three nonzero weights \((1,1,-1)\), up to relabeling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every integer weight vector summing to one defines a valid dense inequality for cut distances; triangle inequalities are a special case.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is a cut-incidence vector on a complete graph
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq V}b_i b_jd_{ij}\le0\).

notation.meaning: cut distance between vertices i and j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: evaluating the weighted form on either side of a cut gives a nonpositive integer product

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hypermetric inequality and triangle specialization are standard and internally consistent, but no inspectable source supports them.

children.title: Dense-Interaction Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where dense interaction structure increases the value of higher-order inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Interaction Strength Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise product envelopes need not enforce consistency across a dense interaction set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a three-vertex clique, the fractional point \(x_1=x_2=x_3=1/2\) and \(y_{12}=y_{13}=y_{23}=0\) satisfies every pairwise Fortet inequality. It violates the clique inequality with \(S=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(r=1\), since \[\sum_{i\in S}x_i-\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq S}y_{ij}=\frac32>1.\] Thus independently exact pairwise hulls do not yield the joint binary-product hull once dense cyclic interactions occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even on three vertices, all pairwise envelopes can hold while a clique inequality fails, demonstrating the gain from dense-interaction cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point lies in every pairwise product envelope but outside the joint binary-product hull.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: displayed coordinates directly verify the separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed three-vertex point is a valid counterexample to joint exactness of pairwise envelopes, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. Nevertheless, it lacks a citation, and the final claim should be scoped to the exhibited cyclic clique rather than suggesting failure for every dense cyclic interaction pattern.

children.title: Roof-Dual Persistency Theory
children.top_down_role: Classical graph-based lower bounds and partial-optimality structure for quadratic pseudo-Boolean minimization.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Discrete Applied Mathematics 123, quadratic optimization and persistency

children.title: Posiform-Cut Graph Representation Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Representations connecting quadratic pseudo-Boolean objectives to cut problems.

children.title: Posiform Representations
children.top_down_role: Posiform encodings of quadratic pseudo-Boolean objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Posiform Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative literal-monomial representation of quadratic pseudo-Boolean functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quadratic posiform is an expression \[\phi(x)=\kappa+\sum_t a_t\prod_{\ell\in L_t}\ell,\qquad a_t\ge0,\] where every literal \(\ell\) is either \(x_i\) or \(1-x_i\), every set \(L_t\) has at most two literals, and no product contains both literals of one variable. Every quadratic pseudo-Boolean function \(f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\mathbb R\) admits such a representation with \(f(x)=\phi(x)\) on \(\{0,1\}^{n}\), although the representation and constant \(\kappa\) need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every quadratic pseudo-Boolean function can be written as a constant plus nonnegative coefficients multiplying products of at most two Boolean literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\) and \(a_t\ge0\) such that \(f(x)=\kappa+\sum_ta_t\prod_{\ell\in L_t}\ell\) for every binary \(x\).

notation.meaning: a Boolean literal, either a variable or its complement
a consistent set of at most two literals

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Boolean complement identities permit coefficient sign changes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation definition fits the leaf, but universal existence of a nonnegative quadratic posiform for every quadratic pseudo-Boolean function is nontrivial and requires an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Cut-Graph Representations
children.top_down_role: Graph constructions connecting quadratic pseudo-Boolean objectives to cut problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Graph Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact source–sink cut representation for submodular quadratic pseudo-Boolean energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=c+\sum_i a_ix_i+\sum_{i<j}a_{ij}x_ix_j\) on \(\{0,1\}^{n}\). If \(a_{ij}\le0\) for every pair, then there exist a directed capacitated graph with terminals \(s,t\), nonnegative capacities, and a constant \(\kappa\) such that each assignment \(x\) determines an \(s\)-\(t\) cut \(S_x\) and \[f(x)=\kappa+\operatorname{cap}(\delta^+(S_x)).\] Consequently, minimizing \(f\) is equivalent to a minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cut. Conversely, direct pairwise cut representability implies submodularity of every binary pair term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic binary function is directly representable by a source–sink cut exactly in the pairwise-submodular regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n}}f(x)=\kappa+\min_{S:\,s\in S,\,t\notin S}\operatorname{cap}(\delta^+(S))\).

notation.meaning: source side of the cut encoding assignment x
arcs leaving the source side of the cut

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonpositive quadratic coefficients are precisely pairwise submodular terms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated sufficiency for nonpositive quadratic coefficients is standard, but the exact converse depends on what “direct pairwise cut representability” permits, particularly auxiliary vertices. An authoritative source and a precise representation model are required.

children.title: Representation Correspondence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between posiform encodings and their associated cut graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Correspondence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-capacity correspondence for nonnegative posiforms using literal nodes and fixed terminals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be a quadratic posiform: a nonnegative weighted sum of products of at most two Boolean literals, plus a constant. Construct a directed graph containing terminals \(s,t\) and complementary literal nodes, with terminal arcs representing unary terms and literal-to-literal arcs representing quadratic terms. Under the consistent-cut convention—exactly one of each complementary pair lies on the \(t\)-side—each arc crosses precisely when its associated literal product equals one. Hence there is a constant \(\kappa\) such that, for every consistent cut encoding \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), \[p(x)=\kappa+\operatorname{cap}(S,\bar S).\] Conversely, the capacity of any such literal cut graph expands into a quadratic posiform.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative unary and quadratic literal terms correspond to graph arcs, so consistent cut capacity equals the posiform up to a constant, and conversely.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a quadratic posiform with nonnegative term coefficients.
Cuts obey the complementary-literal consistency convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(x)=\kappa+\operatorname{cap}(S,\bar S)\) for every consistently encoded assignment, with a converse expansion from graphs to posiforms.

notation.meaning: terminal cut encoding a Boolean assignment

review_flags: Exact literal-graph construction requires a specialized roof-duality source.
standard_field_rationale: standard posiform and cut-capacity correspondence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The specialized literal-node construction and its converse require an inspectable roof-duality or posiform reference; the stated arc correspondence is too construction-dependent to validate from standard-field rationale alone.

children.title: Submodular Binary Quadratic Exactness
children.top_down_role: The graph-representable regime in which the cut formulation is exact.

knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Binary Quadratic Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact minimum-cut formulation for pairwise submodular Boolean minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=c+\sum_i a_i x_i+\sum_{i<j}a_{ij}x_ix_j\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\). Suppose every pairwise term is submodular, equivalently \[f_{ij}(0,0)+f_{ij}(1,1)\le f_{ij}(0,1)+f_{ij}(1,0),\] which for the displayed polynomial convention is \(a_{ij}\le0\). Then an \(s\)-\(t\) cut graph with nonnegative capacities can be constructed whose cut capacity equals \(f(x)-\kappa\) for the encoded assignment. Consequently, minimum cut returns a global minimizer of \(f\); the roof-dual relaxation has an integral optimum and its optimal value equals \(\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pairwise submodular Boolean quadratic function is exactly graph-representable; minimum cut solves it and the roof-dual bound has no gap.
assumptions_latex: Every pairwise term satisfies the Boolean submodularity inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimum-cut and roof-dual optimal values equal \(\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)\), and an integral relaxation optimum exists.

notation.meaning: constant offset in the cut representation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical graph-cut exactness of pairwise submodular Boolean energies.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is standard and appropriately placed, but its graph-representability, integrality, and roof-dual exactness claims require a specific authoritative locator.

children.title: Persistency Certificate Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Partial-assignment guarantees derived from roof-dual solutions.

children.title: Weak Persistency Certificates
children.top_down_role: Partial-assignment guarantees permitting compatibility with at least one optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Persistency Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential persistency certified by integral coordinates of an optimal roof-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\) be a binary quadratic objective and let \(y^*\in\{0,\tfrac12,1\}^n\) be an optimal half-integral roof-dual solution, accompanied by a verifiable certificate of relaxation optimality. Define \(L=\{i:y_i^*\in\{0,1\}\}\). Weak persistency asserts that there exists at least one global minimizer \(x^*\) of \(f\) satisfying \[x_i^*=y_i^*\qquad(i\in L).\] Thus the certified labels can be fixed simultaneously without eliminating all globally optimal Boolean solutions; the assertion does not require every global minimizer to carry those labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integral roof-dual labels are weakly persistent when some global Boolean minimizer agrees with all of them simultaneously.
assumptions_latex: \(y^*\) is an optimal half-integral roof-dual solution.
Relaxation optimality of \(y^*\) is independently certifiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)\) with \(x_i^*=y_i^*\) for every \(i\in L\).
review_flags: A roof-duality persistency theorem locator is required.
standard_field_rationale: standard existential formulation of weak persistency.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The existential formulation matches weak persistency, but a specialized source must confirm that the stated conclusion applies to the specified optimal roof-dual labeling.

children.title: Strong Persistency Certificates
children.top_down_role: Partial-assignment guarantees shared across the relevant optimum set.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Persistency Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal persistency of certified roof-dual labels across all global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a binary quadratic objective \(f\), a labeled set \(L\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and values \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\) form a strong persistency certificate when the certificate verifies \[x_i=\ell_i\qquad\text{for every }x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\{0,1\}^n}f(z)\text{ and every }i\in L.\] In roof-duality preprocessing, such a claim requires a strong-persistency criterion in addition to relaxation optimality; an integral coordinate of an arbitrary optimal half-integral roof-dual solution generally supplies only the weaker existential conclusion. Certified strongly persistent variables may therefore be fixed without removing any global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong certificate proves that every global minimizer shares each certified label, so fixing those variables preserves the entire optimal set.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\) is a binary quadratic objective.
The supplied criterion establishes universal, rather than merely existential, agreement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i=\ell_i\) holds for all global minimizers \(x\) and all certified coordinates \(i\in L\).
review_flags: The precise roof-duality criterion yielding strong persistency needs a specialized source.
standard_field_rationale: universal-agreement definition of strong persistency.

children.title: Unlabeled-Variable Boundary
children.top_down_role: Variables for which roof-dual information does not provide a persistency guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Unlabeled-Variable Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Half-integral coordinates alone provide no Boolean fixing conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^*\in\{0,\tfrac12,1\}^n\) be an optimal roof-dual solution. Persistency conclusions apply only to \(L=\{i:y_i^*\in\{0,1\}\}\); a coordinate with \(y_i^*=\tfrac12\) is unlabeled and cannot be fixed from this certificate alone. This limitation is genuine: for the constant objective \(f(x)=0\), a half-integral relaxation optimum may have \(y_i^*=\tfrac12\), while Boolean global minimizers exist with both \(x_i=0\) and \(x_i=1\). Consequently, neither Boolean value is implied for an unlabeled coordinate, even when the relaxation value is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A half-integral value of one-half certifies no Boolean label; both labels may occur among global minimizers even with zero relaxation gap.
assumptions_latex: \(y^*\) is an optimal half-integral roof-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(y_i^*=\tfrac12\), roof-dual optimality alone implies neither \(x_i=0\) nor \(x_i=1\) for global minimizers.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct constant-objective counterexample and standard half-integral labeling convention.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Roof-Duality Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Nonsubmodular structures that leave variables unresolved or bounds weak.

knowledge_statements.title: Roof-Duality Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes value gaps from unresolved labels in nonsubmodular Boolean quadratics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization of a binary quadratic function \(f\), let \(v_{\mathrm{RD}}\) be its roof-dual relaxation value and \(v_I=\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)\). Always \(v_{\mathrm{RD}}\le v_I\). Pairwise submodularity ensures equality and an integral relaxation optimum. Outside that regime, nonsubmodular interactions permit, but do not force, either a strict gap \(v_{\mathrm{RD}}<v_I\) or half-integral coordinates in an optimum. These phenomena are distinct: the constant objective admits half-integral optima while satisfying \(v_{\mathrm{RD}}=v_I\). Thus unresolved variables are not, by themselves, evidence of a positive value gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsubmodularity permits weak roof-dual bounds and half-integral labels, but unresolved labels can occur even when the relaxation value is exact.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a finite-valued binary quadratic minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{RD}}\le v_I\); submodularity gives equality, whereas nonsubmodularity allows distinct value-gap and unlabeled-variable regimes.
review_flags: A specialized source is needed for the general roof-dual gap characterization.
standard_field_rationale: relaxation ordering and constant-objective separation example.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxation ordering and counterexample are plausible, but the combined characterization of submodular exactness and nonsubmodular gap regimes requires a specialized roof-duality source.

children.title: Semidefinite Bounds for Binary Quadratic Programs
children.top_down_role: Correlation-matrix relaxations and their polyhedral strengthening for binary quadratic models.

children.title: Signed-Binary Correlation SDP
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite relaxation in the signed-binary representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Signed-Binary Correlation SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correlation-matrix relaxation of an unconstrained signed-binary quadratic problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the signed-binary problem \(\min\{s^{\mathsf T}Qs+2q^{\mathsf T}s:s\in\{-1,1\}^n\}\), introduce \(u=(1,s^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\) and replace \(uu^{\mathsf T}\) by \(Y\in\mathbb S^{n+1}\). The correlation SDP is \[\min\ \langle \widetilde Q,Y\rangle\quad\text{subject to}\quad Y\succeq0,\qquad Y_{kk}=1\quad(k=0,\ldots,n),\] where \(\widetilde Q=\begin{pmatrix}0&q^{\mathsf T}\\q&Q\end{pmatrix}\). Every signed vector gives the feasible rank-one matrix \(Y=uu^{\mathsf T}\); dropping \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\) therefore yields a lower bound for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift signed variables to a unit-diagonal positive semidefinite correlation matrix and drop rank one to obtain an SDP lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed correlation SDP is a relaxation and its minimum does not exceed the signed-binary optimum.
review_flags: The locator supports SDP form generally; signed-binary specialization should be checked.

children.title: Zero-One Binary SDP
children.top_down_role: Lifted semidefinite relaxation adapted to zero-one product moments.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-One Binary SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shor moment relaxation for unconstrained zero-one quadratic minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\langle Q,xx^{\mathsf T}\rangle:x\in\{0,1\}^n\}\), replace \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) by \(X\in\mathbb S^n\). The zero-one SDP is \[\min\ c^{\mathsf T}x+\langle Q,X\rangle\quad\text{subject to}\quad \begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad X_{ii}=x_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\] Every Boolean vector induces the feasible rank-one lift \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\). Conversely, imposing rank one recovers the Boolean formulation; omitting rank one produces a convex lower-bounding relaxation for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero-one Shor relaxation replaces binary products by a moment matrix, retains diagonal identities, and drops the rank-one constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SDP optimum is no greater than the zero-one quadratic minimum, with equality after restoring the rank-one constraint.
review_flags: The exact zero-one lifting specialization requires confirmation in the source.

children.title: SDP with Boolean Polyhedral Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite bounds augmented by product-polytope inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: SDP with Boolean Polyhedral Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection of the zero-one SDP with valid product-polytope inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Augment the zero-one SDP by valid inequalities for \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\), for example \[0\le X_{ij},\qquad X_{ij}\le x_i,\qquad X_{ij}\le x_j,\qquad X_{ij}\ge x_i+x_j-1\quad(i<j).\] Every Boolean rank-one lift satisfies these McCormick inequalities, so their addition preserves all feasible Boolean solutions. For minimization, if \(v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{str}}\) denote the basic and strengthened relaxation values and \(v_I\) the integer optimum, then \[v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le v_{\mathrm{str}}\le v_I.\] Additional valid Boolean-quadric or facet inequalities yield the same monotone strengthening relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting the SDP with valid Boolean product inequalities preserves integer solutions and can only improve its minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The base model uses \(X_{ij}\) as a relaxation of \(x_ix_j\).
Every added inequality is valid for all Boolean rank-one lifts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le v_{\mathrm{str}}\le v_I\) for minimization.
review_flags: Boolean-quadric strengthening needs a more specific source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strengthening and bound ordering are correct, but the generic SDP-programming locator does not specifically support the McCormick or Boolean-quadric inequalities claimed here.

children.title: Symmetry-Reduced Binary SDP
children.top_down_role: Block and association-scheme reductions for structured binary quadratic models.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Reduced Binary SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact block reduction of invariant binary SDPs by group averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act by permutation matrices \(P_g\) on a binary SDP, and suppose its objective and feasible set are invariant under \(Y\mapsto P_gYP_g^{\mathsf T}\). For any feasible \(Y\), the Reynolds average \[\bar Y=|G|^{-1}\sum_{g\in G}P_gYP_g^{\mathsf T}\] is feasible, has the same objective value, and commutes with every \(P_g\). Hence an optimum exists in the commutant algebra. An orthogonal change of basis simultaneously block-diagonalizes that algebra, replacing \(Y\succeq0\) by positive-semidefiniteness of its smaller blocks without changing the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a group-invariant binary SDP, averaging yields an equally good invariant solution whose commutant structure permits exact block diagonalization.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts orthogonally by permutations.
The SDP objective and feasible region are invariant under the group action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restricting to the commutant and block-diagonalizing it preserves the SDP optimal value.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex group averaging and simultaneous block diagonalization of the commutant.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The symmetry-averaging and commutant reduction claims are nontrivial and require a source addressing invariant SDPs and exact block diagonalization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gaussian Sign Rounding and the 2/π Binary-QP Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized rounding of a binary quadratic SDP relaxation when the objective matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(z^*=\max\{x^TQx:x_i\in\{-1,1\}\}\) with \(Q\succeq0\), and its SDP relaxation \(z^{\mathrm{SDP}}=\max\{Q\bullet X:X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1\}\). Let \(X^*=V^TV\) be an SDP optimum, draw \(\xi\sim N(0,I)\), and set \(\widehat x=\operatorname{sign}(V^T\xi)\). Then \(\widehat x_i\in\{-1,1\}\), \(\mathbb E[\widehat x_i\widehat x_j]=(2/\pi)\arcsin(X^*_{ij})\), and \(\mathbb E[\widehat x^TQ\widehat x]\ge(2/\pi)z^{\mathrm{SDP}}\ge(2/\pi)z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor an optimal binary-QP SDP matrix, multiply by a standard Gaussian vector, and round each coordinate by its sign. Pairwise rounded correlations equal 2/pi times the entrywise arcsine of the SDP matrix. For a positive-semidefinite objective matrix, the expected rounded objective is at least 2/pi times both the SDP bound and the binary optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[\widehat x^TQ\widehat x]\ge\frac{2}{\pi}z^{\mathrm{SDP}}\ge\frac{2}{\pi}z^*

children.title: SDP-versus-LP Dominance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Bound-order relationships between correlation SDP and product-linearization baselines.

knowledge_statements.title: SDP-versus-LP Dominance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound ordering determined by feasible-set containment after projection to common moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_S\) and \(F_L\) be nonempty compact convex feasible sets for an SDP relaxation and a product-linearization LP expressed in the same finite-dimensional lifted variables \((x,X)\), and suppose both contain every feasible integer lift. For the same linear minimization objective, \[F_S\subseteq F_L\Longrightarrow v_S\ge v_L,\qquad F_L\subseteq F_S\Longrightarrow v_L\ge v_S.\] If neither containment holds, there is no objective-independent dominance: one linear objective can satisfy \(v_S<v_L\), while another can satisfy \(v_L<v_S\). Their intersection satisfies \[\max\{v_S,v_L\}\le v_{F_S\cap F_L}\le v_I,\] where \(v_I\) is the integer optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For compact convex SDP and LP relaxations in common lifted coordinates, containment reverses the ordering of minimization bounds. Without containment, either relaxation can be stronger for different linear objectives, while their intersection dominates both and remains a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F_S\) and \(F_L\) are nonempty compact convex subsets of a common finite-dimensional lifted space.
Both relaxations contain every feasible integer lift.
All comparisons use the same linear minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Containment reverses the ordering of relaxation minima; without containment no objective-independent dominance holds, and \(\max\{v_S,v_L\}\le v_{F_S\cap F_L}\le v_I\).

notation.meaning: SDP and LP feasible sets in common lifted coordinates

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-dimensional convex separation and elementary feasible-set containment ordering for minimization.

children.title: Random Hyperplane Rounding
children.top_down_role: Geometric randomized recovery from correlation-matrix solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Random Hyperplane Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Goemans–Williamson rounding of a feasible correlation matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a feasible correlation matrix \(Y\succeq0\) with \(Y_{ii}=1\). Compute unit vectors \(v_i\) satisfying \(Y_{ij}=v_i^{\mathsf T}v_j\). Draw \(g\) from a rotationally invariant Gaussian distribution in their ambient space and set \[s_i=\operatorname{sign}(g^{\mathsf T}v_i)\in\{-1,1\}.\] Return the cut whose sides are determined by the signs. For each pair, \[\Pr(s_i\ne s_j)=\frac{\arccos(Y_{ij})}{\pi}.\] With \(K\) independent trials, output the best sampled cut according to the original objective; ties and the probability-zero event \(g^{\mathsf T}v_i=0\) may be resolved arbitrarily.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the correlation matrix into unit vectors, cut them with a random through-origin hyperplane, and optionally retain the best of repeated samples.
assumptions_latex: The random vector \(g\) has a rotationally invariant continuous distribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a signed cut with pairwise separation probability \(\arccos(Y_{ij})/\pi\).
review_flags: The original Goemans–Williamson algorithm and separation-probability locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and separation-probability formula are standard and correctly stated, but this nontrivial randomized-rounding claim requires a specific Goemans–Williamson or equivalent authoritative locator.

children.title: Max-Cut Approximation Guarantee Family
children.top_down_role: Performance guarantees associated with the canonical SDP relaxation and rounding family.

knowledge_statements.title: Max-Cut Approximation Guarantee Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Goemans–Williamson guarantee for nonnegative weighted Max-Cut using random-hyperplane rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected graph with weights \(w_{ij}\ge 0\), and let unit vectors \(v_i\) attain the optimal value \(U=\sum_{ij\in E}w_{ij}(1-\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)/2\) of the standard Max-Cut SDP. A uniformly random hyperplane produces signs \(x_i\in\{-1,1\}\) satisfying
\[\mathbb E[\operatorname{cut}(x)]=\sum_{ij\in E}w_{ij}\frac{\arccos(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)}{\pi}\ge \alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}U\ge \alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{OPT},\]
where \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}=\min_{0<\theta\le\pi}\frac{2\theta}{\pi(1-\cos\theta)}\approx0.87856\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random-hyperplane rounding of an optimal standard SDP solution returns a cut whose expected weight is at least 0.87856 times both the SDP value and the optimal cut value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{cut}(x)]\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}U\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{OPT}\).

notation.meaning: optimal value of the standard Max-Cut SDP relaxation

children.title: Max-Cut Integrality-Gap Family
children.top_down_role: Worst-case separation between the SDP bound and attainable cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Max-Cut Integrality-Gap Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case multiplicative gap of the basic Max-Cut SDP for nonnegative weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonnegative weighted graph \(G\) with \(\operatorname{OPT}(G)>0\), define its basic-SDP gap by \(\gamma(G)=\operatorname{SDP}(G)/\operatorname{OPT}(G)\). The Goemans–Williamson inequality gives \(1\le\gamma(G)\le1/\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\). Moreover, there are finite weighted graphs \((G_m)_{m\ge1}\) for which \(\operatorname{OPT}(G_m)/\operatorname{SDP}(G_m)\to\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\); hence the universal bound is asymptotically tight and \(\sup_G\gamma(G)=1/\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The basic Max-Cut SDP overestimates the optimum by at most 1 divided by the Goemans–Williamson constant, and known graph families approach this worst-case ratio.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_G\operatorname{SDP}(G)/\operatorname{OPT}(G)=1/\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\).

notation.meaning: multiplicative integrality gap of the basic SDP on graph G

review_flags: Exact primary-source locator for the asymptotically tight integrality-gap construction is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The upper gap bound follows from the approximation guarantee, but the asserted asymptotically tight graph family and exact supremum require a specific primary-source theorem or construction locator.

children.title: Weighted Max-Cut Variants
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite bound and rounding behavior under nonuniform edge weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Max-Cut Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative weighted Max-Cut and its standard semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with weights \(w_{ij}\ge0\), weighted Max-Cut is
\[\max_{x\in\{-1,1\}^{V}}\frac12\sum_{ij\in E}w_{ij}(1-x_ix_j).\]
Its standard semidefinite relaxation replaces each product \(x_ix_j\) by \(X_{ij}\) and imposes
\[X\succeq0,\qquad X_{ii}=1\quad(i\in V).\]
Equivalently, \(X_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\) for unit vectors \(v_i\). The relaxation value is an upper bound on the maximum weighted cut because every sign vector induces \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted Max-Cut maximizes the total nonnegative weight crossing a bipartition; its standard SDP replaces sign products by inner products of unit vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SDP}(G,w)\ge\operatorname{OPT}(G,w)\).

notation.meaning: sign indicating the side containing vertex i
semidefinite lift of the sign-product matrix

children.title: Cardinality-Constrained Cut Variants
children.top_down_role: Cut models subject to partition-size or balance restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality-Constrained Cut Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted cuts whose designated side has prescribed cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(G=(V,E)\), weights \(w_{ij}\), and \(k\in\{0,\ldots,|V|\}\), cardinality-constrained Max-Cut maximizes
\[\frac12\sum_{ij\in E}w_{ij}(1-x_ix_j)\]
over \(x\in\{-1,1\}^{V}\) subject to \(\sum_{i\in V}(1+x_i)/2=k\), equivalently \(\sum_i x_i=2k-|V|\). In a lifted relaxation with \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), the valid equality \(\langle\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T},X\rangle=(2k-|V|)^2\) can strengthen the linear cardinality equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This variant seeks a maximum-weight cut while requiring one side to contain exactly k vertices; lifted cardinality equalities strengthen its SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i x_i=2k-|V|\) and \(\langle\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T},xx^{\mathsf T}\rangle=(2k-|V|)^2\).

notation.meaning: required cardinality of the positive-sign side

children.title: Side-Constrained Cut Variants

knowledge_statements.title: Side-Constrained Cut Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Max-Cut augmented by linear restrictions on the selected bipartition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) have weights \(w_{ij}\), and encode a bipartition by \(x\in\{-1,1\}^{V}\). A linearly side-constrained cut problem is
\[\max\left\{\frac12\sum_{ij\in E}w_{ij}(1-x_ix_j):Dx\le d,\ Ex=e,\ x\in\{-1,1\}^{V}\right\}.\]
The matrices \(D,E\) and vectors \(d,e\) may encode budgets, membership restrictions, partition balance, or assignment requirements. A valid relaxation must contain every lifted matrix \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) generated by a feasible sign vector, though it may also contain fractional lifted points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A side-constrained cut maximizes crossing weight subject to additional linear inequalities or equalities governing which vertices may occupy each side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{xx^{\mathsf T}:x\in\{-1,1\}^{V},\ Dx\le d,\ Ex=e\}\) is contained in every valid lifted relaxation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: This is the canonical finite-dimensional definition of a linearly constrained binary quadratic cut problem.

children.title: Constraint-Sensitive Rounding Regimes
children.top_down_role: Feasibility and quality behavior of rounding under added cut constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Sensitive Rounding Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and performance must be analyzed jointly when rounding constrained cut relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widehat x\) be a randomized rounding of a relaxation point, let \(F=\{D\widehat x\le d,\ E\widehat x=e\}\), and let \(W(\widehat x)\) denote its cut weight. If \(\mathbb P(F)>0\), rejection or conditional rounding outputs a feasible cut with expected value
\[\mathbb E[W(\widehat x)\mid F]=\frac{\mathbb E[W(\widehat x)\mathbf1_F]}{\mathbb P(F)}.\]
Consequently, an unconstrained expectation guarantee for \(W(\widehat x)\) alone does not imply a constrained approximation guarantee; one must control both feasible probability and objective loss under conditioning or repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For constrained cuts, an objective guarantee is insufficient: rounding must also preserve feasibility with controlled probability and retain value after conditioning or repair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[W(\widehat x)\mid F]=\mathbb E[W(\widehat x)\mathbf1_F]/\mathbb P(F)\).

notation.meaning: event that the rounded signs satisfy every side constraint

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The displayed identity is conditional expectation; its consequence identifies the feasibility condition required by constrained rounding.

children.title: General BQP Rounding Families

knowledge_statements.title: General BQP Rounding Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian sign rounding for a homogenized semidefinite relaxation of a binary quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a feasible SDP matrix \(Y\succeq0\) with \(Y_{ii}=1\) for indices \(i=0,\ldots,n\), a trial limit \(N\ge1\), and optional feasibility constraints. Factor \(Y_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\). For trials \(r=1,\ldots,N\), draw \(g_r\sim N(0,I)\) and set
\[\widehat x_i^{(r)}=\operatorname{sign}(\langle v_i,g_r\rangle)\operatorname{sign}(\langle v_0,g_r\rangle),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\]
Return the best feasible sampled vector; if no side constraints are present, return the best sample. If no feasible sample occurs, report rounding failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the SDP matrix, sample Gaussian hyperplanes, orient every sign relative to the homogenizing vector, and return the best feasible sampled binary solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x^{(r)}\in\{-1,1\}^{n}\) for every trial \(r\).

notation.meaning: standard Gaussian direction in trial r

children.title: General BQP Approximation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Objective-quality regimes for rounded semidefinite solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: General BQP Approximation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Choice between multiplicative and additive guarantees for general binary quadratic objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) on a feasible set \(F\subseteq\{-1,1\}^{n}\), and suppose the problem maximizes \(f\). A multiplicative \(\rho\)-approximation requires \(f(\widehat x)\ge\rho\operatorname{OPT}\) and is informative under a fixed normalization with \(\operatorname{OPT}>0\). Without such normalization, additive guarantees \(f(\widehat x)\ge\operatorname{OPT}-\varepsilon\) or range-relative guarantees are appropriate: replacing \(f\) by \(f+C\) preserves all optimizers but can change an arbitrary multiplicative ratio. Thus general BQP approximation regimes must specify sign and normalization conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplicative BQP ratios require a positive, fixed objective normalization; otherwise constant shifts alter the ratio without changing solutions, so additive or range-relative guarantees are preferable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\arg\max_{x\in F}f(x)=\arg\max_{x\in F}(f(x)+C)\), while multiplicative ratios generally change with \(C\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Objective translation preserves argmax sets but not ordinary multiplicative approximation ratios.

children.title: General BQP Integrality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Instance families exhibiting separation between semidefinite bounds and binary optima.

knowledge_statements.title: General BQP Integrality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance-wise and family-wise gaps for maximization relaxations of binary quadratic programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization BQP instance \(I\), let \(U_R(I)\) be the value of a valid relaxation \(R\) and let \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)\) be the binary optimum. When \(0<\operatorname{OPT}(I)\le U_R(I)<\infty\), the multiplicative integrality gap is \(\gamma_R(I)=U_R(I)/\operatorname{OPT}(I)\), and the gap over a family \(\mathcal I\) is \(\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\gamma_R(I)\). If positivity fails, the additive gap \(U_R(I)-\operatorname{OPT}(I)\), together with an explicit objective normalization, avoids undefined or sign-reversing ratios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A BQP relaxation gap is the relaxed upper bound divided by the positive integer optimum; when positivity fails, a normalized additive gap should be used.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is a valid relaxation for a maximization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_R(\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}U_R(I)/\operatorname{OPT}(I)\).

notation.meaning: relaxation upper bound for instance I

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: This is the standard maximization convention for multiplicative and additive relaxation gaps.

children.title: Rounding Feasibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Constraint structures that obstruct direct feasibility preservation during rounding.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Feasibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-feasible cardinality constraints need not survive independent hyperplane sign rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two binary variables constrained by \(x_1+x_2=0\). In a homogenized SDP, choose mutually orthogonal unit vectors \(v_0\) and \(u\), and set \(v_1=v_2=u\). The first-moment equality \(\langle v_0,v_1\rangle+\langle v_0,v_2\rangle=0\) holds. Nevertheless, Gaussian hyperplane rounding oriented by \(v_0\) gives \(\widehat x_1=\widehat x_2\) almost surely, so \(\widehat x_1+\widehat x_2\in\{-2,2\}\) and feasibility has probability zero. Linear moment feasibility alone therefore cannot guarantee exact side-constraint feasibility after rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-variable SDP point can satisfy a cardinality constraint in first moments while hyperplane rounding violates that constraint with probability one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\widehat x_1+\widehat x_2=0)=0\).

notation.meaning: common vector assigned to both binary variables

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The counterexample follows directly from identical rounded signs and orthogonality to the homogenizing vector.

children.title: Constraint-Sensitive BQP Bound Strength
children.top_down_role: Changes in relaxation power caused by cardinality, knapsack, assignment, and partition structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Sensitive BQP Bound Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strengthening of maximization bounds by valid constraint-derived inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be the set of lifted matrices of feasible binary solutions, and let \(S\subseteq R_2\subseteq R_1\) be two relaxation regions. For a common linear lifted objective \(L(Y)\), suppose the three relevant suprema are finite and define \(\operatorname{OPT}=\sup\{L(Y):Y\in S\}\) and \(U_j=\sup\{L(Y):Y\in R_j\}\). Then
\[\operatorname{OPT}\le U_2\le U_1.\]
Thus adding valid cardinality, knapsack, assignment, or partition inequalities cannot weaken a maximization upper bound. Strict improvement occurs only when the strengthened relaxation has \(U_2<U_1\); the type of the added constraint alone does not guarantee strict improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid constraint-derived inequalities can only lower or preserve a maximization relaxation bound; strict strengthening depends on the resulting relaxation values and is not guaranteed by the constraint type alone.
assumptions_latex: The linear lifted objective \(L\) is identical on all three regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}\le U_2\le U_1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Maximization over nested feasible regions gives the displayed bound ordering.

children.title: Perspective Relaxation Principle

children.title: Separable Quadratic Perspectives
children.top_down_role: Termwise perspective convexification for separable quadratic epigraphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Quadratic Perspectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed perspective convexification of separable on/off quadratic epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(a_i>0\), define the unrestricted on/off quadratic epigraph
\[S_i=\{(0,0,t_i):t_i\ge0\}\cup\{(x_i,1,t_i):x_i\in\mathbb R,\ t_i\ge a_i x_i^2\}.\]
Its closed convex hull is
\[\operatorname{clconv}(S_i)=\{(x_i,z_i,t_i):0\le z_i\le1,\ t_i\ge0,\ t_i z_i\ge a_i x_i^2\}.\]
At \(z_i=0\), the inequality forces \(x_i=0\); for \(z_i>0\), it is equivalent to \(t_i\ge a_i x_i^2/z_i\). For separable terms, auxiliary epigraph variables combine through \(t\ge\sum_i t_i\), and each quadratic perspective inequality has a rotated second-order-cone representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed convex hull of each unrestricted on/off convex quadratic epigraph is given by its closed perspective inequality, which is representable by a rotated second-order cone; separable term epigraphs combine by summation.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\mathbb R\) is unrestricted apart from the on/off condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}(S_i)=\{(x_i,z_i,t_i):0\le z_i\le1,\ t_i\ge0,\ t_i z_i\ge a_i x_i^2\}\).

notation.meaning: epigraph variable for the perspective term
binary on/off quadratic epigraph defined in the statement

review_flags: A precise authoritative theorem locator for the closed convex-hull representation is required.

children.title: Closed-Perspective Boundary Regime
children.top_down_role: Closure behavior at zero activation and its modeling consequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Perspective Boundary Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed extension of a positive-semidefinite quadratic perspective at zero activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succeq0\) and \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx\). Its closed perspective is \[f^{\pi}(x,z)=\begin{cases}x^{\mathsf T}Qx/z,&z>0,\\0,&z=0\text{ and }x\in\ker Q,\\+\infty,&z=0\text{ and }x\notin\ker Q,\\+\infty,&z<0.\end{cases}\] Consequently, the closed epigraph is \(\{(x,z,t):z\ge0,\ t\ge0,\ x^{\mathsf T}Qx\le tz\}\). If the on–off model additionally imposes \(x=0\) when \(z=0\), the kernel-valued boundary is reduced to the inactive point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero activation, the closed quadratic perspective is finite exactly on the nullspace of the quadratic form; explicit support constraints may reduce this boundary to the origin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\{(x,z,t):z\ge0,\ t\ge0,\ x^{\mathsf T}Qx\le tz\}\).

notation.meaning: closed perspective of the quadratic function

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard lower-semicontinuous closure of a quadratic perspective

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, boundary behavior, epigraph, and content kind are mathematically consistent, but no inspectable source is supplied for the closed-perspective claim.

children.title: Conic Perspective Representations
children.top_down_role: Conic representations of activated convex quadratic epigraphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Perspective Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated second-order-cone representation of an activated convex quadratic epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\succeq0\). For \(z,t\ge0\), the closed perspective inequality \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\le tz\) is equivalent to \[\left\|(2Rx,\ t-z)\right\|_2\le t+z.\] Equivalently, it is the rotated-cone constraint \((t/2,z,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r\), where \(\mathcal Q_r=\{(a,b,y):a\ge0,\ b\ge0,\ 2ab\ge\|y\|_2^2\}\). This representation includes the closed boundary at \(z=0\), where it forces \(Rx=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic perspective epigraph is exactly representable by one rotated second-order-cone constraint, including its zero-activation boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\le tz\iff\|(2Rx,t-z)\|_2\le t+z\).

children.title: Perspective-Cut Approximations
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral outer approximations of perspective-strengthened epigraphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective-Cut Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-halfspace approximation of a closed quadratic perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\). For every \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), the inequality \[t\ge 2a^{\mathsf T}Qx-(a^{\mathsf T}Qa)z\] is valid for the closed perspective epigraph. For \(z>0\), \[\frac{x^{\mathsf T}Qx}{z}=\sup_{a\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{2a^{\mathsf T}Qx-(a^{\mathsf T}Qa)z\right\}.\] Consequently, \[\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\left\{(x,z,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R:z\ge0,\ t\ge2a^{\mathsf T}Qx-(a^{\mathsf T}Qa)z\ \text{for every }a\in\mathbb R^n\right\}.\] Requiring these inequalities only for a finite set \(A\subset\mathbb R^n\) gives a polyhedral outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All tangent inequalities, together with nonnegative activation, exactly describe the closed quadratic perspective epigraph; any finite subset gives a polyhedral outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\{(x,z,t):z\ge0,\ t\ge2a^{\mathsf T}Qx-(a^{\mathsf T}Qa)z\ \text{for every }a\in\mathbb R^n\}\).

notation.meaning: reference vector indexing a supporting cut
closed perspective of the quadratic function

children.title: Nonseparable Indicator-Quadratic Convexification

children.title: Rank-One Indicator Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convex-hull families for rank-one quadratic components under support restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Indicator Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact perspective hull for one rank-one quadratic component controlled by a common indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(a\in\mathbb R^n\). Consider the on–off epigraph \(S=\{(x,z,t):z\in\{0,1\},\ z=0\Rightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x=0,\ t\ge(a^{\mathsf T}x)^2\}\). Its closed convex hull is \[\operatorname{clconv}S=\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge0,\ (a^{\mathsf T}x)^2\le tz\}.\] If support restrictions separately force every coordinate used by \(a\) to vanish when inactive, those restrictions must be retained in addition to the displayed rank-one hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-one quadratic controlled by one indicator has an exact rotated-cone hull obtained by perspectivizing the scalar projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}S=\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge0,\ (a^{\mathsf T}x)^2\le tz\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scalar perspective convexification of a two-term on–off disjunction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-one closed-hull representation is internally consistent and fits the representation container, but the exact convex-hull claim lacks an inspectable specialized source.

children.title: Bivariate Interaction Convexification Family
children.top_down_role: Bivariate convex-hull blocks for coupled quadratic interactions.

children.title: Pairwise Interaction Hulls
children.top_down_role: Bivariate convexification blocks for individual coupled quadratic interactions.

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Interaction Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activation-pattern disaggregation for an exact two-variable convex quadratic epigraph hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_{ij}\in\mathbb S_+^2\), and define \(S_{ij}\) as the set of \((u,z,t)\in\mathbb R^2\times\{0,1\}^2\times\mathbb R\) satisfying \(u_k=0\) whenever \(z_k=0\) and \(t\ge u^{\mathsf T}Q_{ij}u\). Its closed convex hull is the projection of variables \(\lambda_s\in\mathbb R_+\), \(u^s\in\mathbb R^2\), and \(t_s\in\mathbb R_+\), indexed by \(s\in\{0,1\}^2\), satisfying \[\sum_s\lambda_s=1,\qquad z=\sum_s\lambda_ss,\qquad u=\sum_su^s,\qquad t\ge\sum_st_s,\] \[u_k^s=0\ \text{if }s_k=0,\qquad (u^s)^{\mathsf T}Q_{ij}u^s\le t_s\lambda_s\quad\text{for every }s\in\{0,1\}^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact pairwise hull is obtained by disaggregating variables over the four activation patterns and imposing one closed nonnegative quadratic perspective epigraph for each pattern.
assumptions_latex: No restrictions beyond the stated support implications are imposed on \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}S_{ij}\) is the projection of the displayed four-pattern perspective system with \(t_s\ge0\) for every \(s\).

notation.meaning: one of the four pairwise activation patterns
continuous variables disaggregated for pattern s

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: perspective disaggregation of a finite convex disjunction

children.title: Two-by-Two Matrix Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convexification based on small principal matrix blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-by-Two Matrix Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite disaggregation of a two-variable lifted moment hull by activation pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(s\in\{0,1\}^2\), introduce \(\lambda_s\ge0\), \(u^s\in\mathbb R^2\), and \(X^s\in\mathbb S^2\). The closed convexification of lifted points satisfying \(X=uu^{\mathsf T}\) and pairwise support pattern \(s\) is represented by \[\sum_s\lambda_s=1,\quad z=\sum_s\lambda_ss,\quad u=\sum_su^s,\quad X=\sum_sX^s,\] \[u_k^s=0\text{ and }X_{k\ell}^s=0\text{ if }s_k=0,\qquad \begin{pmatrix}\lambda_s&(u^s)^{\mathsf T}\\u^s&X^s\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] A quadratic epigraph is added linearly as \(t\ge Q_{ij}\mathbin{\bullet}X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-variable lifted quadratic hull can be represented by four activation-pattern moment matrices and positive-semidefinite perspective constraints.
assumptions_latex: The lifted variables correspond to one pair of coordinates.
\(Q_{ij}\in\mathbb S_+^2\) for the optional epigraph constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge Q_{ij}\mathbin{\bullet}X\) over the disaggregated moment system yields the pairwise quadratic convexification.

notation.meaning: binary activation pattern for the coordinate pair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The moment-matrix formulation is plausible and fits the representation container, but the cited generic LMI section does not establish the specialized exact disjunctive matrix-hull claim.

children.title: Overlapping-Pair Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility across pairwise blocks sharing variables or lifted products.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping-Pair Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal agreement conditions for pairwise activation-pattern convexifications sharing coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every modeled pair \(\{i,j\}\), let \(\lambda_{ij}^{ab}\ge0\) denote the weight of activation pattern \((a,b)\in\{0,1\}^2\), with \(\sum_{a,b}\lambda_{ij}^{ab}=1\). The pair models are singleton-consistent in activation if variables \(\mu_i^a\ge0\) exist such that \[\sum_{b=0}^1\lambda_{ij}^{ab}=\mu_i^a\quad\text{for every pair }\{i,j\}\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\},\qquad \mu_i^0+\mu_i^1=1.\] If \(m_{ij,i}^{ab}\) is the pattern-specific first moment of coordinate \(i\) in pair \(\{i,j\}\), first-moment consistency requires shared variables \(\nu_i^a\) satisfying \[\sum_{b=0}^1m_{ij,i}^{ab}=\nu_i^a\quad\text{for every pair }\{i,j\}\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}.\] The activation-marginal equations are necessary on every interaction graph. If that graph is a forest, the locally consistent pairwise activation weights \(\lambda_{ij}^{ab}\) extend to a joint distribution on all binary indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping pair models must agree on shared singleton activation marginals and first moments. On a forest, consistent pairwise activation probabilities extend to a global binary activation distribution.
assumptions_latex: The global-extension conclusion applies to activation weights and assumes that the pair-interaction graph is a forest.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_b\lambda_{ij}^{ab}=\mu_i^a\) and \(\sum_bm_{ij,i}^{ab}=\nu_i^a\) for every pair incident to \(i\); on a forest, the activation marginals extend to a joint binary distribution.

notation.meaning: weight of activation pattern (a,b) for pair {i,j}
pattern-specific first moment of coordinate i in pair {i,j}
shared singleton first moment for activation state a

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: local marginal consistency and tree-structured extension

children.title: Matrix-Perspective Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Matrix-valued perspective structure for nonseparable convex quadratics.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Perspective Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed matrix-fractional perspective represented by a positive-semidefinite block matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Z\in\mathbb S_+^n\), define the closed matrix-fractional function by \(\phi(x,Z)=x^{\mathsf T}Z^{\dagger}x\) when \(x\in\operatorname{range}Z\), and \(\phi(x,Z)=+\infty\) otherwise. Its epigraph has the semidefinite representation \[t\ge\phi(x,Z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{pmatrix}t&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&Z\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] Choosing \(Z\) as an affine matrix function of relaxed indicator variables produces a matrix-perspective relaxation that preserves coupled, nonseparable quadratic structure rather than perspectivizing scalar terms independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed matrix-fractional perspective equals a block positive-semidefinite constraint and can retain coupling among variables controlled by several indicators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}\phi=\{(x,Z,t):\begin{pmatrix}t&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&Z\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\}\).

children.title: Combinatorially Constrained Indicator Sets
children.top_down_role: Indicator convexification under cardinality, hierarchy, and related support constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorially Constrained Indicator Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact support-pattern disaggregation for indicators restricted to a finite combinatorial family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be a finite family of feasible support patterns, and let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\). Consider the epigraph with \(z\in\mathcal Z\), \(x_i=0\) whenever \(z_i=0\), and \(t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx\). Its closed convex hull is the projection of variables \(\lambda_s\in\mathbb R_+\), \(x^s\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(t_s\in\mathbb R_+\), indexed by \(s\in\mathcal Z\), satisfying \[\sum_s\lambda_s=1,\qquad z=\sum_s\lambda_ss,\qquad x=\sum_sx^s,\qquad t\ge\sum_st_s,\] \[x_i^s=0\ \text{if }s_i=0,\qquad (x^s)^{\mathsf T}Qx^s\le t_s\lambda_s\quad\text{for every }s\in\mathcal Z.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerating feasible supports and imposing one closed nonnegative quadratic perspective epigraph per support gives an exact, potentially exponential, extended formulation of the constrained-indicator hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection of the support-disaggregated system with \(t_s\ge0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal Z\) equals the closed convex hull of the constrained-indicator quadratic epigraph.

notation.meaning: family of feasible binary support patterns
weight assigned to feasible support s
continuous vector disaggregated for support s

children.title: Termwise-Perspective Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where separable perspectives omit coupled convex-hull structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Termwise-Perspective Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete gap caused by perspectivizing only separable terms of a coupled quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<\rho<1\), \(Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}\), and let one binary indicator \(z\) force \(x=0\) when \(z=0\). Decompose \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx=(1-\rho)(x_1^2+x_2^2)+\rho(x_1+x_2)^2\), but perspective only the separable terms. At \(z=1/2\) and \(x=(1/2,1/2)\), the resulting relaxation requires only \[t\ge(1-\rho)\frac{x_1^2+x_2^2}{z}+\rho(x_1+x_2)^2=1,\] whereas the exact common-indicator perspective requires \(t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx/z=1+\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a common indicator, perspectivizing only diagonal terms leaves a strict gap whenever an unperspectivized positive coupled component remains.
assumptions_latex: A single indicator controls both coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \((x,z)=((1/2,1/2),1/2)\), the termwise bound is \(1\) while the exact hull bound is \(1+\rho\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: directly checkable two-variable strict-gap construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The numerical gap calculation is correct, the plain and LaTeX statements agree, and counterexample is the correct content kind, but no inspectable source supports the stated failure regime.

children.title: Disjunctive Quadratic Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Quadratic strengthening obtained from discrete disjunctions and lifted convex hulls.

children.title: On–Off Disjunctive Hulls
children.top_down_role: Convex-hull organization of active and inactive quadratic regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: On–Off Disjunctive Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective description of the convex hull of inactive and active quadratic regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, let \(Q\succeq0\), and define \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\). For \(S=\{(0,0,t):t\ge0\}\cup\{(x,1,t):x\in C,\ t\ge q(x)\}\), its closed convex hull is \[\operatorname{clconv}S=\left\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ x\in zC,\ t\ge\frac{x^{\mathsf T}Qx}{z}+c^{\mathsf T}x+dz\right\},\] where the inequality and \(x\in zC\) use their closed extensions at \(z=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hull of inactive and active convex-quadratic regimes is the closed perspective epigraph together with the scaled active-domain constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}S\) equals the closed perspective formulation over \(0\le z\le1\) and \(x\in zC\).

notation.meaning: scaled active-domain set, with zero-scale closure

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex hull of an inactive point and a convex epigraph via homogenization
