children.title: Quadratic Lift-Project Family
children.top_down_role: Lifted disjunctive strengthening projected into quadratic relaxation spaces.

children.title: Quadratic Lift–Project Operators
children.top_down_role: Disjunctive operators acting on lifted quadratic relaxation spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Lift–Project Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step disjunctive closure operator applied in a quadratic lifted variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb S^n\times[0,1]^m\) be a closed convex relaxation in variables \((x,X,z)\), with \(X\) representing quadratic products. For indicator index \(i\), define the quadratic lift–project operator \[\mathcal L_i(K)=\operatorname{proj}_{x,X,z}\operatorname{clconv}\bigl((K\cap\{z_i=0\})\cup(K\cap\{z_i=1\})\bigr),\] where the convexification may be constructed in a disaggregated copy of the lifted space before projection. The operator is monotone and strengthening: if \(K_1\subseteq K_2\), then \(\mathcal L_i(K_1)\subseteq\mathcal L_i(K_2)\subseteq K_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic lift–project step convexifies the two branches of one indicator in lifted product space and projects the result back, producing a monotone strengthening.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex lifted relaxation.
\(z_i\in[0,1]\) is designated as binary in the original model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_1\subseteq K_2\Rightarrow\mathcal L_i(K_1)\subseteq\mathcal L_i(K_2)\subseteq K_2\).

notation.meaning: projection onto the original lifted variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operator definition and monotonicity inclusions are mathematically consistent and definition is an appropriate content kind. The cited generic convex-set section does not establish this specialized quadratic lift-project operator.

children.title: Projected Quadratic Cut Families
children.top_down_role: Quadratic strengthening retained after projection from lifted disjunctive spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Quadratic Cut Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cuts obtained by projecting valid inequalities from a quadratic lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(Y=xx^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{S}^n\) be a convex lifted relaxation satisfying \(\{(x,xx^{\mathsf T}):x\in S\}\subseteq L\). A projected quadratic cut is an inequality \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) whose lifted form \(\langle Q,Y\rangle+a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) is valid for \(L\). The projected cut family induced by \(L\) is \[\mathcal C(L)=\{(Q,a,b):\langle Q,Y\rangle+a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\text{ for every }(x,Y)\in L\}.\] Every member is valid for \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected quadratic cut results by replacing a valid lifted inequality in the matrix variable with the original quadratic expression.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) contains every lifted point \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) with \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) is valid for every \(x\in S\).

notation.meaning: Lifted symmetric matrix representing quadratic products.
Trace inner product of symmetric matrices.
Family of projected quadratic cuts induced by the lift.

review_flags: Exact intended lift–project operator is not specified by the node path.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is plausible, but no citation identifies the intended quadratic lift-project construction. The domains of Q, a, and b are also not stated, so the precise projected family cannot be validated.

children.title: Lift–Project Depth Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Strength progression across repeated or higher-order lift–project rounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Lift–Project Depth Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-depth hierarchy generated by repeated quadratic lift–project closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a relaxation of \(S\), and let \(T\) be a closure operator satisfying \(S\subseteq T(K)\subseteq K\) whenever \(S\subseteq K\). Define \(K_{r+1}=T(K_r)\) for integers \(r\geq0\). Then \[S\subseteq K_{r+1}\subseteq K_r\subseteq K_0.\] Consequently, for every minimization objective \(f\), the relaxation bounds \(v_r=\inf\{f(x):x\in K_r\}\) satisfy \(v_r\leq v_{r+1}\leq v_S\), where \(v_S=\inf\{f(x):x\in S\}\). Finite convergence requires an additional rank or exactness property of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated valid lift–project closure produces nested relaxations and monotonically improving minimization bounds; finite convergence is operator-dependent.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq T(K)\subseteq K\) for every relaxation \(K\) under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq K_{r+1}\subseteq K_r\) and \(v_r\leq v_{r+1}\leq v_S\) for all \(r\geq0\).

notation.meaning: Valid tightening closure induced by a lift–project operator.

review_flags: Finite-depth behavior depends on the unspecified quadratic lift–project operator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nestedness and bound monotonicity follow from the displayed assumptions, but no source connects this abstract operator iteration to the terminal quadratic lift-project hierarchy. Calling T a closure operator is also ambiguous because only validity and contraction, not the usual closure axioms, are specified.

children.title: Projection-Loss Regimes
children.top_down_role: Strength lost when lifted disjunctive information is returned to a smaller relaxation space.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Loss Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when projecting a tractable lifted relaxation loses quadratic-strengthening information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{S}^n\) be a convex relaxation and let \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(L)\). Projection is lossless for linear optimization in \(x\): \[\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:(x,Y)\in L\}=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in P\}.\] It can be lossy for objectives or constraints depending on \(Y\). Specifically, if \(x_0\in P\) admits \(Y_0\) with \((x_0,Y_0)\in L\) but \(Y_0\neq x_0x_0^{\mathsf T}\), then eliminating \(Y\) without retaining all projected consequences cannot certify the rank-one relation at \(x_0\). Thus exactness is preserved only when the retained description enforces every required consequence of \(Y=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection preserves linear optimization over retained variables but may discard information enforcing quadratic products or rank one.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is nonempty and its relevant infima are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linear objectives in \(x\) are projection-invariant, whereas the relation \(Y=xx^{\mathsf T}\) may be lost.

notation.meaning: Projection of the lifted relaxation onto original variables.

review_flags: The taxonomy does not specify a particular projection operator or loss metric.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality for objectives depending only on x is correct, but the asserted boundary for preserving exactness is not formulated using a definite projection operator, retained description, or loss measure. A source is required to establish the intended failure regime and its hypotheses.

children.title: Split-Derived Quadratic Cuts
children.top_down_role: Quadratic strengthening induced by split disjunctions on integer variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Split-Derived Quadratic Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Split closure for a quadratic lifted relaxation with integer-designated variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{S}^n\) relax \(Y=xx^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(x_I\) be integer-designated. For \(\pi\in\mathbb{Z}^{|I|}\) and \(k\in\mathbb{Z}\), define the split disjunction \(D_{\pi,k}=\{\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\leq k\}\cup\{\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\geq k+1\}\). A split-derived quadratic cut is an inequality \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) whose lifted inequality \(\langle Q,Y\rangle+a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) is valid for \[\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\bigl((L\cap D_{pi,k}^{-})\cup(L\cap D_{pi,k}^{+})\bigr),\] where the two terms denote the respective half-spaces of the split.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split-derived quadratic cut is the projection of a lifted inequality valid after convexifying the two sides of an integer split.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) contains every exact lifted feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting quadratic inequality is valid for all integer-feasible points represented by \(L\).

notation.meaning: Two-term split disjunction on the integer variables.

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

review_flags: Locator may support split methodology without the exact lifted quadratic formulation.

children.title: Multi-Term Disjunctive Quadratic Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convexification for quadratic models with several discrete operating regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Term Disjunctive Quadratic Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenized convex-hull formulation for finitely many closed convex quadratic regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_k=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_{kj}(x)\leq0, j=1,dots,m_k\}\) be nonempty closed convex sets defined by convex quadratic functions, for \(k=1,dots,K\). If their recession behavior makes the perspective formulation closed, then \[\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\Bigl(\bigcup_{k=1}^K C_k\Bigr)=\left\{x=\sum_{k=1}^Kx^k:\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k=1, \lambda_k\geq0, \lambda_k g_{kj}(x^k/\lambda_k)\leq0\right\},\] using each closed perspective at \(\lambda_k=0\). This yields an ideal continuous convexification before any formulation-specific conic or linear representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of finitely many convex quadratic regimes is represented by disaggregated variables and closed perspective constraints.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_k\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The closed perspectives correctly encode recession points at \(\lambda_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The disaggregated perspective formulation equals \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^K C_k)\).

notation.meaning: Disaggregated variable assigned to regime k.
Closed perspective of a convex function.

review_flags: A precise authoritative source for the closed multi-term perspective formulation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closed multi-term perspective hull formula depends on precise recession and closedness conditions that are only described informally. The index expressions use literal 'dots' rather than \dots. A source is needed before the exact formulation and hypotheses can be fixed reliably.

children.title: Exact Binary Product Linearizations

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Binary Product Linearizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull linearization of one binary–bounded-continuous product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1\}\), let \(\ell\leq y\leq u\) with finite \(\ell\leq u\), and introduce \(z=xy\). The convex hull in \((x,y,z)\)-space is exactly \[0\leq x\leq1, \ell\leq y\leq u, \ell x\leq z\leq ux, y-u(1-x)\leq z\leq y-\ell(1-x).\] When \(x\) is restricted to binary values, these inequalities force \(z=0\) for \(x=0\) and \(z=y\) for \(x=1\); with \(0\leq x\leq1\), they describe the ideal linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four linear inequalities give the exact convex hull of a product between a binary variable and a bounded continuous variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed polyhedron is \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,z):x\in\{0,1\}, \ell\leq y\leq u, z=xy\}\).

notation.meaning: Auxiliary variable representing the product xy.
Finite lower and upper bounds on y.

children.title: Piecewise-Linear Quadratic Approximations
children.top_down_role: Domain-partitioned linear approximations of quadratic functions and products.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Linear Quadratic Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Secant and tangent approximations of a univariate convex quadratic on a bounded partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=x^2\) on \([a,b]\), and let \(a=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_m=b\). On \([t_{i-1},t_i]\), the secant \(s_i(x)=(t_{i-1}+t_i)x-t_{i-1}t_i\) satisfies \(q(x)\leq s_i(x)\), while every tangent \(\tau_j(x)=2t_jx-t_j^2\) satisfies \(\tau_j(x)\leq q(x)\). Hence the piecewise-linear functions \(\underline q(x)=\max_j\tau_j(x)\) and \(\overline q(x)=s_i(x)\) on each active interval obey \[\underline q(x)\leq x^2\leq\overline q(x).\] If \(h=\max_i(t_i-t_{i-1})\), both pointwise gaps are at most \(h^2/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition secants overestimate a convex square, partition tangents underestimate it, and the maximum error decreases quadratically with mesh width.
assumptions_latex: All partition nodes are used as tangent points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline q(x)\leq x^2\leq\overline q(x)\) and both gaps are bounded by \(h^2/4\).

notation.meaning: Secant interpolant on partition interval i.
Tangent affine function at partition node j.

children.title: Polyhedral Outer Approximation of Convex Quadratics
children.top_down_role: Linear outer approximations of convex quadratic epigraphs and constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(T\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is finite for the finite polyhedral approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}(q)\subseteq P_T\), and \(\operatorname{epi}(q)=\bigcap_{\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n}P_{\{\bar x\}}\).

notation.meaning: Epigraph of the convex quadratic q.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane representation and finite outer approximation of a convex quadratic epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(d\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(Q\succeq0\). For every expansion point \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), convexity gives \[q(x)\geq q(\bar x)+\nabla q(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x).\] Therefore, for any finite \(T\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), the polyhedron \[P_T=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}:t\geq q(\bar x)+\nabla q(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\text{ for every }\bar x\in T\}\] contains \(\operatorname{epi}(q)\). Using every expansion point recovers the epigraph exactly: \[\operatorname{epi}(q)=\bigcap_{\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n}P_{\{\bar x\}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangent inequalities give polyhedral outer approximations of a convex quadratic epigraph, and the intersection of the tangent half-spaces over all expansion points equals the epigraph.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Outer Approximation of Convex Quadratics

children.title: Linearization Size–Strength Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Extended-formulation growth and relaxation-quality tradeoffs in MILP-oriented reformulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearization Size–Strength Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity of relaxation strength under nested linearization refinements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the original feasible set, and let \(P_r\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^{p_r}\) be extended polyhedra indexed by refinement level \(r\), with \(F\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(P_r)\). If refinements are nested, \(\operatorname{proj}_x(P_{r+1})\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(P_r)\), then for minimization \[\inf_{(x,w)\in P_r}c^{\mathsf T}x\leq\inf_{(x,w)\in P_{r+1}}c^{\mathsf T}x\leq\inf_{x\in F}c^{\mathsf T}x.\] Thus additional segments, disaggregated variables, or valid inequalities cannot weaken the bound when nesting is preserved, but generally increase variables or constraints. No universal strict improvement follows solely from larger formulation size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested linearization refinements improve or preserve bounds but enlarge formulations; size alone does not guarantee stronger projections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimization lower bounds are nondecreasing with refinement and never exceed the exact optimum.

notation.meaning: Extended polyhedral relaxation at refinement level r.
Number of auxiliary variables at level r.

review_flags: The locator supports refinement methodology; explicit size bounds remain formulation-dependent.

children.title: SDP–RLT Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: Combined matrix-cone and reformulation–linearization strengthening.

children.title: Box-Constrained SDP–RLT
children.top_down_role: Combined relaxation specialized to finite variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Box-Constrained SDP–RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-level SDP–RLT relaxation generated from finite variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\ell_i\leq x_i\leq u_i\), introduce \(X\in\mathbb{S}^n\) for \(xx^{\mathsf T}\). The box SDP–RLT relaxation imposes \[\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\] and, for every \(i,j\), the linearizations of the four valid products \[(x_i-\ell_i)(x_j-\ell_j)\geq0, (x_i-\ell_i)(u_j-x_j)\geq0, (u_i-x_i)(x_j-\ell_j)\geq0, (u_i-x_i)(u_j-x_j)\geq0,\] replacing each \(x_ix_j\) by \(X_{ij}\). Every exact lifted box point satisfies these constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Box SDP–RLT combines a moment positive-semidefinite constraint with all pairwise linearized products of bound inequalities.
assumptions_latex: All bounds \(\ell_i,u_i\) are finite with \(\ell_i\leq u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(x,xx^{\mathsf T}):\ell\leq x\leq u\}\) is contained in the displayed SDP–RLT relaxation.

notation.meaning: Symmetric matrix of lifted quadratic products.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the SDP–RLT construction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed moment constraint and bound-product linearizations form a standard box SDP-RLT relaxation, and representation is the appropriate kind. No source with a specific SDP-RLT locator is supplied, so the exact family cannot be accepted under the evidence contract.

children.title: Polyhedrally Constrained SDP–RLT
children.top_down_role: Combined relaxation using products of general linear constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedrally Constrained SDP–RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SDP–RLT relaxation from pairwise products of general linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\geq0, i=1,dots,m\}\). Introduce \(X\in\mathbb{S}^n\). The first-level polyhedral SDP–RLT relaxation consists of \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\geq0\), \[\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\] and, for every \(1\leq i\leq j\leq m\), \[a_i^{\mathsf T}Xa_j-b_j a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i a_j^{\mathsf T}x+b_ib_j\geq0.\] The last inequality is the linearization of \((a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i)(a_j^{\mathsf T}x-b_j)\geq0\). Hence all exact lifts \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) with \(x\in P\) are feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General polyhedral SDP–RLT adds a moment PSD constraint and linearizations of every pairwise product of defining linear inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the lifted surrogate for \(xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(x,xx^{\mathsf T}):x\in P\}\) is contained in the SDP–RLT feasible set.

notation.meaning: Polyhedron supplying the RLT generating inequalities.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports polyhedral SDP–RLT.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise product linearization is algebraically consistent, but no specific source supports this polyhedral SDP-RLT formulation. The defining index also uses literal 'dots' instead of \dots. Source support is needed before issuing a corrected replacement.

children.title: QCQP SDP–RLT
children.top_down_role: Combined strengthening for quadratic objectives and quadratic constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: QCQP SDP–RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined semidefinite and RLT relaxation of a linearly bounded QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a QCQP with quadratic inequalities \(x^{\mathsf T}Q_kx+q_k^{\mathsf T}x+r_k\leq0\) and linear inequalities \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\geq0\). Introduce \(X\in\mathbb{S}^n\). Its first-level SDP–RLT relaxation replaces each quadratic constraint by \[\langle Q_k,X\rangle+q_k^{\mathsf T}x+r_k\leq0,\] imposes \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\), retains every linear inequality, and adds \[a_i^{\mathsf T}Xa_j-b_j a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i a_j^{\mathsf T}x+b_ib_j\geq0\] for all pairs. Substitution \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) proves containment of every QCQP-feasible point in the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QCQP SDP–RLT linearizes quadratic constraints in a matrix lift, adds a moment PSD constraint, and includes products of linear constraints.
assumptions_latex: The QCQP quadratic and linear inequalities are explicitly given.
RLT products are generated from inequalities known to be nonnegative on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible \(x\) yields a feasible lifted point \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) in the SDP–RLT relaxation.

notation.meaning: Lifted surrogate for the quadratic product matrix.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the combined QCQP SDP–RLT formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction is a plausible first-level SDP-RLT relaxation and the containment conclusion is correctly limited to feasible exact lifts. No cited source identifies this precise QCQP formulation, its level convention, or the selected RLT generators.

children.title: SDP–RLT Exactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem structures for which combined conic and product consistency closes the relaxation gap.

assumptions_latex: \(K_{\mathrm{SR}}\) is an SDP--RLT lifted feasible region in variables \((x,X)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{\mathrm{SR}}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\{(x,xx^\top):x\in F\}\), and every linear lifted objective has zero relaxation gap.

notation.meaning: convex hull of rank-one lifts of feasible points
feasible region of the combined SDP--RLT relaxation

review_flags: exact structural subclasses require a dedicated SDP--RLT source
exactness stated as a necessary-and-sufficient lifted-set criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes exactness of a fixed SDP--RLT formulation, rather than cataloguing problem subclasses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The SDP--RLT relaxation is exact over \(F\) precisely when
\[
K_{\mathrm{SR}}=K_F:=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\{(x,xx^\top):x\in F\}.
\]
Equivalently, for every \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), every \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n\), and every finite optimum,
\[
\inf_{(x,X)\in K_{\mathrm{SR}}}\bigl(c^\top x+\langle Q,X\rangle\bigr)
=
\inf_{x\in F}\bigl(c^\top x+x^\top Qx\bigr).
\]
For one specified objective, equality of these two infima is objective-wise exactness and does not imply equality of the lifted feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SDP–RLT is formulation-wise exact exactly when its lifted feasible set equals the closed convex hull of feasible rank-one lifts; objective-wise equality alone is weaker.
knowledge_statements.title: SDP–RLT Exactness Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this exactness criterion. The objective-wise equivalence also requires explicit closedness and convexity of the lifted relaxation; otherwise equality of all linear infima identifies only its closed convex hull.

children.title: SDP–RLT Redundancy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Domains where one component of the combined relaxation adds no further strength.

assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(R\) denote its SDP and RLT constraint families.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SDP component is redundant exactly when \(K_R\subseteq K_S\); the RLT component is redundant exactly when \(K_S\subseteq K_R\).

notation.meaning: region after imposing the SDP constraints
region after imposing the RLT constraints

review_flags: problem-specific redundancy regimes require a dedicated SDP--RLT source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives formulation-relative redundancy criteria; neither component is universally redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_S:=K_0\cap S\), \(K_R:=K_0\cap R\), and \(K_{SR}:=K_0\cap S\cap R\). The SDP constraints add no strength to the RLT relaxation if and only if
\[
K_R=K_{SR},
\]
which is equivalent to \(K_R\subseteq S\). The RLT constraints add no strength to the SDP relaxation if and only if
\[
K_S=K_{SR},
\]
which is equivalent to \(K_S\subseteq R\). Objective-relative redundancy only requires equality of the corresponding optimal values for the specified lifted linear objective and is strictly weaker than these set equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One component is formulation-wise redundant precisely when the feasible region produced by the other component already satisfies all of its constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: SDP–RLT Redundancy Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulation-relative redundancy criteria are mathematically coherent and fit the condition container, but no source supports their SDP–RLT interpretation.

children.title: Intermediate LP–SOCP–SDP Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxation families interpolating between polyhedral bounds and full semidefinite bounds.

children.title: Eigenvector-Cut Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral outer approximations derived from selected matrix directions.

assumptions_latex: \(M(x,X)\in\mathbb{S}^{n+1}\) is affine in the lifted variables.
\(V\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\) is a finite set of selected directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(v^\top M(x,X)v\ge 0\) define a polyhedral outer approximation of \(M(x,X)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite directional approximation of one lifted positive-semidefinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Replace \(M(x,X)\succeq0\) by the finite family
\[
v^\top M(x,X)v\ge0\qquad(v\in V).
\]
Because \(M\) is affine, every displayed condition is linear in \((x,X)\), and every positive-semidefinite matrix satisfies it. Hence the resulting feasible region contains the SDP region. If a candidate \((\bar x,\bar X)\) has an eigenpair \((\lambda,v)\) of \(M(\bar x,\bar X)\) with \(\lambda<0\), then \(v^\top M(x,X)v\ge0\) separates that candidate from the positive-semidefinite cone. Using all directions recovers \(M(x,X)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected directional quadratic-form inequalities give an LP outer approximation of a PSD constraint; an eigenvector associated with a negative eigenvalue supplies a violated cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvector-Cut Relaxations

children.title: Selected Principal-Minor Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Partial conic enforcement over chosen low-dimensional submatrices.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Enforcing \(M[I,I]\succeq0\) for \(I\in\mathcal I\) is a valid outer relaxation of \(M\succeq0\), monotone under enlargement of \(\mathcal I\).

notation.meaning: principal submatrix indexed by the set I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial PSD enforcement through a prescribed family of principal submatrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The selected principal-minor relaxation of \(M(x,X)\succeq0\) is
\[
M(x,X)[I,I]\succeq0\qquad(I\in\mathcal I).
\]
Every positive-semidefinite \(M(x,X)\) satisfies these constraints, so they define an outer relaxation. If \(\mathcal I_1\subseteq\mathcal I_2\), the feasible region for \(\mathcal I_2\) is contained in that for \(\mathcal I_1\). If \(\mathcal I\) contains the full index set, the relaxation equals the original PSD constraint. For \(|I|=2\), each block condition is representable by a rotated second-order cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD constraints on selected principal submatrices form a valid outer relaxation; adding index sets strengthens it, and including the full matrix recovers the SDP constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Selected Principal-Minor Relaxations

children.title: Sparse-Block Cone Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: Selective cone enforcement over sparse cliques or interaction blocks.

children.title: Clique Cone Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Selective conic enforcement over graph cliques.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is a selected family of cliques of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The clique relaxation imposes \(M[C,C]\succeq0\) for every \(C\in\mathcal C\).

notation.meaning: symmetric lifted matrix indexed by N

review_flags: chordal completion equivalence intentionally not asserted
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines clique-local cone enforcement without assuming chordality or PSD-completion equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a symmetric lifted matrix \(M\in\mathbb S^N\), the clique cone relaxation associated with \(\mathcal C\) is
\[
M[C,C]\succeq0\qquad(C\in\mathcal C).
\]
Each constraint is necessary for \(M\succeq0\); consequently, their intersection is an outer approximation of the global PSD cone. Enlarging a clique or adding a clique can only shrink the relaxation. When \(N\in\mathcal C\), the global PSD constraint itself is present and the approximation is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clique cone relaxation enforces PSD only on selected clique-indexed blocks. It contains the global PSD cone and strengthens monotonically as clique coverage grows.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique Cone Relaxations

children.title: Interaction-Block Cone Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Selective conic enforcement over prescribed variable or interaction blocks.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interaction-block relaxation is the intersection of the local cones \(M[B,B]\succeq0\) over \(B\in\mathcal B\).

notation.meaning: principal lifted block indexed by B

review_flags: interaction-block terminology may vary by source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blocks are chosen from modeled interactions and need not be graph-theoretic cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an interaction-block family \(\mathcal B\), define the block-cone outer approximation by
\[
K_{\mathcal B}:=\{(x,X):M(x,X)[B,B]\succeq0\ \text{for every }B\in\mathcal B\}.
\]
Blocks may be selected to contain supports of objective or constraint terms. Since every principal submatrix of a positive-semidefinite matrix is positive semidefinite,
\[
\{(x,X):M(x,X)\succeq0\}\subseteq K_{\mathcal B}.
\]
Thus local interaction cones preserve validity while avoiding a single full-dimensional cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interaction-block relaxations impose PSD on blocks chosen to cover modeled variable interactions, producing a valid outer approximation of the global PSD constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Interaction-Block Cone Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-PSD construction is mathematically valid, but the exact meaning of “interaction-block cone relaxation” is source-dependent, and the cited cone-covering locator does not inspectably establish this terminology or formulation.

children.title: Block-Overlap Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility requirements among intersecting conic blocks.

assumptions_latex: \(Y^B\in\mathbb S^B\) is a local lifted matrix for each \(B\in\mathcal B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local blocks represent one global partial matrix exactly when their entries agree on every overlap.

notation.meaning: local lifted matrix on block B

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entrywise consistency condition for independently represented overlapping cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The local matrices are overlap-consistent when
\[
Y^B[B\cap D,B\cap D]=Y^D[B\cap D,B\cap D]
\qquad(B,D\in\mathcal B).
\]
This condition is necessary and sufficient for the existence of a single symmetric partial matrix \(Y\), specified on \(\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal B}B\times B\), whose restriction to each block is \(Y^B\). It does not by itself guarantee that the partial matrix has a global positive-semidefinite completion; that additional conclusion depends on the block graph and completion hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independently modeled cone blocks define one global partial matrix exactly when every pair assigns identical entries to their common indices; PSD completion requires additional structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Overlap Consistency

children.title: Cone-Coverage Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Relaxation strength as clique or block coverage varies.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B_1\) and \(\mathcal B_2\) are block families on the same lifted matrix.
\(K_{\mathcal B}\) enforces PSD on every block in \(\mathcal B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If every block of \(\mathcal B_1\) lies within a block of \(\mathcal B_2\), then \(K_{\mathcal B_2}\subseteq K_{\mathcal B_1}\).

notation.meaning: feasible region of a block-cone relaxation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orders block-cone relaxations by containment coverage, not merely by the number of blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write \(\mathcal B_1\preceq\mathcal B_2\) when, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_1\), some \(D\in\mathcal B_2\) satisfies \(B\subseteq D\). Because positive semidefiniteness of \(M[D,D]\) implies positive semidefiniteness of every principal submatrix \(M[B,B]\),
\[
\mathcal B_1\preceq\mathcal B_2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
K_{\mathcal B_2}\subseteq K_{\mathcal B_1}.
\]
Thus greater containment coverage yields a relaxation at least as strong. If the full index set \(N\) belongs to \(\mathcal B_2\), then \(K_{\mathcal B_2}=\{(x,X):M(x,X)\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block family is at least as strong as another when its blocks contain all blocks of the other; a full-index block recovers the global PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Coverage Strength Regimes

children.title: Structural-Information Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Valid problem information added to the base lifted quadratic relaxation.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Global Quadratic Optimization via Conic Relaxation: using additional information

children.title: Redundant Quadratic Constraint Families
children.top_down_role: Additional valid quadratic relations used to strengthen lifted relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Quadratic Constraint Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers valid but optimization-redundant quadratic inequalities whose lifts may strengthen a relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A redundant quadratic constraint for \(F\) is an inequality
\[
q(x):=x^\top Qx+2a^\top x+\alpha\le0
\]
that holds for every \(x\in F\) and therefore does not change \(F\). Under the lift \(X=xx^\top\), it yields the inequality
\[
\langle Q,X\rangle+2a^\top x+\alpha\le0,
\]
which is valid for every rank-one feasible lift \((x,xx^\top)\) with \(x\in F\). Adding it to a lifted outer relaxation preserves all such lifts but may remove points with \(X\ne xx^\top\); hence redundancy in the original variables does not imply redundancy after relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic inequality already valid on the feasible set is redundant originally, but its linearized lifted form can exclude non-rank-one relaxation points and strengthen the bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted inequality \(\langle Q,X\rangle+2a^\top x+\alpha\le0\) is valid for every rank-one lift \((x,xx^\top)\) with \(x\in F\), and adding it to an outer relaxation preserves all such lifts.

notation.meaning: quadratic relation valid on the original feasible set
matrix variable replacing the product xx-transpose

review_flags: locator supports quadratic strengthening only indirectly

children.title: Symmetry-Orbit Strengthening Calculus
children.top_down_role: Reduction and valid inequalities induced by model symmetry.

children.title: Symmetry Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduction of equivalent quadratic structures using model automorphisms.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite group acting orthogonally on \(\mathbb R^n\).
\(K\) is a nonempty convex lifted feasible set invariant under the induced action.
\(L\) is a linear objective invariant under that action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimum exists in the fixed-point subspace, so restricting the lifted problem to group-fixed variables preserves its optimal value.

notation.meaning: group average of a lifted point
fixed-point subspace of the induced action

review_flags: attainment is required for the optimizer conclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-group reduction for convex lifted relaxations with invariant linear objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume the minimum of \(L\) over \(K\) is attained. For every \(z\in K\), define
\[
\Pi_G(z):=\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}g\cdot z.
\]
Convexity and invariance give \(\Pi_G(z)\in K\), while \(\Pi_G(z)\in\operatorname{Fix}(G)\) and objective invariance gives \(L(\Pi_G(z))=L(z)\). Consequently,
\[
\min_{z\in K}L(z)=\min_{z\in K\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)}L(z),
\]
and the reduced problem has an optimal group-fixed solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite symmetry group, averaging any feasible lifted point preserves feasibility and an invariant linear objective, so optimization may be restricted to group-fixed variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry Reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: With attainment assumed, the finite-group averaging theorem is correct and fits the symmetry-reduction container, but no authoritative symmetry-reduction source is supplied.

children.title: Orbit Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Aggregation of variables, products, or constraints belonging to common symmetry orbits.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite permutation group on an index set \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The entries of \(Y\) are constant on the group orbits of ordered index pairs, permitting one variable per orbit.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entry-orbit parameterization of permutation-invariant lifted matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) act on ordered pairs by \(g\cdot(i,j)=(g(i),g(j))\). The invariance equations
\[
P_gYP_g^\top=Y\qquad(g\in G)
\]
are equivalent to
\[
Y_{ij}=Y_{k\ell}\quad\text{whenever }(k,\ell)\in\mathcal O(i,j).
\]
Hence an invariant symmetric matrix admits the orbit representation
\[
Y=\sum_{O\in(N\times N)/G}y_OA_O,
\]
where \(A_O\) is the symmetric indicator matrix of the pair orbit \(O\), with coincident transpose-orbits identified. Substituting this representation aggregates all entries in the same orbit into one scalar variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A permutation-invariant lifted matrix is constant on pair orbits, so all entries in each orbit can be represented by one aggregate variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Orbit Aggregation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied. Moreover, an ordered-pair orbit need not have a symmetric indicator matrix when its transpose is a distinct orbit; the representation must explicitly use transpose-orbit unions or otherwise identify their coefficients.

children.title: Orbit-Derived Quadratic Cuts
children.top_down_role: Valid quadratic strengthening generated from orbit structure.

assumptions_latex: \(q(x)\le0\) is a valid quadratic inequality on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every transformed inequality \(q(g^{-1}x)\le0\), and every nonnegative orbit aggregate of them, is valid on \(F\).

notation.meaning: finite symmetry group of the feasible set
quadratic inequality obtained by applying symmetry g

review_flags: authoritative source for orbit-derived quadratic cuts not supplied
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity calculus for transporting and aggregating quadratic cuts over finite symmetry orbits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(g\in G\), define \(q_g(x):=q(g^{-1}x)\). Since \(g^{-1}x\in F\) whenever \(x\in F\), every orbit image
\[
q_g(x)\le0
\]
is valid on \(F\). Moreover, any nonnegative aggregate
\[
\sum_{g\in G}w_gq_g(x)\le0,

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a structured domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), define its exact lifted graph by \(G_D=\{(x,xx^{\mathsf T}):x\in D\}\). A domain-specific quadratic cut family is a collection of affine inequalities \(\alpha_k+\beta_k^{\mathsf T}x+\langle C_k,X\rangle\geq0\), indexed by \(k\in K\), each valid on \(G_D\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance when RLT includes all bound products underlying McCormick envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the RLT construction includes every lower-bound and upper-bound slack product whose linearization produces the termwise McCormick inequalities. Then its feasible region satisfies \(R_{\mathrm{RLT}}\subseteq R_{\mathrm{MC}}\). Hence, for minimization of the common lifted objective \(L\), \(\inf_{R_{\mathrm{MC}}}L\leq\inf_{R_{\mathrm{RLT}}}L\). Under compactness, the dominance is strict for \(L\) exactly when no minimizer of \(L\) over \(R_{\mathrm{MC}}\) satisfies all additional RLT inequalities. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a lifted polyhedral relaxation for a minimization problem, and let \(C\) consist of valid second-order-cone constraints, such as \(\|(2X_{ij},X_{ii}-X_{jj})\|_2\leq X_{ii}+X_{jj}\) with \(X_{ii},X_{jj}\geq0\). Consequently, for the common lifted linear objective \(L\), \(\inf_P L\leq\inf_{P\cap C}L\leq v^*\), where \(v^*\) is the original optimum. The first inequality is strict exactly when the conic restrictions eliminate all polyhedral minimizers, assuming attainment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment-based comparison; formulation labels alone imply no universal ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two valid lifted relaxation regions \(P\) and \(C\), polyhedral versus SOCP dominance is determined by containment, not by representation class alone. If \(C\subseteq P\), then the SOCP bound dominates: \(\inf_P L\leq\inf_C L\). If \(P\subseteq C\), the polyhedral bound dominates. If neither containment holds, the relaxations are generally incomparable: there may exist lifted linear objectives \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) for which the respective bound orderings are opposite. Under compactness and \(C\subseteq P\), strict SOCP dominance for \(L\) occurs exactly when \(\operatorname*{argmin}_P L\cap C=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compact conic representation of convex quadratic epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the rotated second-order cone by \(\mathcal{K}_{r}=\{(u,v,z):u\geq0,\ v\geq0,\ 2uv\geq\|z\|_2^2\}\). If \(Q=A^{\mathsf T}A\succeq0\), then \[x^{\mathsf T}Qx\leq t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \|Ax\|_2^2\leq t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (t,\tfrac12,Ax)\in\mathcal{K}_{r}.\] Thus a convex quadratic epigraph has an exact finite SOCP representation. A formulation restricted to finitely many affine inequalities generally supplies only a polyhedral approximation unless additional variables and a problem-specific exact polyhedral description are available.

children.title: SOCP Principal-Minor Bounds

assumptions_latex: \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\) is the lifted moment matrix.
The original problem is a minimization problem with lifted linear objective \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Y\succeq0\ \Longrightarrow\ Y_{ii}Y_{jj}\geq Y_{ij}^2\quad(i<j),\] so the full SDP region is contained in the SOCP principal-minor region.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive semidefiniteness implies nonnegativity of every principal minor, and each order-two condition is SOC-representable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-two principal-minor relaxation of a lifted positive-semidefinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each pair \(i<j\), nonnegativity of the corresponding order-two principal minor of \(Y\) requires \(Y_{ii}\geq0\), \(Y_{jj}\geq0\), and \(Y_{ij}^2\leq Y_{ii}Y_{jj}\). This is equivalently the second-order-cone constraint \[\|(2Y_{ij},Y_{ii}-Y_{jj})\|_2\leq Y_{ii}+Y_{jj}.\] Imposing all such constraints gives the SOCP principal-minor relaxation. Since \(Y\succeq0\) implies every order-two principal-minor constraint, the full SDP feasible region is contained in this SOCP region. Therefore its minimization bounds satisfy \(v_{\mathrm{SOCP}}\leq v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\leq v^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Positivity Strength Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete separation between pairwise principal-minor constraints and full matrix positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[M(r):=(1-r)I_3+r\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T},\qquad -1<r<-\tfrac12.\] Every \(2\times2\) principal submatrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&r\\r&1\end{pmatrix}\succ0\), whereas \(M(r)\) has eigenvalue \(1+2r<0\) in the direction \(\mathbf{1}\) and hence satisfies \(M(r)\not\succeq0\). Thus order-two principal-submatrix constraints do not imply full matrix positivity. If the remaining lifted constraints admit such a matrix and the objective separates it from the SDP set, the SOCP–SDP bound inequality is strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-dimensional matrix can have every two-by-two principal submatrix positive definite while having a negative eigenvalue, so pairwise constraints may be strictly weaker than full SDP positivity.
assumptions_latex: The SOCP surrogate tests only all \(2\times2\) principal submatrices of a symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pairwise principal-minor positivity does not imply full positive semidefiniteness, so the SOCP feasible set can strictly contain the SDP feasible set.

notation.meaning: Three-dimensional equicorrelation matrix with off-diagonal parameter r

children.top_down_role: Bounds combining matrix positivity with RLT consistency.

knowledge_statements.title: SDP–RLT Combined Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection strengthening of compatible SDP and first-level RLT lifted formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[F_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}:=F_{\mathrm{SDP}}\cap F_{\mathrm{RLT}},\qquad \beta_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}:=\inf_{(x,X)\in F_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}}L(x,X).\] The combined feasible set contains every original lift \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) and is contained in each component relaxation. Consequently, it is a valid relaxation and satisfies \[\beta_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}\ge\max\{\beta_{\mathrm{SDP}},\beta_{\mathrm{RLT}}\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting compatible SDP and RLT feasible sets preserves validity and gives a minimization bound at least as strong as either component bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F_{\mathrm{RLT}}\) and \(F_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) are valid lifted relaxations in the same variables \((x,X)\).
Their intersection is nonempty and the common objective is \(L(x,X)=\langle Q,X\rangle+2q^{\mathsf T}x+c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}\ge\max\{\beta_{\mathrm{RLT}},\beta_{\mathrm{SDP}}\}\), while remaining a valid lower bound.

children.title: SDP–RLT Dominance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which matrix-cone consistency strictly strengthens RLT.

knowledge_statements.title: SDP–RLT Dominance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound ordering induced by intersection, without assuming containment between standalone SDP and RLT sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}=F_{\mathrm{SDP}}\cap F_{\mathrm{RLT}}\), minimization satisfies \[\beta_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}\ge\beta_{\mathrm{SDP}},\qquad \beta_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}\ge\beta_{\mathrm{RLT}}.\] No universal ordering between \(\beta_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) and \(\beta_{\mathrm{RLT}}\) follows without additional containment or structural assumptions. Under attainment, \(\beta_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}=\beta_{[0m\mathrm{RLT}}\) exactly when an RLT-optimal point belongs to \(F_{\mathrm{SDP}}\), and \(\beta_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}=\beta_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) exactly when an SDP-optimal point belongs to \(F_{\mathrm{RLT}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SDP–RLT intersection dominates each standalone relaxation, while standalone SDP and RLT bounds have no universal ordering without additional containment.
assumptions_latex: The RLT, SDP, and combined relaxations share the same lifted variables and minimization objective.
All three infima are finite, and the relevant optima are attained when an equality criterion is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The combined relaxation dominates both components; the two component relaxations need not dominate one another.

notation.meaning: Bounds from the RLT, SDP, and intersected relaxations

children.title: Matrix-Consistency Increment
children.top_down_role: Incremental bound strength attributable specifically to semidefinite consistency.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Consistency Increment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-specific gain obtained by imposing full moment-matrix positivity on an RLT relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\Delta_{\mathrm{mat}}:=\beta_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}-\beta_{\mathrm{RLT}}\ge0\] and \[S_{\mathrm{RLT}}^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,X)\in F_{\mathrm{RLT}}}L(x,X).\] Then \[\Delta_{\mathrm{mat}}=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S_{\mathrm{RLT}}^*\cap F_{\mathrm{SDP}}\neq\varnothing,\] and \[\Delta_{\mathrm{mat}}>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S_{\mathrm{RLT}}^*\cap F_{\mathrm{SDP}}=\varnothing.\] The increment therefore records objective-relevant matrix inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding SDP matrix consistency strictly improves the RLT bound exactly when every RLT-optimal lifted point fails the SDP constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(F_{\mathrm{RLT}}\) is compact, \(F_{\mathrm{SDP\text{-}RLT}}=F_{\mathrm{RLT}}\cap F_{\mathrm{SDP}}\neq\varnothing\), and \(L\) is linear.
The minima over both feasible sets are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matrix-consistency increment is positive exactly when every RLT minimizer violates the SDP matrix constraint.

notation.meaning: Improvement from adding full matrix consistency to RLT

children.title: Relaxation Incomparability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem classes where standard relaxation families lack a universal bound ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Incomparability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-independent incomparability characterized by failure of feasible-set containment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\in\{1,2\}\), define \(\beta_k(c):=\min_{z\in F_k}c^{\mathsf T}z\). If \(F_1\nsubseteq F_2\) and \(F_2\nsubseteq F_1\), then there exist \(c,d\in\mathbb{R}^d\) such that \[\beta_1(c)<\beta_2(c),\qquad \beta_2(d)<\beta_1(d).\] Thus neither relaxation supplies a uniformly stronger minimization bound over all linear objectives. Additional containment, structural assumptions, or restrictions on the objective family are required for a universal ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noncontained compact convex relaxation sets admit objectives favoring each set in turn, so their bounds are incomparable without additional structure.
assumptions_latex: \(F_1,F_2\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) are nonempty compact convex lifted relaxation sets.
Neither containment holds: \(F_1\nsubseteq F_2\) and \(F_2\nsubseteq F_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist linear objectives producing \(\beta_1<\beta_2\) and other linear objectives producing \(\beta_2<\beta_1\); hence no universal bound ordering exists.

notation.meaning: Minimum of a linear objective over relaxation k

children.title: Quadratic Relaxation Exactness Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Structural routes by which a convex quadratic relaxation attains the original optimum.

children.title: Hidden-Convexity Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness arising from explicit or transformed convex quadratic geometry.

assumptions_latex: There is an exact transformation \(T:S\to C\) onto a convex set \(C\), with \(f(x)=g(Tx)\), where \(g\) is convex.
The transformed convex problem attains its infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\min_{y\in C}g(y)\), so the convex reformulation or a relaxation representing its epigraph is exact.

notation.meaning: Convex transformed feasible set and objective
Exact change of variables or lifting map

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness through an equivalent convex image, including transformations that expose convex quadratic geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(T:S\to C\) is onto and satisfies \(f(x)=g(Tx)\) for every \(x\in S\), where \(C\) is convex and \(g:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex. Then \[\inf_{x\in S}f(x)=\inf_{y\in C}g(y).\] If the right-hand infimum is attained, it equals \(\min_{y\in C}g(y)\). Consequently, any conic or lifted relaxation whose projection is exactly the epigraph \(\{(y,t):y\in C,\ t\ge g(y)\}\) has zero optimality gap. This exactness derives from equivalence of the transformed feasible geometry, not merely from a locally convex approximation of the original quadratic functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic problem is exactly solvable through hidden convexity when an exact transformation maps it onto a convex problem with the same objective values.
knowledge_statements.title: Hidden-Convexity Exactness

children.title: Rank-Based Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness identified through low-rank optimal lifted solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Based Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one certificate for exactness of a Shor-type SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an attained SDP optimum satisfies \[Y^*=\begin{pmatrix}1&(x^*)^{\mathsf T}\\x^*&X^*\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}(Y^*)=1,\] then \[Y^*=\begin{pmatrix}1\\x^*\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1\\x^*\end{pmatrix}^{\mathsf T},\qquad X^*=x^*(x^*)^{\mathsf T}.\] Under the lifted-constraint consistency assumption, \(x^*\) is feasible and optimal for the original quadratic problem, and the SDP bound equals the original optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal rank-one SDP moment matrix corresponds to an original feasible optimizer and certifies equality of the relaxation and original optimum.
assumptions_latex: A lifted SDP relaxation has an attained optimal solution \(Y^*=\begin{pmatrix}1&(x^*)^{\mathsf T}\\x^*&X^*\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\).
All lifted constraints reduce to the original feasibility conditions when \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^*=x^*(x^*)^{\mathsf T}\), \(x^*\) is original-feasible, and the SDP bound equals the original optimum.

source_refs.locator: 2.14.1 The SDP Cone p. 81; 2.14.3 SDP Programming p. 84

source_witnesses.locator: 2.14.1 The SDP Cone p. 81; 2.14.3 SDP Programming p. 84

children.title: Polyhedral Hull Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness produced by complete product-hull or envelope descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Hull Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness from a complete convex-hull description of lifted product points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x,X)=\langle Q,X\rangle+2q^{\mathsf T}x+c\). If \(F=\operatorname{conv}Z(S)\), then \[\min_{(x,X)\in F}L(x,X)=\min_{(x,X)\in Z(S)}L(x,X)=\min_{x\in S}\bigl(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2q^{\mathsf T}x+c\bigr).\] Hence a complete polyhedral description of the lifted convex hull is exact for every quadratic objective using this lifting. Valid envelope or RLT inequalities have this uniform exactness property only when they collectively describe the entire hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral lifting is exact for every linearized quadratic objective when it equals the convex hull of all feasible product lifts.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and compact, and \(Z(S):=\{(x,xx^{\mathsf T}):x\in S\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every quadratic objective linearized as \(L(x,X)\), \(\min_{(x,X)\in F}L(x,X)=\min_{x\in S}L(x,xx^{\mathsf T})\).

notation.meaning: Exact lifted image of original feasible points

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Convex Hull p. 12; 1.9 Polyhedral Convex Sets p. 27

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Convex Hull p. 12; 1.9 Polyhedral Convex Sets p. 27

children.title: Integrality-Driven Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness arising from ideal mixed-integer convexifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Driven Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness criterion for ideal mixed-integer lifted formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The integrality-driven exactness condition is \[F=\operatorname{conv}(S_I).\] Under this condition, every lifted linear objective \(L(z)=c^{\mathsf T}z+c_0\), including an exactly linearized quadratic objective, satisfies \[\min_{z\in F}L(z)=\min_{z\in S_I}L(z).\] Thus dropping the integrality restrictions introduces no objective-value gap. Equality for only one selected objective does not establish ideality, which requires convex-hull equality and uniform exactness over all linear objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ideal mixed-integer lifting has a continuous relaxation equal to the integer hull, making every linearized quadratic objective exact.
assumptions_latex: \(S_I\) is the lifted feasible set satisfying the required integrality restrictions, and \(F\) is the continuous relaxation of an extended formulation.
The formulation is ideal: \(F=\operatorname{conv}(S_I)\), and the relevant minima are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every linearized quadratic objective has the same minimum over \(F\) and \(S_I\); hence the continuous relaxation is exact.

notation.meaning: Lifted feasible set with integrality enforced
Continuous feasible set of the extended formulation

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Convex Hull p. 12; 1.9 Polyhedral Convex Sets p. 27

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Convex Hull p. 12; 1.9 Polyhedral Convex Sets p. 27

children.title: Structural Exactness Classes
children.top_down_role: Exactness tied to interaction signs, matrix rank, or sparse graph structure.

children.title: Sign-Structured Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness attributable to favorable interaction-sign patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Structured Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines exactness within a prescribed sign-switching class; it does not assert that every sign pattern guarantees exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal I\) be a family of quadratic programs, let \(R(I)\) be a relaxation of \(I\), and let \(v_R(I)\leq v(I)\) denote their minimization values. For a prescribed cone \(\mathcal K\) of sign-structured symmetric matrices, define
\[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sign}}(R,\mathcal K)=\left\{I\in\mathcal I:\exists D=\operatorname{Diag}(d),\ d_i\in\{-1,1\},\ DQ_jD\in\mathcal K\ \forall j,\ v_R(I)=v(I)\right\}.\]
Here \(Q_j\) are all objective and constraint quadratic matrices. Membership means that one simultaneous sign switching places the data in the chosen sign class and that the relaxation has zero value gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The class contains instances whose quadratic data share a prescribed sign pattern after one diagonal sign switch and whose selected relaxation has zero optimal-value gap.
assumptions_latex: \(R(I)\) is a valid lower-bounding relaxation for every minimization instance \(I\in\mathcal I\).
\(v_R(I)\) and \(v(I)\) are finite when exactness is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sign}}(R,\mathcal K)\iff (\exists D:\ DQ_jD\in\mathcal K\ \forall j)\land v_R(I)=v(I)\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix implementing a simultaneous sign switch.
Prescribed cone or class encoding the intended matrix sign structure.
Optimal value of the chosen relaxation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record defines a parameterized zero-gap intersection rather than documenting a recognized sign-structured exactness mechanism. A source must identify the intended relaxation, matrix sign class, and conditions under which that structure yields exactness.

children.title: Low-Rank Structural Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness attributable to restricted quadratic matrix rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Structural Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a rank-bounded exactness class relative to a fixed quadratic relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an integer \(r\geq 0\), let \(I\) be a quadratic program with objective and constraint matrices \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_m\), and let \(R(I)\) be a lower-bounding relaxation. Define
\[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{rank}}(R,r)=\left\{I:\max_{0\leq j\leq m}\operatorname{rank}(Q_j)\leq r,\quad v_R(I)=v(I)\right\}.\]
Thus low rank is a restriction on the original quadratic data, while exactness is the independent requirement of equality between relaxed and original optimal values. If \(R(I)\) is a lifted matrix relaxation, existence of an optimal lifted matrix \(Y=yy^{\mathsf T}\) additionally supplies a recoverable optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This class consists of rank-bounded quadratic instances for which the selected relaxation has no value gap; a rank-one lifted optimum additionally permits solution recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(R(I)\) is a valid lower-bounding relaxation of the minimization problem \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{rank}}(R,r)\iff \max_j\operatorname{rank}(Q_j)\leq r\land v_R(I)=v(I)\).

notation.meaning: Uniform rank bound on quadratic data.
Lifted matrix used by a matrix relaxation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-gap class is formally defined, but it does not state a sourced low-rank exactness mechanism. Moreover, a rank-one lifted matrix yields recovery only when the lift's normalization and projection ensure that its factor represents a feasible original optimizer.

children.title: Sparse-Graph Structural Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness attributable to sparse interaction topology.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Graph Structural Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines exactness for instances whose quadratic interactions lie in a prescribed sparse graph family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a quadratic program \(I
i Q_0,
\ldots,Q_m\), define its aggregate interaction graph \(G(I)=(V,E)\) by \(V=\{1,
\ldots,n\}\) and
\[\{p,q\}\in E\iff p\neq q\ \text{ and }\ (Q_j)_{pq}\neq0\ \text{ for some }\ j.\]
Given a graph family \(\mathcal G\) and a lower-bounding relaxation \(R\), define
\[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{graph}}(R,\mathcal G)=\{I:G(I)\in\mathcal G,\ v_R(I)=v(I)\}.\]
The definition separates graph sparsity from exactness: sparsity alone is not asserted to make the relaxation exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The class contains zero-gap relaxation instances whose aggregate quadratic interaction graph belongs to a specified sparse graph family.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_m\in\mathbb S^n\) represent every quadratic expression in \(I\).
\(R(I)\) is a valid lower bound with finite optimal values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{graph}}(R,\mathcal G)\iff G(I)\in\mathcal G\land v_R(I)=v(I)\).

notation.meaning: Aggregate quadratic interaction graph of the instance.
Real symmetric matrices of order n.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interaction graph is well defined, but the record merely intersects an unspecified graph family with the zero-gap instances. A source is needed to identify the sparse graph class, relaxation, and actual structural exactness result.

children.title: Combined-Structure Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness regimes arising from compatible sign, rank, or sparsity features acting together.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined-Structure Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the intersection of sign, rank, and graph restrictions with zero relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a relaxation \(R\), sign class \(\mathcal K\), rank bound \(r\), and graph family \(\mathcal G\). The combined-structure exactness class is
\[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{comb}}(R,\mathcal K,r,\mathcal G)=\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sign}}(R,\mathcal K)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathrm{rank}}(R,r)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathrm{graph}}(R,\mathcal G).\]
Equivalently, an instance belongs to this class precisely when its quadratic matrices admit the prescribed simultaneous sign switching, each has rank at most \(r\), its aggregate interaction graph belongs to \(\mathcal G\), and \(v_R(I)=v(I)\). No individual structural restriction is thereby claimed sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combined-structure exactness requires the chosen sign, rank, and graph restrictions simultaneously, together with equality of relaxed and original optimal values.
assumptions_latex: \(R\), \(\mathcal K\), \(r\), and \(\mathcal G\) are fixed consistently with the three component classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{comb}}=\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sign}}\cap\mathcal E_{\mathrm{rank}}\cap\mathcal E_{\mathrm{graph}}\).

notation.meaning: Rank threshold for every quadratic data matrix.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intersection is internally consistent but inherits the unspecified relaxation and structural classes of all three prerequisites. It does not establish a combined-structure exactness mechanism without a sourced specialization.

children.title: Quadratic Relaxation Complexity Frontiers
children.top_down_role: Complexity boundaries for constructing, solving, separating, and closing quadratic relaxation gaps.

children.title: Nonconvex QP Hardness Frontier
children.top_down_role: Hardness distinctions among general, box-constrained, simplex-constrained, and structured quadratic programs.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex QP Hardness Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses simplex-constrained indefinite quadratic maximization to locate an NP-hard frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) be a simple graph with adjacency matrix \(A_G\), clique number \(\omega(G)\), and simplex \(\Delta_n=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\). The Motzkin–Straus identity gives
\[\max_{x\in\Delta_n}x^{\mathsf T}A_Gx=1-\frac{1}{\omega(G)}.\]
Consequently, exact global solution of simplex-constrained quadratic programs with an indefinite objective is NP-hard: its optimal value determines \(\omega(G)\). This hardness persists despite bounded variables and one linear equality, whereas positive-semidefinite quadratic minimization over a polyhedron is convex and polynomial-time solvable to prescribed rational accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Indefinite quadratic optimization remains NP-hard even on a simplex, while positive-semidefinite quadratic minimization over polyhedra lies on the convex, tractable side.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite simple graph and \(A_G\) has zero diagonal.
Input data are rational and complexity is measured in the standard bit model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(G)=1-1/\omega(G)\), so exact simplex-constrained indefinite quadratic maximization is NP-hard.

source_refs.locator: Complexity Issues in Global Optimization: A Survey p. 27
5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

source_witnesses.locator: Complexity Issues in Global Optimization: A Survey p. 27
5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

children.title: Quadratic Envelope Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational limits on exact convex-envelope descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Envelope Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates efficient exact convex-envelope access to exact global optimization of nonconvex quadratics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty compact rational polytope and let \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\). Its convex envelope \(g=\operatorname{vex}_P f\) satisfies
\[\min_{x\in P}g(x)=\min_{x\in P}f(x).\]
Therefore, any polynomial-time procedure that constructs an exact polynomial-size tractable representation of \(g\) for every rational pair \((P,f)\), and permits polynomial-time minimization of that representation, would solve every bounded nonconvex quadratic program in polynomial time. Since this class contains NP-hard simplex-constrained instances, no such general procedure exists unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A universally efficient exact convex-envelope representation would solve bounded nonconvex quadratic programs exactly; NP-hardness therefore rules it out unless P equals NP.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is nonempty and compact, and \(P,Q,c\) have rational encodings.
The proposed envelope representation supports polynomial-time exact optimization in the bit model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm P\neq\mathrm{NP}\implies\) no universally polynomial-size, polynomial-time optimizable exact quadratic-envelope representation exists.

notation.meaning: Greatest convex function on P dominated by f.

children.title: RLT Hierarchy Growth
children.top_down_role: Lifted dimension and constraint growth across RLT levels.

knowledge_statements.title: RLT Hierarchy Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts monomial lifts and polynomially multiplied constraints at a fixed RLT level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\) variables, a degree-\(d\) RLT lift indexed by all monomials \(x^\alpha\) with \(|\alpha|\leq d\) contains
\[N(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d}\]
monomial coordinates before identifications or sparsity reductions. If \(m\) original linear inequalities are multiplied by every monomial of degree at most \(d-1\), this construction generates at most
\[m\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}\]
raw product inequalities, in addition to bound-product and consistency constraints. Thus size is polynomial in \(n\) for fixed \(d\), but grows as \(\Theta(n^d)\) in coordinates and is exponential when \(d\) grows proportionally with \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degree-d RLT lift has a binomial number of monomial coordinates and multiplied constraints, polynomial for fixed level but rapidly growing with the level.
assumptions_latex: All monomials of total degree at most \(d\) are retained in the dense lift.
Duplicate, symmetry, and sparsity reductions are not counted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d}=\Theta(n^d)\) for fixed \(d\), with at most \(m\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}\) raw multiplied inequalities.

notation.meaning: Number of monomials of total degree at most d.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stars-and-bars coordinate count is correct, but multiplying arbitrary linear inequalities by every monomial is valid only under sign or nonnegativity conditions, and RLT level conventions vary. A source and a precise construction are required before the constraint count can be accepted.

children.title: Semidefinite Scalability Frontier
children.top_down_role: Matrix-dimension, density, and cone-solution limits of full semidefinite relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Scalability Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies the dense storage and cone dimensions inherent in a full semidefinite lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A full semidefinite relaxation with one matrix variable \(Y\in\mathbb S^k_+\) represents \(k(k+1)/2\) independent scalar entries. Explicit dense storage therefore requires \(\Theta(k^2)\) numbers, and forming a dense eigenvalue or Cholesky factorization requires \(\Theta(k^3)\) arithmetic operations. With \(m\) affine constraints, a primal-dual interior-point method additionally forms and solves dense Newton systems whose dimension can be \(m\). Hence full dense SDP relaxations encounter quadratic memory and cubic-or-higher factorization costs; sparsity, chordal decomposition, or first-order methods change these costs but not the dimension of the undecomposed cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full order-k PSD variable already needs quadratic storage and cubic dense factorization work; dense constraint systems can impose further costs.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is stored without exploiting sparsity or low rank.
Arithmetic counts refer to conventional dense linear algebra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim(\mathbb S^k)=k(k+1)/2\), dense storage is \(\Theta(k^2)\), and dense matrix factorization is \(\Theta(k^3)\).

notation.meaning: Cone of real positive-semidefinite matrices of order k.

children.title: Valid-Inequality Separation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Tractable and hard separation regimes for quadratic polyhedral strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Valid-Inequality Separation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the optimization–separation frontier for rational polyhedral strengthening families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^N\) be a full-dimensional rational polytope with polynomially bounded facet encoding, representing a family of valid inequalities for a lifted quadratic relaxation. A strong separation oracle takes rational \(y\) and either certifies \(y\in P\) or returns rational \((a,
\beta)\) satisfying \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leqeta\) for all \(x\in P\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}y>\beta\). Under the standard well-described-polytope assumptions, polynomial-time strong separation and polynomial-time linear optimization over \(P\) are polynomially equivalent. Consequently, NP-hard linear optimization over \(P\) precludes polynomial-time exact separation unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For well-described rational strengthening polytopes, exact separation and linear optimization are polynomially equivalent; NP-hard optimization therefore implies NP-hard separation.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty, full-dimensional, well-described rational polytope.
Complexity uses rational inputs and the standard oracle bit model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SEP}(P)\equiv_{\mathrm{poly}}\operatorname{OPT}(P)\); hence NP-hard \(\operatorname{OPT}(P)\) implies NP-hard exact \(\operatorname{SEP}(P)\) unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).

notation.meaning: Polytope defined by the strengthening inequality family.
Candidate lifted point to be separated.
Coefficients of a separating valid inequality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited geometric separation section does not establish the oracle-model optimization–separation equivalence. In addition, the displayed validity condition contains the invalid command "\leqeta" and inconsistently uses eta where beta is required. An authoritative oracle-complexity source is needed before mathematical revision.

children.title: Quadratic Relaxation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Recurring geometric and numerical mechanisms producing weak or unusable quadratic bounds.

children.title: Variable-Bound Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Degradation of box-based relaxations when finite bounds are absent or weak.

children.title: Loose Finite Variable Bounds
children.top_down_role: Weakening of box-based relaxations under overly broad finite domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Loose Finite Variable Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-variable lifted example shows quadratic deterioration as finite bounds are loosened.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M>0\), impose \(-M\leq x\leq M\), introduce \(w=x^2\) as the bilinear product \(x\cdot x\), and apply only its four bound-product RLT inequalities. They reduce to
\[w\geq2Mx-M^2,\qquad w\geq-2Mx-M^2,\qquad w\leq M^2.\]
For the problem \(\min\{w:x=0,\ w=x^2\}\), the true value is \(0\), whereas the lifted linear relaxation attains \(-M^2\). Thus the additive relaxation gap is \(M^2\), although the supplied bounds remain finite, and becomes arbitrarily large as those bounds are loosened.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite bounds do not ensure a useful RLT relaxation: in a scalar square example, the gap grows quadratically with bound width.
assumptions_latex: The lift treats the two factors of \(x^2\) using only bound-product linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(M)=0\), \(v_R(M)=-M^2\), and \(v(M)-v_R(M)=M^2\to\infty\) as \(M\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Lifted surrogate for the square of x.

children.title: Missing Finite Variable Bounds
children.top_down_role: Loss of standard box-envelope structure when finite domains are unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Missing Finite Variable Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Without finite factor bounds, standard McCormick or bound-product inequalities are unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{-w:x=0,\ w=x^2,\ x\in\mathbb R\}\). The original problem has the unique feasible lifted value \(w=0\) and optimal value \(0\). If \(w=x^2\) is replaced by a purely linear lifted model but no finite lower or upper bound on \(x\) is available, the standard McCormick bound-product inequalities cannot be formed. The resulting unconstrained surrogate \(w\in\mathbb R\) gives
\[\inf\{-w:x=0,\ w\in\mathbb R\}=-\infty.\]
Thus omitting finite bounds can turn a bounded quadratic problem into an unbounded relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Missing finite bounds can prevent McCormick construction and leave lifted products unrestricted, making a bounded quadratic problem’s relaxation unbounded.
assumptions_latex: No convex square constraint such as \(w\geq x^2\) is added.
The relaxation uses only linear bound-derived product inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v=0\) while \(v_R=-\infty\).

notation.meaning: Unrestricted lifted surrogate for the missing product relation.
Optimal value of the weakened lifted relaxation.
